name: Grote Knip
description:
This was our favorite beach on our recent vacation stay out of about 8 that we snorkled. 
We bought 2 chairs and an umbrella for $15, never looked for facilities or food because we don't eat anything before snorkeling.  I believe up in the parking area there was a food truck, maybe smoothies?
Plentiful parking.  The beach was fairly clean. 
We saw good coral and beautiful fish here. We did, however, have quite a few jellyfish we ran into and when we spoke to someone in town at the dive shop, she said December is jellyfish season. We went back and got footage on our action camera to show proof.  She explained that a lot of times when it's overcast, weird things show up in the water.
Love this beach though!

description: Kids loved it but they didn't get the dent in their pocket that I did. Portions of the lighted walk were cute photo ops, but all in all the price felt like they took more than the experience gave. Even more of a cash grab was the "deluxe" package that went for about $25 more each than the regular ticket.  The kids got a cheap necklace, bag and letter.  Was so not worth the extra $$.It didn't help that the event got cancelled twice on us, due to weather.  That wasn't their fault but the reprocessing of the tickets into vouchers left us with tickets that we were required to pay even more!  The days left to book were all higher in price.   I called and was told to email customer service.  They did eventually fix the vouchers in the end, so that we could get the same experience we originally paid for but the inconvenience left a sour taste.If you have money to burn and are a huge Harry Potter fan, go for it.  If you are on the fence and on a budget, drive through a Christmas light display somewhere.  You'll leave there with a happy feeling.

Featuring a stage just four feet from the floor and the farthest seating area being a mere 120 feet from the stage, The Pearl offers the utmost in intimate viewing of your favorite acts. name: Beacon Street
description: Visit this historic and ritzy Boston neighborhood to soak up its classic New England charm as you stroll down cobblestoned, gas-lamp lined streets. Bring your walking shoes, camera, and select a nice day to wander through the hilly neighborhood and check out its exclusive addresses. Louisburg Square, Mt. Vernon street, Chestnut street and the extremely narrow and widely photographed Acorn street make a nice walking path. Make sure to meander down Charles street to poke into boutiques and antique shops, cafes, and restaurants on this quaint shopping street. Don’t forget to catch a glimpse up close of the State House with its beautiful and iconic dome.

name: Niagara Falls Canada
description: The crashing waters of Niagara Falls—comprising two American falls and one Canadian—are truly a sight to behold. Get up close on a boat ride (be prepared to get soaked!), enjoy amazing aerial views from the Skylon Tower or on a helicopter tour, stroll along the White Water Walk, or hit the Journey Behind the Falls attraction that offers views of the falls from below and behind. Adventure seekers can also go zip-lining, jet-boating, hiking and cycling with the falls as the backdrop. For a truly magical experience, stay after dark when the falls are illuminated. For peak water flow, visit between June and August. – Tripadvisor

If so, Parasailing is the perfect thing for you! Increase the fun factor and fly together with your friends or family all together above the Croatian Adriatic Sea at the famous beach of Makarska! name: Apostle Islands Cruise Service
description: The sea caves are surreal.I had a perfect time on the A.I. Cruise and went on the Grand Tour. You get your value's worth because this tour is 3 hours long. I would advise you to show up at least 45 minutes early. If you don't, you will not get seating on the top deck. You don't want to be inside when you can have a clear view. The tour guide is excellent, he goes over all the facts and history of each island and the area. He does stop and let the return trip be quiet. I prefer this order. With the boat at speed, the topside of the boat was chilly & eventually seats opened up cause of wind chill. The only feedback I have is that Devil's Island is toured slower, or again, because that was the peak of the trip and I didn't feel like it was slow enough.Coming here during peak autumn colors is the best. In October it does get cold in the mornings and evenings.I brought a real camera and my high end camera phone and took as many photos as possible. It was unusual to have peak autumn ending by the 3rd week, but that was just great timing.

name: Virak Buntham Express
description: We used this company to travel around Cambodia in 3 separate bus journeys. Our first one which was from Phnom Penh to Banlung (8 hour drive) , the drive was smooth with enough toilet / food breaks and they provided us with free water. Our second trip wasn’t as good as the driver was going very fast over potholes and speed bumps which meant we couldn’t get comfortable. It was another 8 hour journey (from Banlung to Siem Reap) and I understand that it’s not his fault the road was bumpy, however i do think he could have tried to go slower as since we were sat in the back we kept lifting off our seats from the force of the bumps. Our final bus journey in Cambodia was a 3 hour one from Siem Reap to Battambang and it was okay. My partner was quite squashed with the little leg room and the bus wasn’t overly comfy but as it was a short drive it was okay.

name: Mount Etna
description: This mountain in Catania is known for being the one of the oldest and most active volcanoes in Europe. At the peak, you can enjoy stunning views of the gorgeous Sicilian countryside, especially magical at sunset. Other than that, there are also incredible craters and ice caves to explore. To get to the summit, you'll need to book a tour, which is also a great opportunity to learn more about the fascinating geography and history of the volcano from an experienced guide. Don't forget to wear comfortable shoes and dress in layers, as temperatures can vary depending on the altitude.

name: V&a Waterfront
description: The V&A Waterfront is a 123-hectare mixed-use destination, and one of Africa’s most visited cultural and historical hubs. Set on the edge of a natural, historic working harbour with the iconic Table Mountain as its backdrop, it offers local and international visitors a cosmopolitan mix of experiences ranging from leisure, shopping and exclusive entertainment. It also offers prime residential and commercial property. The prime positioning of the V&A Waterfront boasts sweeping views of the ocean, city bowl and mountain peaks. Up to 100 000 people visit every day during peak season. Contributing R259.1 billion in nominal terms to the South African economy over the last twelve years, the V&A Waterfront’s cumulative contribution to the provincial GGP since 2002 was over R227 billion. The property also reported a 19% increase in retail trade sales for 2014, marking four consecutive years of consistent growth since 2011. By end 2014, total visitor numbers to the property had grown to 24 million a year. Although the V&A Waterfront remains South Africa’s favourite attraction for international visitors, they account for only 23% of all visitors. Visits by locals increased to 63%, while 14% of visitors were from upcountry. With 22 official landmarks on-site, it is also part of South Africa’s historical legacy. Jointly owned by Growthpoint Properties Limited and the Government Employees Pension Fund (GEPF), represented by the Public Investment Corporation Limited (PIC), the V&A Waterfront was developed in 1988 by the state-owned transport corporation, Transnet Limited, while official commercial trading commenced in November 1990.

name: Cabo Girao
description:
Cabo Girao is an elevated viewing area set on the cliffside with a glass skywalk on one of the highest cliffs in Europe. Making for stunning vistas and breathtaking views of the ocean, cliffs, and coastal highways.

At 2€ per person to enter, it is very affordable. Purchase tickets upon arrival. Check the weather before going, a clear day offers the best views.

Arrive as early as possible, parking is free but limited, and the venue tends to become crowded quickly.

It is an easy walk to the observation area.

There is a gift shop and restaurant on site. We even saw a local cat hanging out. We love seeing cats wherever we go! 

We spent maybe 20 minutes here.  It was absolutely worth the stop. It would be a great sunset viewing area. 

But don't fret if you can not make it here. Madeira is full of amazing viewpoints!

name: Rose Parade
description:
Visited Pasadena to participate in decorating flowered floats and attend the famous Rose parade. The process of decorating floats was fascinating. Stripping rose stems, inserting them in vials, placing them on the float itself was certainly team effort. 
The parade itself viewed from either a grand stand or standing on the street is a must see event. The adrenaline infused enthusiastic marching bands raised goose bumps. 
One criticism - this beautiful city did not provide sufficient trash receptacles or portable toilets to accommodate the enormous crowds along the parade route.

name: Dixville Notch State Park
description: Absolutely lovely, albeit small, state park - but definitely one of the BEST places I’ve found to enjoy the fall colors!! I visited in early October and it was phenomenal!! I drove the main road quite a ways and also hiked Table Rock - highly recommend (see my review of the hike for more info)!But even if you aren’t hiking and you just want to drive through, it’s totally worth it for the colors! There are numerous pull outs and stop offs - some even have picnic tables and beautiful, reflective lake views! One of the lakes had a sizable resort on it that made for some gorgeous photos!There are a couple of waterfalls in the park but I didn’t visit them this trip so I can’t speak to them but I’m sure they’re lovely! The view from Table Rock was incredible!Fun fact about the surrounding town of Dixville: apparently it’s the first town to cast votes in the presidential election haha!! There are historical signs throughout the park that tell you history and fun facts- worth reading!I didn’t find any fee stations or staffed entrance booths - and their website doesn’t list this park as a “day use fee area” so I think it’s pretty much free to enter. The roads are very well maintained and in excellent condition. They were doing road work while I drove through but it was a non issue. There was very little traffic as well. I didn’t see any bathrooms anywhere so come prepared!Overall it’s totally worth a visit even though it’s a small park - especially for the fall colors! And the hiking - highly recommend!!

description: After looking on a Norway tourism website I followed their link to book a train from Flam to Oslo. Turns out their charge is over double the actual price you would pay going through the correct EnTur site plus added a $194AUD non-refundable service fee. Despite booking a fully flexible fare, when I tried to cancel the Rail Ninja booking it was going to cost the $194AUD plus another 50% modification fee. This meant it would cost more to cancel than the actual fare being charged by EnTur.They are an utterly unscrupulous internet scam. Despite paying the so called service fee, it is impossible to get any service what so ever. I have had no replies to 3 contact us form submissions and I now understand they are a scam organisation who must simply pay for the google add to run on the first page of google search.Don't touch them, THEY ARE A COMPLETE SCAM. I'm even beginning to wonder if we actually have any tickets. Guess I'll find out in 2 days.

description: Welcome to Rainbow Mountain Cusco Journey through an undiscovered land of wild desert landscapes, snow capped peaks, herds of alpaca, and arrive at the ultimate destination - The “Rainbow Mountain” hidden deep in the Andes. Throughout your journey you will pass through a vibrant green valley with the impressive Ausangate mountain towering in the distance. You will experience first hand how locals live in the mountains and even have a chance to speak with them. As you get closer to the Rainbow Mountain you will begin to see the first signs of the colored minerals that formed the painted hills. Your guide will explain what makes up the existence of the “Rainbow Mountain”, and finally with one last push you will hike up to a vantage point that gives you a 360 degree view of the beautiful landscape that makes up this sacred land.

name: Sierra Railroad Dinner Train
description: Considered one of the five best dinner trains in the West, the historic Sierra operates year-round from the town of Oakdale, CA (near Modesto & Stockton). Beer Trains and murder mystery shows are the most well-known trips, but we also offer the High Noon Express, detailing the history of this movie railroad, and the Old Vine Express with wine tasting! name: Seogwipo Submarine
description: I wanted to see the Seogwipo tourist spot from the Sanbangsan sightseeing boat on Jeju Island, so I went there without making a reservation.Fortunately, the driver (Kim Tae-in), who always takes me to the tourist spots (places I want to go), made a reservation by phone, so I was able to board the boat.You can go around by car, but the view from the sea is the best.Boarding time: 1 hour, 11:00, 14:00, 15:00Please be at the dock 20 minutes before boarding. The fare is 19,000 W, but there is a discount for those over 65, so it was 17,000 W. It seems that there are free or discounts for those over 65 for paid facilities. Please be sure to bring your passport.The music (trot) and announcements on the boat are loud. They sell grilled squid, so if you can't stand the smell, please go out on the deck and sit on the bench. There are times when it rocks quite a bit, so please listen to the staff and board safely.It's a small tourist boat, but we encountered two dolphins, which are hard to see. (I was told it would bring me luck)I'll be going again in the fall with a friend.

Experience the longest ziplines in Texas with a 3 hour tour with 5 ziplines! Enjoy all day access to our private lake front property with grills, beach games, loungers and hammocks. name: Palledin Balloon Excursions (2025) - All You Need to Know BEFORE You Go (with Reviews)
description: We joined Bill for a wonderful balloon trip over St. George UT on Christmas weekend 2022.  While chilly and cloudy, it was a beautiful day and we had a great trip.  We assisted Bill and his ground crew with getting the balloon inflated and then enjoyed a peaceful hour floating over the houses, pools, trampolines and fields of Southern UT.  The views of the red cliffs and the Pine Valley mountains were spectacular.  Bill regaled us with stories of the decades he has been ballooning in St George.  He described the changes he has seen, and bemoaned a rapidly approaching lack of places to land - as the area continues to be filled with houses.  He also was informative about the local geography.The only thing I would have changed is that often Bill is able to float inches above the Virgin River during his flights.  Unfortunately, during our flight the winds were quite variable and that did not occur.Bill mentioned he is looking to get out of commercial ballooning Spring 2023.  This will be a loss to those looking for a fun and unique way to experience the area.

description: Hawn State Park is one of the loveliest parks in a system full of lovely parks. Clear, sand-bottomed streams, wild areas ripe with orchids and awe-inspiring views combine to make Hawn a place that Missourians treasure. Geology buffs love Pickle Creek for the number of exposed rock types. Hikers frequent the Whispering Pine Wild Area for its quiet trails with expansive views. Bird watchers flock to the park for its variety of birds. And there are plenty of quiet spaces for people to get away and enjoy the outdoors.

description: Established in 1969, The Moorings is the world's premier yacht charter company. With over 500 yachts in destinations from the warm white shores of the Caribbean to the timeless Mediterranean and beyond, we’re here to make your time at sea simply unforgettable. We offer a collection of getaways including hands-on sailing and power yacht charters, all-inclusive crewed yacht vacations and more.

name: Walkabout Florence Tours
description: This was a very fun day trip and an excellent tour guide. Pisae, Tuscany, a winery, gelato and everything in between! I thoroughly enjoyed this trip and will recommend it to my friends and family.

description: Jump into a world of creativity, color and playful learning at LEGOLAND Discovery Center Philadelphia, the ultimate indoor LEGO® playground! Families with children ages 3-10 will enjoy an interactive LEGO-themed ride and a 4D cinema where your favorite LEGO characters come to life. Explore MINILAND Philadelphia, featuring local landmarks made from over a million bricks and get hands-on in LEGO-themed build and play areas where kid’s imaginations can explore endless possibilities.

name: Beach Sulic
description: The beach is rocky rather than sand and it would be advisable to have something soft to sit or lie on. It was however very sheltered and peaceful providing easy access to the warm sea. There wasn't much in the way of facilities but was perfect for relaxing and was easily accessible.

name: Angel's Envy Distillery
description: Located in the heart of Louisville, Angel's Envy Distillery is downtown’s first fully operational bourbon production facility. Built on a tremendous legacy and a pioneering spirit, Angel’s Envy innovated the foundations of whiskey through a unique “secondary finishing” technique. By maturing our whiskeys in charred oak barrels, then transferring them to secondary finishing casks, we crafted a distinct blend of refined complexity with an inviting flavor profile. We invite you to visit our distillery whether you are a seasoned bourbon aficionado or a curious newcomer. Join us 7 days a week for distillery tours, whiskey tastings, cocktail classes, and shopping.

name: Dublin Free Walking Tour (2025) - All You Need to Know BEFORE You Go (with Reviews)
description: We love Dublin! Join us at at the Spire (the big needle!) at 10am, 11am or 2pm (Southside Tour) and 3pm (Northside Tour) every day for the Free Walking Tour. On this 3 hour walking tour we will give you the best possible introduction to our beautiful, fascinating old city. Look for the Yellow Umbrella! We look forward to sharing Dublin with you!

name: LX Factory
description: Once an old industrial textile complex, LX Factory is now home to Lisbon’s trendiest restaurants, bars, and shops. Located beneath the Ponte de 25 Abril Bridge, the revitalized hotspot resembles a village where you can walk down cobbled streets and admire the street art adorning the walls of old warehouses. Here, you can dine in a former industrial canteen, shop at a multi-story bookstore, watch artists at work in their ateliers and studios, catch a live performance or exhibition, and more. On the weekend, stop by the open-air flea market which sells everything from handmade jewelry to vintage clothing. – Tripadvisor

name: Dolphin Quest
description: Dolphin Quest Bermuda, located at the historic National Museum of Bermuda, brings people and dolphins closer than ever in fun, interactive dolphin encounter programs for all ages. This unique experience is on-of-a-kind in Bermuda. A Dolphin Quest encounter program is great for everyone from kids to honeymooners! Reservations can be made up to one year in advance. A portion of the proceeds from all Dolphin Quest encounter programs supports vital marine education, conservation and scientific study. TripAdvisor Certificate Excellence winner since 2015! Thank you to all our guests who visited us in 2021 and took the time to submit their feedback by providing a Trip Advisor review. Your contributions have resulted in Dolphin Quest receiving the 2021 Traveler's Choice Award. We appreciate your support.

We will open again in early May 2025.

The Bar Harbor Whale Watch Company offers a variety of boat cruises for all ages that show different sights and wildlife in the area around Mount Desert Island, Maine. The cruises that we offer include whale watching, puffin and lighthouse cruise, nature cruise, lobster fishing and seal watching.

We also have a gift shop in our ticket office, where you can purchase souvenirs during your time in town. We hope to see you on one (or more!) of our boat cruises so we can show you why Bar Harbor, Maine is such a special place!

name: Woodfield Mall
description: Just 40 minutes west of Chicago, Woodfield Mall is one of the largest shopping destinations in the United States. With more than 2 million square feet of retail shops, restaurants, and family-friendly amenities, Woodfield Mall has a unique mix that creates a completely new and refreshing experiences with every visit. As an iconic destination, Woodfield Mall features nearly 300 stores, specialty shops and restaurants, including Nordstrom, Macy's, and JCPenney while complemented with best of brand retailers Apple, Michael Kors, lululemon, Anthropologie, BOSS, A/X Armani Exchange, MAC Cosmetics, H&M and Zara. Don’t miss Woodfield Mall’s expansive list of dining options ranging from 8 full service restaurants such as Texas de Brazil, P.F. Changs, Uncle Julio's, and The Cheesecake Factory to over 30 fast casual selections throughout the mall. Woodfield Mall recently added a new world-class Dining Pavilion, offering flavor-packed fare for every appetite with 11 eateries featuring an array of dining choices and health-conscious eateries from favorites such as Blaze Pizza and Chipotle Grill and locals such as Stan’s Donuts & Coffee. Woodfield Mall offers a unique mix of entertainment options for all ages. Enterrium, YuKids Island or Peppa Pig World of Play are all one-of-its-kind venues at Woodfield Mall, or you can catch a comedy show at The Improv Comedy Club. Shoppers can also enjoy great guest amenities such as Signature Meet & Greet Service, free WiFi, Valet Parking, Children’s Play Area and Trolley Transportation.

name: Ortega Falls
description: After completing the Walker Canyon Trail hike, headed west twelve miles to Highway 74 and the Ortega Falls Trail for additional hiking. This challenging 0.20 mile moderately rated out and back trail with a 39-foot elevation is easily completed in 10 minutes or less. This trail is open year-round and no longer requires a permit or pass. To reach this trail, take Ortega Highway 74 to a turnout on the north side of the road, approximately 1.5 miles from the Ortega Oaks Candy Store (currently closed). There is no signage advising the trail or waterfall. Just look for a lot of vehicles parked in a small parking lot. This trail is not for novice hikers or small children, as there is no clearly defined trail, and its is easy to get confused and lost. The trail is sandy with rocks and a lot of steep climbing. Be sure to wear good footwear. Flip flops are a no-no. The views along the short trail are amazing. Unfortunately, due to the California drought, this 35-foot waterfall was dry. The pool at the base of the waterfall did have a few inches of water in it as well as a lot of trash. Be advised that the trail is littered with broken beer bottles, cans, and trash. Graffiti litters the rocks and detracts from the beauty of this hiking trail. Strongly recommend avoiding this hiking trail at this due to poor conditions. Would have enjoyed seeing the waterfall in full flow. If you do venture to this hiking trail, be sure take sufficient water with you as well as hat to protect you from the beating sun.

description: Athos Sea Cruises - Mount Athos cruise Ship departs once up to twice a day from Ouranoupolis port, right next to the "gates" of Holy Mount Athos. The ship heads to the southwestern part of Mount Athos peninsula. In 15 minutes reach the first Russian cloister and after sailing by unique beaches, it arrives in the area of the first monastery, Iera Moni Dochiariou and follows other 7 monasteries, as well as the Holy Mount's central port, Daphni, and finally the cloisters, small villages, where groups of monks live in every house. During the cruise visitors have the chance to admire the untouched nature and the unique architecture of Mount Athos monasteries. There is an audio guide tour in different languages (Greek, English, Russian, Serbian, Polish, Bulgarian and German). In these beautiful calm turquoise waters you will see very often dolphins to follow the ship. There is a restaurant, a bar and a small exhibition of souvenirs in the ship. Nice beach with good facilities. Arrive early to get parking and you pay via app or website. There is wifi at the payment stand if you have poor cell service. Parking is $5 an hour, but you get notifications when you're time is close to ending and you can add more time from your phone.

There are lots of good and large shells to be had, but you have to look in the right places for them. We made the same mistake as most people and were looking for them on the waters edge. We learned from others that the best pickings are further away from the water, between the sea grass and the mound on which the side-by-sides drive on. If you walk down the beach passed everybody you'll have more shells than you know what to do with. 

Big shells are all over. The interesting and more unique shells are usually found while digging through the big patches of shells, far away from the water. When in doubt ask the people with big bags of shells where to look.

name: Abbazia di San Fruttuoso
description:
We visited the Abbey of San Fruttuoso during the long weekend of April 25th and we loved it. There are fast and punctual ferries that leave from Camogli every hour and at a more than affordable cost.
The visit inside the Abbey is certainly worth it even if it is now devoid of furnishings. A 15-minute video, which can be watched while sitting, explains its interesting history.
The view from the numerous paths full of splendid plants is priceless.
Certainly the plus is being able to go in low season periods when the small beach in front of the Abbey is free of hordes of tourists camped out.
Super recommended.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

name: King Spa & Sauna
description:
Reading all the negative reviews inspired me to write this. I go here once a year and it's always an incredible experience, but you have to know what you're walking into. 

It's a traditional Korean bathhouse. Aside from the normal hot tubs, steam room, and warm pools, picture 10 massage tables lined up in a row with naked women on top and old ladies in underwear scrubbing layers of dead skin off your body for 40 min. Awkward at first, but it's amazing. So smooth after!  The co-ed part is a bunch of different sauna rooms with various temperatures and health benefits (ie charcoal). There is a cafeteria with traditional Korean food. There is a movie theatre, rest area, nap area..it's literally open for 24 hours. It's a place to go to lounge and daudle. It would actually be perfect for someone with a long layover, but you'd want at least 4 hours here. You also get a uniform, aka super baggy t shirt and shorts. It looks ridiculous at first but everyone has it on so it becomes the norm. Someone said this place feels like an amusement park and it resonates. The staff can come off rude but they're not, they're just being Korean. If you come here, try to lean into all the weirdness and soak in the experience!

description: We'd heard and read so much about Diana's Baths that it was a "must do" for this vacation.  We'd read that parking could be a problem so we got there about 8:45 on a Monday morning.  Parking was no problem at that hour.  We met just a few hikers on the path to the falls;  so it was a delightful hike [about .08 mile] with a wide path with few roots and quite level the whole way.  It was a beautiful quiet walk with wonderful scenery, rocks and boulders.  Not long after getting to the beginning of the falls, more visitors started appearing and it was getting crowded.  If you can climb large boulders, you can do get a picture-perfect views with gorgeous settings all around.  This is a great hike and would suggest either early morning or later in the afternoon. There are lots of good and large shells to be had, but you have to look in the right places for them. We made the same mistake as most people and were looking for them on the waters edge. We learned from others that the best pickings are further away from the water, between the sea grass and the mound on which the side-by-sides drive on. If you walk down the beach passed everybody you'll have more shells than you know what to do with. 

Big shells are all over. The interesting and more unique shells are usually found while digging through the big patches of shells, far away from the water. When in doubt ask the people with big bags of shells where to look.

The visit inside the Abbey is certainly worth it even if it is now devoid of furnishings. A 15-minute video, which can be watched while sitting, explains its interesting history.
The view from the numerous paths full of splendid plants is priceless.
Certainly the plus is being able to go in low season periods when the small beach in front of the Abbey is free of hordes of tourists camped out.
Super recommended.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

name: King Spa & Sauna
description:
Reading all the negative reviews inspired me to write this. I go here once a year and it's always an incredible experience, but you have to know what you're walking into. 

It's a traditional Korean bathhouse. Aside from the normal hot tubs, steam room, and warm pools, picture 10 massage tables lined up in a row with naked women on top and old ladies in underwear scrubbing layers of dead skin off your body for 40 min. Awkward at first, but it's amazing. So smooth after!  The co-ed part is a bunch of different sauna rooms with various temperatures and health benefits (ie charcoal). There is a cafeteria with traditional Korean food. There is a movie theatre, rest area, nap area..it's literally open for 24 hours. It's a place to go to lounge and daudle. It would actually be perfect for someone with a long layover, but you'd want at least 4 hours here. You also get a uniform, aka super baggy t shirt and shorts. It looks ridiculous at first but everyone has it on so it becomes the norm. Someone said this place feels like an amusement park and it resonates. The staff can come off rude but they're not, they're just being Korean. If you come here, try to lean into all the weirdness and soak in the experience!

description:
Nice beach with good facilities. Arrive early to get parking and you pay via app or website. There is wifi at the payment stand if you have poor cell service. Parking is $5 an hour, but you get notifications when you're time is close to ending and you can add more time from your phone.

There are lots of good and large shells to be had, but you have to look in the right places for them. We made the same mistake as most people and were looking for them on the waters edge. We learned from others that the best pickings are further away from the water, between the sea grass and the mound on which the side-by-sides drive on. If you walk down the beach passed everybody you'll have more shells than you know what to do with. 

Big shells are all over. The interesting and more unique shells are usually found while digging through the big patches of shells, far away from the water. When in doubt ask the people with big bags of shells where to look.

A classic revue in the club is made up of original sketches and songs accompanied by their world-famous improv, which typically relies on audience participation. description:
We visited the Abbey of San Fruttuoso during the long weekend of April 25th and we loved it. There are fast and punctual ferries that leave from Camogli every hour and at a more than affordable cost.
The visit inside the Abbey is certainly worth it even if it is now devoid of furnishings. A 15-minute video, which can be watched while sitting, explains its interesting history.
The view from the numerous paths full of splendid plants is priceless.
Certainly the plus is being able to go in low season periods when the small beach in front of the Abbey is free of hordes of tourists camped out.
Super recommended.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

name: King Spa & Sauna
description:
Reading all the negative reviews inspired me to write this. I go here once a year and it's always an incredible experience, but you have to know what you're walking into. 

It's a traditional Korean bathhouse. Aside from the normal hot tubs, steam room, and warm pools, picture 10 massage tables lined up in a row with naked women on top and old ladies in underwear scrubbing layers of dead skin off your body for 40 min. Awkward at first, but it's amazing. So smooth after!  The co-ed part is a bunch of different sauna rooms with various temperatures and health benefits (ie charcoal). There is a cafeteria with traditional Korean food. There is a movie theatre, rest area, nap area..it's literally open for 24 hours. It's a place to go to lounge and daudle. It would actually be perfect for someone with a long layover, but you'd want at least 4 hours here. You also get a uniform, aka super baggy t shirt and shorts. It looks ridiculous at first but everyone has it on so it becomes the norm. Someone said this place feels like an amusement park and it resonates. The staff can come off rude but they're not, they're just being Korean. If you come here, try to lean into all the weirdness and soak in the experience!

description: Belváros-Lipótváros, located centrally in Budapest, is defined by its striking architecture and deep historical roots. Its streets are lined with charming cafes and boutiques, while the Danube River provides a stunning backdrop. The neighborhood is home to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building and St. Stephen’s Basilica, both must-sees for any history or architecture enthusiast. The Central Market Hall offers a gastronomic extravaganza, with traditional Hungarian dishes and fresh produce. Easy access through trams and buses makes exploring this historical and cultural hub a delight for any traveler.

name: Bowman's Beach
description:
Nice beach with good facilities. Arrive early to get parking and you pay via app or website. There is wifi at the payment stand if you have poor cell service. Parking is $5 an hour, but you get notifications when you're time is close to ending and you can add more time from your phone.

There are lots of good and large shells to be had, but you have to look in the right places for them. We made the same mistake as most people and were looking for them on the waters edge. We learned from others that the best pickings are further away from the water, between the sea grass and the mound on which the side-by-sides drive on. If you walk down the beach passed everybody you'll have more shells than you know what to do with. 

Big shells are all over. The interesting and more unique shells are usually found while digging through the big patches of shells, far away from the water. When in doubt ask the people with big bags of shells where to look.

name: Second City
description: Enjoy the best in Chicago-style sketch and improv comedy in one of the city’s most popular comedy theaters. The Second City is six-decade-old and is where the likes of Tina Fey and Steve Carrell shot to stardom. A classic revue in the club is made up of original sketches and songs accompanied by their world-famous improv, which typically relies on audience participation. If that’s not your piece of cake, make sure you get seats at the back of the room. You might want to arrive early to grab dinner and walk around Chicago’s historic Old Town before the show. – Tripadvisor

name: Rainbow Street
description: A wonderful street in Amman, Jordan. Many shops, restaurants, cafes and places of interest like Jara Market and others. This street will be very viral with pedestrians after sunset. Had a short visit in the morning and dine in in one of the restaurants there.

name: Abbazia di San Fruttuoso
description:
We visited the Abbey of San Fruttuoso during the long weekend of April 25th and we loved it. There are fast and punctual ferries that leave from Camogli every hour and at a more than affordable cost.
The visit inside the Abbey is certainly worth it even if it is now devoid of furnishings. A 15-minute video, which can be watched while sitting, explains its interesting history.
The view from the numerous paths full of splendid plants is priceless.
Certainly the plus is being able to go in low season periods when the small beach in front of the Abbey is free of hordes of tourists camped out.
Super recommended.

name: Elevated Acre
description: A captivating blend of old and new, Downtown Manhattan offers a unique view into the past, present, and future of New York City. Iconic landmarks like the historic Wall Street, the poignant 9/11 Memorial, and the awe-inspiring One World Trade Center punctuate the skyline, while the lush greenery of Battery Park provides a tranquil respite from the urban landscape. For foodies, the neighborhood is a culinary wonderland, featuring everything from Michelin-starred restaurants to diverse food markets such as the famed Eataly. Art lovers will find themselves drawn to the stunning exhibitions at the Whitney Museum of American Art or captivated by the street performances in Washington Square Park. With several subway lines crisscrossing the area, exploring the rest of the city is just a train ride away.

name: Dolmabahce Palace
description: This palace was built in the mid 1800s to replace an earlier structure that was made of wood. The new palace incorporated sixteen separate buildings with stables, a flour mill and a clock tower among them.

name: Bluefield Tea Gardens
description: Bluefield Tea is proud to open its doors to visitors, showcasing our commitment to transparency and quality. Our open factory policy reflects our belief that we have nothing to hide and everything to share about our tea-making process. Visitors are invited to witness firsthand the care and dedication that goes into every cup of Bluefield Tea. In recognition of our efforts towards sustainability, we are honored to have received the prestigious Gold Award for Global Sustainability. This accolade highlights our ongoing commitment to ethical practices and environmental stewardship. At Bluefield Tea, we strive to not only produce exceptional teas but also to do so in a way that benefits the planet and future generations. Whether you're a tea aficionado or simply curious about the world of tea, we welcome you to experience the magic of Bluefield Tea firsthand. Come visit us and discover why we're not just a tea factory—we're a symbol of excellence, transparency, and sustainability in the

name: Linh Phuoc Pagoda
description: The temple grounds have a dragon of length 49 m, the dragon enclosure is made of 12,000 beer bottles, and the dragon mouth covers the Buddha. In front of the temple grounds is a 37 m high seven-storeyed tower, which is considered the highest temple bell tower in Vietnam. In the heart of the tower is a 4.3 m high bell that is considered the heaviest bell in Vietnam; it is 2.33 m wide, weighs 8,500 kg, and was cast in 1999.

name: Dalat Flower Park
description: Da Lat Flower Garden is a beautiful and peaceful attraction, perfect for nature lovers and photography enthusiasts. Located near Xuan Huong Lake, the garden showcases a wide variety of vibrant flowers, including roses, hydrangeas, and orchids, all blooming in colorful displays. The well-maintained pathways make it easy to explore, and the atmosphere is serene and relaxing. Visitors can enjoy walking through themed sections and admiring the artistic arrangements. It's a wonderful place to escape the busy city and connect with nature. Da Lat Flower Garden is a must-see destination for anyone visiting the city

name: Valley of Love
description: Just as true love has to surpass several obstacles, the Valley of Love in Dalat had to surpass many challenges in the past in order to gain its rightful name today. In the beginning, the valley was called Vallée D’amour (Valley of Love) by the French before being renamed The Valley of Piece. In 1935, its beauty and captivation persuaded people to once again name it after the most wonderful thing in the world: Love. Thanks to being the honeymoon destination of newly-married couples, this valley is even regarded as Niagara Fall of Vietnam. The Valley of Love today is located 4 miles away from the center of Dalat, the little Paris, on Phu Dong Thien Vuong St.

name: Crazy House
description:
A new experience to be able to visit one of the inns designed by one of the architects from Vietnam. And a house concept that is indeed made out of the box, because when entering the house, we might get lost, because every corner is confusing. And there are some areas where the stairs are getting smaller and the stairs are in a fairly high position. So you could say you have to be careful too.

In addition to being a tourist destination, we can also try staying here. Because it is indeed designed as an inn too.

To enter here there is an entrance ticket fee.
If you are visiting Da Lat, make sure to include it in your travel plans.

name: Trúc Lâm Monastery of Da Lat

name: Xuan Huong Lake
description: Xuan Huong Lake is one of the most scenic spots in Dalat, offering a peaceful atmosphere and stunning views. Walking or cycling around the lake is a great way to enjoy the cool weather and take in the beauty of the surrounding landscape. However, during peak tourist seasons, it can get quite crowded, and some areas around the lake could be better maintained. The food stalls nearby offer tasty local snacks, but prices can be a bit high. Despite these minor drawbacks, Xuan Huong Lake remains a must-visit spot for anyone looking to relax and enjoy nature in Dalat

name: Da Lat Cable Car - Robin Hill

name: Playa Hermosa
description: We had a beautiful and memorable morning taking a small private boat tour of Playa  Hermosa and Playa Papagallo on the comfortable “Tropical Tide”, captained by Mario Cortez. He and his crew of two took us around the point of land just north of Playa Hermosa, to a long secluded beach where the four of us friends/guests waded easily in shallow water to the shore. We walked to a gracious and grand ceiba tree, observed many small hermit crabs in the sand, and swam in the refreshing water of the ocean. Mario is knowledgeable and shared with us many things about the area. Upon leaving we headed to Playa Papagallo where we were offered delicious fresh pineapple and watermelon accompanied by cold water or cervezas. We followed large flocks of frigate birds to areas in the water where numerous large Jackfish were feeding on sardines. The crew ultimately caught four nice sized Jacks and filleted them as we headed back, accompanied be a number of dolphins. As we disembarked from the boat Mario presented us with a beautiful Jack filet that the resort chef agreed to grill for our dinner tonight! I heartily recommend this experience to those traveling to this part of Costa Rica!

description: The trip is a two hour ride up and then down the river, in a boat that is fairly open to the elements, so could be chilly in the off season. The staff are friendly and allow a few at a time to visit the upper deck at the stern where the captain is to get a better view. We were given a cup of warm cider and donuts which was a nice surprise, I don't know if this is done on all trips. The only downside was the commentary. From the moment the boat departs, passengers were drip fed with some poor quality, country style music from speakers throughout the vessel. It was difficult to talk to fellow passengers without raising your voice, and to be honest, to enjoy the tranquility of the river, away from traffic and other noise, the trip would have been better without this.A crew member sat on a high seat by the entrance gangway playing with her mobile phone. Occasionally, she would mute the music to give a short one line sentence on which house she liked best on the riverbank, all done without enthusiasm or interest, and as soon as she finished speaking, she turned up the awful music again. We learned nothing about the river or its history, or the part it plays in society today.It was a nice enough trip on a sunny afternoon, but could have been so much better with a properly trained commentator and less of the piped music.

description: We had a beautiful and memorable morning taking a small private boat tour of Playa  Hermosa and Playa Papagallo on the comfortable “Tropical Tide”, captained by Mario Cortez. He and his crew of two took us around the point of land just north of Playa Hermosa, to a long secluded beach where the four of us friends/guests waded easily in shallow water to the shore. We walked to a gracious and grand ceiba tree, observed many small hermit crabs in the sand, and swam in the refreshing water of the ocean. Mario is knowledgeable and shared with us many things about the area. Upon leaving we headed to Playa Papagallo where we were offered delicious fresh pineapple and watermelon accompanied by cold water or cervezas. We followed large flocks of frigate birds to areas in the water where numerous large Jackfish were feeding on sardines. The crew ultimately caught four nice sized Jacks and filleted them as we headed back, accompanied be a number of dolphins. As we disembarked from the boat Mario presented us with a beautiful Jack filet that the resort chef agreed to grill for our dinner tonight! I heartily recommend this experience to those traveling to this part of Costa Rica!

description: Excellent trip with a guide , with explanations about Nanny and the maroons.The fall is very High, access with easy stars at the end.

name: St. Mary's Monastery
description:
The road isn’t good. 2 cars are challenging.
If you go in the summer, you’ll get a lot of sweat. They receive a set number of people to the abbey and you cannot sign in until they leave. There’s not much to see inside. 1 time just to have seen, you can go beyond that unnecessary.

name: Horn Pond
description: The views are amazing and refreshing, both sunrise and sunset .I will always come where every time, irrespective of the time of the season

name: Bean Point
description: We took a day trip and this island didn’t disappoint! The beaches are clean and restrooms nearby. Lots of great restaurants, cafes and desserts. I would recommend starting your day early to avoid long lines entering the island and finding a parking space.

name: FlixBus
description: FlixMobility is a global mobility provider, offering new alternatives for convenient, affordable and environmentally-friendly travel via the FlixBus and FlixTrain brands.

name: Serra da Estrela
description: The Serra da Estrela is a true natural treasure of Portugal, where the grandiosity of the mountains meets the serenity of the landscapes. With its imposing peaks, green valleys and crystal clear lakes, it is a destination that delights in any season of the year. In winter, it turns into a snow-covered paradise, while in summer it reveals stunning trails and unforgettable panoramic views.

name: House From A Christmas Story
description: The House from a Christmas Story, now restored to its movie splendor, is open year round to the public for tours. Directly across the street from the house is the Museum, which features original props, costumes and memorabilia from the film, as well as hundreds of rare behind-the-scenes photos. Among the props and costumes are the toys from the Higbee's window, Randy's snowsuit, the chalkboard from Miss Shields' classroom and the family car. After reliving A Christmas Story at Ralphie's house don't forget to visit the museum gift shop for your own Major Award Leg Lamp and other great movie memorabilia. Admission for all guests is $20 plus digital ticketing and admission tax. Ages 5 and up.

name: Stavropoleos Monastery
description: Built in 1724, this beautiful church is one of Bucharest's oldest.

name: Tallink Silja Line
description:
This is a great way to get from Helsinki to Stockholm without flying. It sails between the two cities leaving Helsinki at 5pm local and arrives at Stockholm at 10am local time. 

The terminal where the ship departs from Helsinki has a tram stop in front of it which is useful if you need to get there and do not have any transfers or do not want to walk.

The check in process was simple and easy, I scanned a QR code and collected my boarding pass (which doubled as my room key) as well as two tickets, one for a restaurant and one for a bus transfer at Stockholm. 

I paid for an A suite with a sea view, however the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the suite itself is quite dated. I tried to move one of the beds to make a double bed but the wall and the floor under the bed were dirty so I decided against that. This was disappointing as the suite was one of the more expensive options.

The ship itself departed and arrived on time and the facilities on board were great otherwise. Another reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that wifi is only available in the COMMON AREAS of the ship and not in the suites (unless you pay for the very expensive suites).

name: Reef Explorer Semi Sub by Cozumel Tours
description: Outstanding one hour tour on the Neptune. We were on a Celebrity Cruise and it was a shore excursion.  Relaxing, comfortable and not in the least claustrophobic.  We saw the barrier Reef and all the fish and Coral you could imagine.Highly recommend!

name: Hawaiian Railway
description:
・We rented a car from Waikiki, and the parking lot was free (15 cars can be parked)
・We left Waikiki at 9:00 and arrived before 10:00
・It was a Sunday, so there were two tours, one at 13:00 and one at 15:00. We took the 13:00 tour, which was about a 2-hour tour
・Tickets were $13/person (there is a senior discount for people over 60 years old, and they confirmed this when we purchased the ticket)
・Recommendation when purchasing tickets: cold bottled water, about $1 I think
・After purchasing the ticket, we drove to the nearby Ka Makana Alii shopping mall until the time. It has the Cheesecake Factory and Bodyworks, and is a very enjoyable mall
・We got back on the bus before 13:00.

Let's go! The locals are cute, and the lady is also a tour guide in English...
・The seats are switched on the way there and back, so you can enjoy both the ocean side and the mountain side.
・When crossing the road without a railroad crossing on the way there, it's like a small event! We crossed the road while honking our horns. We waved to drivers of parked cars and motorbike riders!

The ride along the coast is surprisingly short, about 10 minutes, but from the industrial area to Ko Olina, you can enjoy a very laid-back atmosphere. (When driving through residential areas, you might be greeted by cheerful seniors from the lanais of their homes...)

Some people got off at Aulani Disney on the way.

name: Free Tour Verona
description: This tour is the perfect way to enjoy the most important sights of Verona. If you have few hours or many days, nevermind! It's the best activity to do in the city. Our amazing tour guides will be ready to satisfy those who wish to get the most and best out of the city. The meeting point is in Via Leoncino 61, nearby the Arena, at the Info Tourist Office.

name: Panhandle Helicopter
description: Since 2008, Panhandle Helicopter has offered scenic helicopter tours over the "world's most beautiful beaches" in Panama City Beach, FL. We are proud to provide a bird's eye view of our beautiful emerald coast and local marine life. Safety is our #1 priority, but our goal is to provide you with an experience of a lifetime. We look forward to flying with you!

name: Taiko Center Kyoto Studio
description: Offering WADAIKO workshop which is part of Japanese culture and is one of the traditional performing arts in Kyoto studio. Your class is private lesson with an instructor, and everything you need is provided in the session. This is the perfect activity for a trip to Japan with family, friends, or by yourself, where everyone can easily experience Japanese drumming. You will enjoy a unique experience where you can experience culture and tradition while learning how to play Japanese drums, which are used in Japanese festivals. Let's make unforgettable memories together in the historic land of Kyoto.

name: Dive in la Paz
description: Come with us in the best place in the world: The Sea of Cortes, named by the famous Jacques Yves Cousteau "The aquarium of the world! Our priority is a family and friendly ambiance, professional services and taking care of this beautiful ecosystem! We offer Diving day and night trip, dive courses, whale watching, snorkel with whale shark and sea lions, Balandra beach trip...

name: Fuji Safari Park
description: Initially this safari park was Fairly good and full of wildlife. After our drive around, me and my wife decided to walk outside the park , on our walk I spotted one of the park staff smashing a bamboo pole against a giraffe trying to get the giraffe off the road . Obviously unaware we were watching this . For me , personally, it was disturbing and spoilt the experience.  I think if this kind of behavior is normal in the park. It's really not a place most people, me included would want to visit . Animals should be treated with the care and respect they deserve. Especially, if they are confined to a park or zoo . I have wanted to write this review for a while , but I just saw something that sparked me into leaving a review.

name: Hakone Sightseeing Cruise
description: Replicas of pirate ships cruise Lake Ashi, offering views of forests, hotels and the striking red gateway to the Hakone Shrine.

name: Pacific Adventures
description: We are committed to deliver the highest quality standards of service, offering experiences in which every detail has been taken care of for our guests to be able to live in a unique way the soul of our destinations. We invite our guests to breathe the fun and the excitement of a new adventure in the same way that they can enjoy the peace of the calm nature.

name: Costa Rican Vacations
description: Enjoy private, custom designed trips by Local Experts. From adrenaline-inducing adventures to relaxing beach vacations, our team will listen to your needs and craft the ideal experience to fit. No other agency can match our commitment to customers, local knowledge and expertise. We offer 24/7 In-country support, and 100% satisfaction guarantee. Let us design your perfect, worry-free vacation so that you can focus on enjoying it!

name: Filikuri Beach
description: Filikuri beach is a small bay surrounded by high cliffs. The Filikuri beach is located between the beach of Potam and the beach of Llaman. Access to the beach become easily by boats which you can hire from different places or even swimming. If you want to spend an entire day in Filikuri make sure to get enough food and plenty of water with you because no shops on the beach.

name: King Spa
description:
my family travel to Japan for summer vacation and discovered the culture of Onsen, tradition of hot and cold, sinus & hot tubs, along with the therapeutic massage.
we did some research and found a similar location back home called spa world in Centerville, Virginia. 
that it was an hour ride from our home in Maryland. We took the track ghostly enjoyed ourselves. Well there we mentioned to another couple how wonderful it was to have found something similar to the Japanese on in the US and the couple suggest we visit King Spa in Chantilly., 
The next weekend we drove to Chantilly and were amazed at how large King Spa is. our experience there as far surpassed anything we found in Japan even though it’s more of a Korean style spa. The service is five star. The cleanliness is is outstanding in the facility is absolutely amazing. They have about a dozen hot saunas of all different types in the pool outside is the absolute perfect warm temperature along with three Jacuzzis and then another indoor pool with a waterfall.  food also is excellent, Korean Pho,  and  also burgers, Philly cheesesteak , chicken, wings, and other treats.  we started telling all of our friends about King spa but now we’re a little reluctant to as it’s getting a bit crowded on weekends because obviously everyone is telling their friends about it.  with that said I would highly recommend King spa is the place for ultimate relaxation and good health.
