description: This popular working religious complex, completed in 1994, includes a shrine and a monastery.

name: Dalat Flower Park
description: Da Lat Flower Garden is a beautiful and peaceful attraction, perfect for nature lovers and photography enthusiasts. Located near Xuan Huong Lake, the garden showcases a wide variety of vibrant flowers, including roses, hydrangeas, and orchids, all blooming in colorful displays. The well-maintained pathways make it easy to explore, and the atmosphere is serene and relaxing. Visitors can enjoy walking through themed sections and admiring the artistic arrangements. It's a wonderful place to escape the busy city and connect with nature. Da Lat Flower Garden is a must-see destination for anyone visiting the city

name: Valley of Love
description: Just as true love has to surpass several obstacles, the Valley of Love in Dalat had to surpass many challenges in the past in order to gain its rightful name today. In the beginning, the valley was called Vallée D’amour (Valley of Love) by the French before being renamed The Valley of Piece. In 1935, its beauty and captivation persuaded people to once again name it after the most wonderful thing in the world: Love. Thanks to being the honeymoon destination of newly-married couples, this valley is even regarded as Niagara Fall of Vietnam. The Valley of Love today is located 4 miles away from the center of Dalat, the little Paris, on Phu Dong Thien Vuong St.

name: Crazy House
description:
A new experience to be able to visit one of the inns designed by one of the architects from Vietnam. And a house concept that is indeed made out of the box, because when entering the house, we might get lost, because every corner is confusing. And there are some areas where the stairs are getting smaller and the stairs are in a fairly high position. So you could say you have to be careful too.

In addition to being a tourist destination, we can also try staying here. Because it is indeed designed as an inn too.

To enter here there is an entrance ticket fee.
If you are visiting Da Lat, make sure to include it in your travel plans.

name: Dalat Market
description: This enormous market is where the locals shop for vegetables, fruit and wine.

name: Xuan Huong Lake
description: Xuan Huong Lake is one of the most scenic spots in Dalat, offering a peaceful atmosphere and stunning views. Walking or cycling around the lake is a great way to enjoy the cool weather and take in the beauty of the surrounding landscape. However, during peak tourist seasons, it can get quite crowded, and some areas around the lake could be better maintained. The food stalls nearby offer tasty local snacks, but prices can be a bit high. Despite these minor drawbacks, Xuan Huong Lake remains a must-visit spot for anyone looking to relax and enjoy nature in Dalat

name: Dalat Railway Station And Museum
description: In its heyday, Dalat Station boasted three arrivals and departures daily. The French built the railway station itself, while the zigzagging tracks were planned and implemented by the Swedish, experts in tricky terrain.

name: Da Lat Cable Car - Robin Hill
description: The cable car runs from Robin Hill to the Truc Lam Monastery and was built by an Austrian company. The ride covers 2,3km, with 50 brightly painted cabins spanning the distance. The panoramic views of Dalat are worth the effort. Contact by What's App: - Reservation - Booking Tour - Car rental - Accommodation

name: Charm spa massage Đà lạt
description: Berry is an incredibly sweet and professional receptionist! She always welcomes guests with a bright smile, provides attentive support, and makes you feel comfortable from the moment you step into the spa. Her thoughtfulness and friendly attitude will definitely make you want to come back! 🌸✨

name: Da Lat Night Market
description: Discovered and architecturally planned by the French more than a century ago, the temperate climate of Da Lat found up here makes it one of the most romantic cities in Vietnam https://azguidepost.com/see-do-eat-guide-to-dalat-vietnams-city-of-eternal-spring/

name: Tuyen Lam Lake
description: My time at Tuyen Lam Lake was so refreshing. The landscape is breathtaking, with peaceful waters reflecting the green hills around it. Renting a paddle boat allowed me to explore the lake further, making for a relaxing and scenic experience. Tuyen Lam Lake is a must-visit for nature lovers wanting to experience Da Lat’s serene charm.

name: Bao Dai's Palace - King's Palace 1 (Dinh 1)
description: Preserved almost intact, this is the most popular of the three Bao Dai palaces in town; Bao Dai was ousted by Ho Chi Minh in 1945.

name: Lang Biang Trail
description:
Lang Biang Trail

Trekking on Langbian Mountain offers a unique experience, showcasing its renowned beauty with three pointed peaks. Standing at an elevation of 2167 meters above sea level, you can enjoy panoramic views of Dalat and the surrounding towns. The trail takes you through hilly grasslands, forests, and jungles, providing an opportunity to immerse yourself in the local people's way of life and their warm hospitality.

Join us on this popular trek in Dalat, where you can learn about the flora and fauna of Vietnam's central highlands. Marvel at the breathtaking sights of plantations, evergreen pine forests, mountains, picturesque valleys, and the stunning Golden Lake from Langbian's three peaks.

Covering a total distance of approximately 14 kilometers, this trek presents a thrilling challenge that will test not only your leg strength but also the endurance of your knees as you navigate the ups and downs of the hills. Along the way, you will witness the gradual transformation o

name: Statue Of Golden Buddha
description: Appears as "Thien Vien Van Hanh" on maps. Is located off "Phu Duong Thien Vuong" street and is only a few minutes walk from the Valley of Love.

name: Sculpture Tunnel
description:
Went with one friend and spent 2 hours taking pictures, doing the shooting and archery activities (cheap and fun) with a couple beers. Its what you make of it, if you actually spend time looking close or trying to make funny photos its a great half day activity but we saw others just rushing around disappointed. 120.000VND is a fair price compared to other local activities and the drinks/snacks inside aren’t extortionate.

One thing to note is that it seems like they are expanding at the moment with building so in a few months time it will be even better to go to.

name: Lam Vien Square
description: While in Dalat, we took the opportunity to visit the bustling and vibrant Lam Vien public square. The establishment features various shops for shopping opportunities, cafes- there are small food vendors that offer a range of culinary delight and kids will have lots of fun activities to do from gaming to virtual reality. Visitors can enjoy the live atmosphere, take leisurely strolls, and soak in charming surroundings. While strolling you can spot K'fe restaurant - an amazing architectural designee establishment that blew my mind.

name: Cau Dat Tea Hill
description: Chao was my guide and she was so nice and sweet! She can help u take photos too if you're travelling solo.  Highly recommend. Very relaxed tour with good scenery!

name: The French Quarter
description: The French colonial houses in this neighborhood are in disrepair, but still exude a sense of Dalat’s former ambience.

name: XQ Da Lat Art House
description: A great place to visit if you like good art. Was very impressed by many of the works on display. Spent three hours wandering around the place. Had to look at some of the portraits up close, they looked as good as photos but are embroidered!

name: Thien Vuong Co Sat Pagoda
description: This serene pagoda was built by locals and is commonly called the "Chinese pagoda."

name: Domaine de Marie Church
description: Domaine de Marie is a complex of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Da Lat.The monastery church is located on a hilltop and dates back to its original construction in 1940 and represents the French and Vietnamese style of architecture. It was built in a style reminiscent of 17th century French architecture. The walls are made of pink limestone. And the roof of the complex is designed in the Nha Rong style, a type of house on stilts typical of the Central Highlands of Vietnam. Local residents nicknamed it the “Cherry Church.”The church has stained glass windows and a large 3-meter statue of the Virgin Mary standing on a globe. The statue resembles a Vietnamese woman and was designed by French architect Joncher in 1943. It was presented by Mrs. Suzanne Humbert, wife of Jean Decoux (Governor General of French Indochina from July 1940 to March 9, 1945). She died in a traffic accident in 1944. Her grave is located just outside the church lobby, in a spacious area strewn with many flowers.The church is part of the complex of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Da Lat, which also has two monasteries where local children are educated.

name: Linh Son Pagoda
description: The pagoda sits on top of a hill not far from the center of Dalat.  It has a very nice garden in the back; visitors should be sure to explore behind the main temple building.

name: Trickland 3D Museum
description: Trick Land is the first 3D painting museum in Dalat, Vietnam. All paintings are done by Vietnamese artists. Welcome to an interesting and wonderful place where you can touch painting with your hands, become the main character of the painting, take pictures with it and feel it.

name: Da Lat King Palace I
description: King Palace 1 is situated not far from Dalat city center. It is sorrounded by a pine forests. It has great historical stories mostly associated with the last 13th emperor of Vietnam, King Bao Dai. While inside the palace, you have to imagine what it was like for a king to live in such a beautiful, charming and romantic place. The rooms look intact with realistic statues of the emperor and empress. There is the support of a recorded voice over in three languages (English, Vietnamese and Korean) that help you to understand the in-depth details of the activities that happened during the hostilities and war situations in the southern  Vietnam. There is an interesting story about the underground escape route that had been built during the period. Unfortunately, the opportunity to view this phenomenal place is not part of the tour. Lots of boutique sold on sight, horse riding activities and photo shoots with king&queen costumes.

name: Lam Dong Museum
description: the presence of the military school in the town give a musical note.The sight of the sunshine equal to the warm feeling of not being cold,this is the last bit of unreconstructed french culture.I went there in 1974.This is a online review.

name: Dalat Cathedral
description: My group visited this Cathedral for the first time on Sunday 15/12/24 in the afternoon and adoration was going on so we went in quietly and sat at the back of the Church. It’s a beautiful Cathedral. After the adoration was over we proceeded to the altar and there was an unusual but lovely nativity scene with Noah’s ark. Shortly after, someone lit up the decorations and it was so attractive. There is also a well stocked religious articles’ shop at the back of the Cathedral that sold many books, rosaries, statues & other items. The side entrance of the Cathedral was made to look like the entrance into a cave which I thought was unique and interesting. On the whole it was a nice visit to the Cathedral

name: Park Prenn
description: This is a place to avoid... your typical asian mistreatment of animals and animal cruelty!!! The animals live in very bad conditions and are forced with violence and pain if they don’t comply with the guides. I would go back, but only to condemn and protest against the horrible things that are going on there!!!

name: Hang Nga Guest House and Art Gallery
description: "The crazy house" is part art gallery, part hotel and all the whimsy of an eccentric architect. Have a cup of tea inside a giant giraffe, visit the monkey cage and relax in the sculpture garden.

name: Prenn Falls
description: Popular attractions augment the natural misty beauty of the cascading water; try the cable car ride, smile for roving photographers and climb the rickety ladder to the tree house.

name: Blandy's Wine Lodge
description: Located in a historical building in the very center of Funchal, Blandy's Wine Lodge has been the heart of the family's wine business for 7 generations, ageing the finest Madeira wines in a traditional canteiro method. Each room in the Lodge has unique wine ageing potential due to the different temperatures and humidity conditions, resulting in the diverse profiles of wines aged inside the building. We invite you to join us on our tours, wine tastings and events! Learn more about Madeira wine, history of the Blandy Family, witness canteiro wine ageing and enjoy one of the many wine tasting options we offer.

name: St. Beatus-Höhlen, Swiss Caves
description:
i dont consider this a must-do, especially if it is your first trip to bernese oberland. 

but the cave with river system is more interesting than i thought

plus, the bus route there is scenic since it goes along lake thun 

take note you have to hike a steep paved trail for 15 min once you get there, since the entrance to the cave is in the middle of a rock face.

name: Pier 39
description: From amazing views and a sea of sea lions to chowder bread bowls and California wines, your visit to San Francisco starts at PIER 39. Kick off your visit by exploring two levels of dining, entertainment, shopping and attractions, all surrounded by unbeatable views of the city and the bay. Take it from the world famous sea lions: a visit to San Francisco starts at The PIER.

name: Edessa Waterfalls
description: Spectacular waterfalls! Nature at it's best. I suggest to start in the old town with the unique architecture and then wander down through the main park then to the waterfalls. I strongly suggest to visit the small cave. It only cost one euro to go in and then venture all the way down to see the other waterfalls. It's a bit of a walk but well worth it.Be prepared to get wet(feet included) when you got to the bottom.

name: KSL City Mall
description:
The last time I came here was in July 2023. That time I came alone. This time, my wife asked me to orientate her. I showed her how to take bus F100 from JB Sentral Bus terminal (bus fare RM1.50 and on return RM1.40). Simple and easy, and there is free wifi on board the bus. We do not have free WiFi on our buses or trains.

We explored the many shops and restaurants in the mall, and she said the general layout is like a maze. The atrium and the alleys are narrow and congested. Seem like the mall management is overly efficient in capitalizing on every inch of the floor to generate rental profits. Even the cart layout at the Glutton Corner is quite clamped.

She was amazed at the dozens of hair salons and massage parlors at the upper floors and wondered if their businesses would be able to sustain in such a competitive environment. LOTUS supermarket is quite crowded, and many Singaporeans who are price conscious probably come here for grocery shopping beside cinema shows, body massage, and gastronomic indulgence.  We noted that 1.2kg of quick cook oats cost RM8.99 (about S$2.80/-) while a 1 kg quick cook oat at our NTUC Fair price supermarket would cost S$4/-. It is more than a dollar difference. 

We went to a nearby kopitiam and ordered a bowl of thunder tea rice, which cost RM9.50 (at Tampoi, the same bowl cost RM7 or RM8) and a plate of char kway teow costs RM8/-. While the char kway teow is palatable, the portion is too meagre, and my wife got another bun (RM6) in order to make her stomach full. One Singaporean uncle complained that the bak kut teh at a shop opposite KSL cost RM20 with only two or three pieces of miserable pork ribs in the broth. I also noticed the price of tao Sar piah biscuits has also increased. Previously, a particular brand only cost RM14, but I saw the box now increased to RM19/-. 

Singaporeans like to find relaxation at KSL. We are always searching for cheaper and better services and goods in JB. Pin Min Xuan Cantonese dim sum attracted long queue of patrons. Singaporeans like not only the quality but it is relatively cheaper than you can find in Singapore. If things become too expensive, then it would deter many of Singaporeans from coming here.

name: Aquatica San Antonio
description: Aquatica San Antonio is where the South Seas meets South Texas in a waterpark experience only SeaWorld could create. With waters from serene to extreme, Aquatica features all the attractions and amenities that family memories are made of. Come immerse yourself in the wonders of the sea at Aquatica(R) San Antonio, and your inner Aquatican as you play side-by-side with the sea, or relax on white-sand beaches.

name: Lohan Nightclub
description: Lohan Nightclub is a concept created by well known businessman Dennis Papageorgiou and Hollywood superstar Lindsay Lohan as a means to revive the local Athenian clubbing scene and bring people together. With an industrial baroque aesthetic, a top of the line sound and lighting system, and the best DJ and live acts.

name: New Years Eve Fireworks London
description: With its iconic Nelson’s Column, majestic oversized lions and brightly-lit fountains, Trafalgar Square is not just considered the heart of this bustling London hub, but the very core of the city itself. Beyond this esteemed gathering place are more famous icons, as well as a disproportionate numbers of the city’s most popular cultural attractions including the National Gallery and many West End theaters. Along the way to these major sites are quiet lanes and antiquated pubs to discover, as well as riverside vistas to enjoy on the embankment. With a calendar full of celebratory events, any time of year is a fine time to visit.

name: United States Botanic Garden
description: Steeped in history, the United States Botanic Garden inspires people to appreciate, study, and conserve plants to enrich society locally and globally. The U.S. Botanic Garden campus includes the Conservatory, the gated outdoor gardens, and Bartholdi Fountain and Gardens. The Garden features more than 44,000 plants with major collections including orchids, roses, plants native to the United States, food and economic plants, carnivorous plants, and more.

name: Vondelpark
description: At one of Amsterdam's most famous parks, travelers can enjoy a host of outdoor activities amid beautiful English-style landscaping. Here, you can hike the countless trails or ride a bike around to spot charming bandstands and even a sculpture by Picasso along the way. Have a picnic by the pond as herons and ducks waltz past or pop by one of the many cafes in the park. You might want to visit between April and May to see the park awash with tulips in bloom or between May and September to watch live concerts at the open-air theater. – Tripadvisor

name: Kinstone
description: This Modern Megalithic Garden leaves you feeling as if you have visited an older world in a different time. We offer tours, retreats, workshops, and even concerts! No place like it! Kinstone features one of the largest privately owned stone circles in the world and tons and tons of granite boulders, standing stones and sculptures. Come to enjoy the stones, see our gardens, find a spot for quiet contemplation to re-connect to nature, or make a personal pilgrimage along The Way of the Stones. Located in rural Fountain City, Wisconsin, just off County Road M on Cole Bluff Lane, it is a contemplative, park-like place with spectacular views. This 30-acre bluff-top property has over 100 standing stones; three stone circles, dolmen, classic 7-circuit labyrinth, thatched, cordwood chapel, dry-stack stone sculpture, natural buildings, food forest gardens, raised bed gardens and more. There are several alignments of interest at Solstices and Equinoxes. You will love to wander around this place!

name: British Pullman, A Belmond Train, England
description: Escape the every day on a thrilling adventure aboard the Belmond British Pullman luxury train. Step into lovingly restored vintage carriages—each with a story to tell. Our liveried stewards are on hand to pamper as gastronomic delights arrive at linen-coated tables, set with sparkling crystal and bespoke silverware. Savour exquisite cuisine with five course lunches, afternoon teas and exclusive celebrity chef dinners. Or choose from enchanting trips to historic cities, stately homes and sporting events. Embark on a timeless adventure from London, and revel in the spirit of the golden age of travel.

name: Sedona Stargazing
description: Sedona Stargazing is pleased to offer you a personalized and custom astronomy experience by professional astronomers. You will meet us at our observing location which is a 20 minute ride from West Sedona in the Village of Oak Creek. Your tour includes an overview of the constellations using a high power laser pointer. We then give you an up close view of planets, galaxies, star clusters and nebula through one of our large powerful telescopes. Each guest has a pair of wide field view binoculars and each reservation group will have their own Celestron C11 gps auto position telescope. Our astronomers are exceptionally knowledgeable and provide you with an educational and entertaining experience. Sedona Stargazing has received the Award of Excellence 10 years in a row from TripAdvisor resulting in our induction into the TripAdvisor Hall of Fame. We have been featured in National Geographic and the New York Times and ranked by TripAdvisor as one of the top 10 US Space Based Attractions

name: Southern Michigan Railroad
description: For those willing to embark on a short fantasy with some Christmas cheer, you’ll find the Santa Train to be a nice experience. You’ll appreciate the quaint and historic nature of the train as the slow moving rustic scenery gives way to an industrial park. You’ll “ohhh and ahh” at Santa waving and greeting you on the back platform of “The Santa Train” on a neighboring track as your train pulls up. You’ll keep your spirits up as you alight one train for a quick photo op with the Santa Train as you wait to hop on for your turn to see the Jolly Old Elf. You’ll the joke and kid about Santa being in his “traveling suit” as you unwrap both magical Santa Keys given to you by Santa as you take your seats. Then as you start your return journey, you’ll sip a perfectly kid sized hot chocolate and you’ll sing along as the train becomes a Christmas Karaoke party.For those more akin to Scrooge, the Grinch before his change of heart, or are expecting a Disney level theatrical experience, you may struggle. Try to keep your, “the music is too loud”, “this train is slow”, “bathrobe” and “oh gee this isn’t  Starbucks” comments to yourself. Smile and make the trip magical for those who still believe.In all seriousness, we had a great time and are glad we were able to get tickets.

name: Old Bisbee Ghost Tour
description: The Old Bisbee Ghost Tour is the original ghost tour in Bisbee and the only one of its kind. With over 16 years of experience in bringing the haunted history of Bisbee, Arizona to visitors of our amazing town! Your Ghost Host will lead you on this walking tour through Old Bisbee's streets, stairways, and old alleys after dark on an adventure to discover and learn about the ghosts that haunt this 125 year old town. Learn their history and favorite haunts while seeing Old Bisbee when very few do, after sunset. Visit the haunts of Julia, a lady of the evening who enjoys the company of married men staying alone in her room, Nat the miner who owed money to the Money Man and paid for it with his life, and the Lady in White who saved the lives of three children.

name: Safari Desert Tours
description: Safari Desert Tours offer a selection of private day Tours and Sahara desert Tours. departure from All cities in Morocco.

name: Burgh Bits and Bites Food Tours
description: We had a great and tasty time with Richard! Super informative and entertaining. Even locals on the tour said they learned a lot.

name: Oamaru Blue Penguin Colony
description: The Oamaru Blue Penguin Colony provides visitors with an opportunity to see little penguins in their natural environment. In the evening, visitors are captivated by watching the nightly arrival of penguins from their days fishing at sea. The Colony is a tourism operation with a strong research and conservation focus. At the core of the operation is a long-term conservation programme that ensures the penguins are protected and that the population achieves long-term stability. An important and unique part of that conservation programme is the Colony's Research Scientist who is now one of New Zealand’s leading little penguin experts.

name: Bavarian Belle Riverboat
description: Thank you for visiting Frankenmuth. Our family operates the Bavarian Belle riverboat, an authentic SternDriven Paddlewheel riverboat. We offer a 1-hour historical narrated tour of the Frankenmuth area on our fully restored 150-passenger vessel. The Bavarian Belle is open air canopied on the upper deck and has a fully enclosed lower salon with restrooms. We offer a snack bar and soft drinks on board. The Bavarian Belle is located "At The Waterfall" in the River Place Shops shopping village. Our dock and lower level are handicap accessible. One hour trips are offered Monday - Sunday 11am till Dusk, (departing every 90min), Early May to Mid-October. Please call for pre-Memorial Day and post-Labor Day hours. Extended hours are available for Group Tours and Special Events (Weddings, Reunions, etc.). Tickets are $18.00 for adults and $7 for children 12 and under, children 4 and under are Free. Group tickets are discounted to $17.00 per adult ticket with groups of 20 or more adults.

name: Koloa Zipline
description: Kauai's LONGEST zipline course is home to 3 of the 5 longest ziplines on Kauai. Featuring our 1/2 mile Waita Zip. Each of our lines average over 1,000' in length and have you Flying through the jungle, soaring above the forest and gliding across the water. We're also the only Zipline on Kauai that offers headfirst ziplining with our Flyin' Kauaian Harness! Located just 5 minutes from the major resorts of Poipu, Koloa Zipline is the closest of all activities to the South side of Kauai.

name: Beetrip
description: Beetrip is a travel agent specialising in inbound tour. Our products are various from car, hotel to package tours ( full services) and motorbike tour...Our mission is to bring out the most convenient and the best experience for travellers while travelling to Vietnam.

name: L'Apothiquaire Spa
description: The original L'Apothiquaire branch is ideally situated in the heart of downtown, close to the main hotels and offering the perfect urban sanctuary and spa. Housed in a quaint, lovingly restored century-old French townhouse. L'Apothiquaire features high ceilings, original tiling, an exposed brick wall and wooden stairs. The antique furniture enhances the old world charm which transports you away from the hectic pace of modernity. Upon entering, L'Apothiquaire is a boutique with traditional wooden cabinets - resembling a 17th century French Apothecary. Along the cabinets is an array of the comprehensive range of L'Apothiquaire's beautifully packaged organic body and face oils, scrubs, bath salts, organic soaps and organic herbal blends, from France. An intimate foot-care room overlooks a small courtyard featuring a gargoyle and orchids. Upstairs are seven private & semi-private treatment rooms draped with luxurious, velvet curtains. An elegant suite featuring a private Jacuzzi. Treatments follow the L'Apothiquaire philosophy of using only the finest, natural and organic ingredients to offer a delicate but effective healing process for mind and body. Trained beauty consultants will put you at ease, tailor a treatment to suit your individual needs and recommend an going program to ensure your renewed radiance is maintained. L'Apothiquaire Artisan Beaute opened in 2005 and was voted 'Best Beauty Salon' in the same year. It offers the ultimate in body care and facials, a unique experience not to be missed.

name: Brothers - Boutique Men's Spa & Salon
description: Brothers was created to provide a comfortable, spirited and valuable place for men to get a great haircut, a traditional shave, facial treatments and many spa services. In short, the ultimate grooming experience for men. Located in the heart of the city, next to the iconic Opera House. All this while sipping on a craft beer or glass of cold whisky, we take care of you so you don't have to...

name: Apocalypse Now Bar
description: Apocalypse Now Bar is not only the oldest bar in Saigon but also a safe and famous destination for tourists for 28 years. People come to Apo, not to drink, but to meet and enjoy the warm and open atmosphere without any Saigon bars. The tourist often say to each other: "Not to come to Saigon but to Apo, it seems that they have not come to Saigon ..."

We aim to provide customers with the number one quality experience in Ho Chi Minh City. We offer a one-week nail warranty for customers and design nails according to their requirements and preferences, using 100% genuine, long-lasting polish. Our team consists of professional and dedicated technicians who are here to serve you. Additionally, when you visit ROSEMARY, you will be treated to snacks and drinks. All our products are 100% imported."

We provide the best local guides and tailored tours for a better understanding about the culture, cuisine, traditions, the real stories behind this fascinating city of Vietnam. Currently we are having 30+ local experts with a great diversity of personalities and tour types to show you around - the local way

name: Sa Spa
description: Located in a quiet alley at the heart of Saigon, Sa spa was designed with inspiration from a cozy Saigon house, where tropical garden, vintage wooden furniture, charming lace and silk curtains reflect the essence of true Saigonians. We provide a full range of skin care treatments, massage therapy, body care, manicures, pedicures, waxing and hair care in a beautiful and relaxing environment.

In this store I found an endless variety of beautiful silk colors, different designs and a personal approach to the client. 
I was very pleased with the price)) .

name: OUROS Travel
description:
OUROS Travel is a Vietnam travel company specializing in tailor-made multi-destination tours and ground transportation services. 
We provide:

name: Vera Nails & Spa
description: New salon offers various types of beauty services. We offer facials, eyelash extension, hair washing/shampoo, earwax removal, shaving, foot and body massages, manicure and pedicure, artificial nails with a large selection of brand name regular or gel polishes. Your safety is our top priority so we clean and sterilize our equipment after every customer so you can have a peace of mind.

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

name: Garner State Park
description:
It’s a pretty drive getting to the park, kind of a rollercoaster at times with all the hills and curves. Old Baldy Trail is a short trail, about half mile, but feels way longer as it’s very steep and rocky. Along the way you can get a bird’s-eye view of the Frio River canyon. The last part of the trail gets steeper and more difficult but at the summit you are rewarded with 360 views of the whole area. It’s a fun hike, but challenging, and watch for loose rocks. 
White Rock Cave Trail leads to part of the Bridges Trail which ultimately leads to the Crystal Cave Trail. It is a couple of miles with some very steep and rocky parts. Some areas were very challenging due to the steepness of the trails. The panoramic views and scenery along the way make up for the hard trek. There are also caves along the way to explore. 
Lots to do and explore in the day use campgrounds and Frio River area. It’s a nice park with several hiking trails, including a leisurely half mile nature trail. There are outdoor things to do and plenty of spots to camp out for a day. It can be as relaxing or as extreme as you want.

name: Valley Shepherd Creamery
description: For all the critics complaining about the "cheap" experience that is "expensive", please keep in mind the Creamery is a family artisan cheese business started by a couple who risked everything to do something amazing when no one else was.  There is an actual cheese cave, built by the owners, and it is the most incredible cheese you will ever experience. I take every single guest to New Jersey of mine to the cheese shop. When the season allows, we take the tour. In the fall, we take our picnic basket with a bottle of wine, buy bread, cheese, sausage, and then go to the apple orchard nearby for apples and other goodies, and find a spot to picnic either on the orchard or a nearby creek. Give a small family business a break, people, this is back-breaking 24/7 work for approximately 20 years.  I only buy cheese at the Creamery (it's REAL goat and sheep cheese!), or when I'm eating my way through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx where I get my Italian cheeses. It is worth the price. The animals are shepherded into a merry-go-round they designed and had shipped in pieces from Italy, and they are doing what they love, which is RARE. I often ship boxes or stock up my suitcase to take to my family. One time the staff even packed my order and left it for me to pick up after hours so I could make my flight. The first time I stumbled upon the Creamery I was driving by and thought I was in England because the sheep were in the the roadside pasture.  Sometimes the animals are there for your viewing, or petting at the fence - just like at the Zoo when you can't see the animal you most expected - do you criticize the Zookeeper for not giving you what you paid for? I am your biggest cheerleader, Valley Shepherd Creamery!

description: The cruise itself was quite nice.However, we had a major problem as the speakers were incredibly loud, especially damaging was the vocal volume.The singing itself was quite nice, but the volume was ear piercing, at dangerous levels. It was extremely uncomfortable for myself my wife and her parents.I reported the issue to the staff not once not twice, but three times. They said they would do something about it, but they did not. We had to cover our ears to protect them, but unfortunately the damage was done.My wife had severe ear pain for the next 3 days and my ear was also quite sore for a few hours after leaving the vessel.I reported the issue to the captain and his staff .Although I am a foreigner here in Vietnam, I speak fluent Vietnamese so communciation was not an issue.. I also mentioned it to the singer, I told her the music was excellent, but the volume was dangerously loud.She laughed and thought it was funny as did the other members of staff.I then called the company the next day to report the issue in order to protect future customers and they basically ignored my report.Two weeks later. I contacted them again and they denied that it was possible for someone's hearing to be damaged by high volume on speakers.I have worked with sound for over 20 years and it is certainly possible (common knowledge in fact).It is not safe to play music at this volume particularly when live vocals are involved.It's a shame because the cruise has a lot of potential but I would strongly warn against going on this Cruise unless you bring ear protection.Very disappointing.Saigon is lovely though as his Vietnam. name: Tallink Silja Line
description:
This is a great way to get from Helsinki to Stockholm without flying. It sails between the two cities leaving Helsinki at 5pm local and arrives at Stockholm at 10am local time. 

The terminal where the ship departs from Helsinki has a tram stop in front of it which is useful if you need to get there and do not have any transfers or do not want to walk.

The check in process was simple and easy, I scanned a QR code and collected my boarding pass (which doubled as my room key) as well as two tickets, one for a restaurant and one for a bus transfer at Stockholm. 

I paid for an A suite with a sea view, however the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the suite itself is quite dated. I tried to move one of the beds to make a double bed but the wall and the floor under the bed were dirty so I decided against that. This was disappointing as the suite was one of the more expensive options.

The ship itself departed and arrived on time and the facilities on board were great otherwise. Another reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that wifi is only available in the COMMON AREAS of the ship and not in the suites (unless you pay for the very expensive suites).

name: Löyly Sauna
description:
After researching extensively, Loyly was heavily suggested, and it was one of the few saunas which were open on Monday and allowed mixed genders, so we decided to book before we came to Helsinki.
We booked our slot from 20:00-22:00, we arrived just before 20:00 and were served by two friendly ladies who explained where everything was and handed us our towels and locker keys. The locker rooms are unbelievably small given the number of lockers they have, so it’s slightly difficult to navigate getting changed and getting to your locker when there’s a few people in there. I dread to think what it’s like on the weekend!
There were only two saunas open instead of three but after reading the reviews this seems to be a common occurrence. The two saunas which were open were decent but for the size of the establishment and how busy it can get, I was expecting bigger saunas as even we noticed that sometimes they were both full. Beware some people (guessing they’re locals) will come in and pour water over the rocks without asking, this didn’t bother me because I have a high tolerance to heat; but if you don’t, be prepared to move out quickly.
There are communal showers with hot and cold water available. There’s a jetty with two rails which take you directly to the Baltic Sea. The water is very shallow with large, sharp rocks, so make sure you don’t run and jump in! It’s nice that the sauna is separate from the restaurant and outdoor dining area as I would’ve felt uncomfortable wandering around half naked whilst people were eating. I’d suggest bringing another towel with you, as we found after getting in the water we’d use the towels to dry off, but when we went to shower then get changed, the towels were still wet.
They have multiple seating inside and out if you fancy a break from the heat. They also have a log fire with comfy sofas and tap water available to keep you hydrated. You also have the option to set up a tab, if you’d like to have any soft or alcohol drinks.
Overall, a brilliant experience to immerse yourself into the finish culture. Slightly let down that only two saunas were available and that the locker rooms were very small.

name: German Village
description: A highway bridge over Interstate 70 is all that separates the German Village Historic District from downtown Columbus, but as one looks east from the interstate, the difference between old and new is glaring. A 20+ story structure sits just north of the interstate bridge, and just south, in German Village, no structure is higher than three stories. Five blocks south, the spire of St. Mary Church stands 197’ off the sidewalk and towers over everything around it. Structures and sidewalks are orange masonry, and many streets (about half) are still brick pavers. German Village does not have a recreated sense of history or kitschy Bavarian feel ~ rather, it is a neighborhood with architecture dating from the 1840s-1890s that has been preserved, and its use as a shared residential and commercial neighborhood has been maintained. People walk to their destinations, park on the street due to the overwhelming absence of driveways, and live life at a very pedestrian level. The neighborhood is extremely dense ~ very often only inches separate neighboring structures, and many structures were built for multi-family use. German Village is notably different because its appearance has changed so little.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

description: Went for Greenday, Simple plan, Avril and Sum 41..I really wanted to see them (Sum have announced that, after this year, they will no longer do anything) and so it was worth it just because they were bands that UNFORTUNATELY we will not see often in Italy..but this organization deserves to fail. Yesterday, July 9, I went mainly for Simple, but due to motorway accident + Milan exit that sucks as always, we delayed the arrival by an hour, that is at 5 pm (gate opening at 4 pm from schedule) and the thing was "resolved" with queue of two and a half hours, missing the entire repertoire of Simple Plan + half of Avril. One access, VIP access with security people twiddling their thumbs and passing the time laughing and joking. I'm talking about yesterday, because they made me miss a gig and a half, but in June, with Greenday it was still bad. Audio-wise probably a bluetooth speaker would have made more, the output is not even noteworthy, packed and squeezed into some kind of funnel and I just wonder if there had been an emergency, how could we have ever quickly escaped from that place. Of course now there are these fantastic Tokens or whatever they are called: 10 euros for 5 of the latter, embarrassing I would say. Which, I find absurd, if you want water and you walk past the station that sells it, you can't take it. So do 300/400 meters to go to the cash register where you can exchange your money for these tokens, queue, exchange money, do another 300/400 meters, another line and maybe finally after 1 hour you can order a bottle of water without a cap. Anzi no! Water finished, beer and spritz all you want, but water not, while in the background speaks the Guide voice of the concert that says "I recommend! Drink a lot to avoid fainting." You deserve to fail, none of our comments will change anything unfortunately because here we navigate in very very large organizations, but I just hope to save some poor innocent soul who would just like to enjoy music, but would only end up queuing up long and going home disappointed and with at least 100 euros less in their wallet. name: Turtle Conservation Center
description: The Turtle Rescue and Rehabilitation Center or Phang Nga Coastal Fisheries Research and Development Center (PCFRDC), Thai name ศูนย์วิจัยและพัฒนาประมงชายฝั่งพังงา is located in the city of Thai Mueang (30 minutes drive from Phuket from the exit to the mainland in Phang Nga from the Sarasin Bridge). The center breeds turtles and releases adult individuals into the wild.The territory of this center is quite large, there are 6 large covered pavilions, marked with the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, on which there are concrete vessels with taps from which sea water is poured as needed (the location next to the beach of Tai Muang allows you not to limit yourself in sea water, which is very convenient). In appearance, the vats for turtles do not look glamorous, of course, but the contents of these concrete boxes are amazing and diverse, this is definitely worth seeing for everyone interested in marine fauna. There are practically no people on the territory, we walked around several pavilions, an exhibition and pools with fish, only near the turtles we met a group of volunteers. One of them spoke English quite well (the guy graduated from the economics faculty and came to the center for the rescue of turtles to volunteer), he told us about the center. Entrance to the territory is free.The rehabilitation center in halls A and B houses clownfish, jellyfish, sea urchins and young turtles (it turns out there are as many as 28 species of clownfish, 11 of which are bred at the PCFRDC). The fish reproduce well even in captivity, they are actually fed with plankton grown especially for them, and then sold to other aquariums and oceanariums throughout Thailand. Further on there is a section where you can see rescued, but already injured turtles - both green and olive, which are unlikely to be able to live in normal marine conditions. Young turtles become prey for various predators, ready to bite off their back leg or a piece of shell. name: Mystery Spot
description: The Mystery Spot is a gravitational anomaly located in the redwood forests just outside of Santa Cruz, California. It is a circular area of effect around 150 feet or 46 meters in diameter. Within the Mystery Spot you will be stunned as your perceptions of the laws of physics and gravity are questioned. But don't take our word for it, come and decide for yourself! The Mystery Spot was discovered in 1939 by a group of surveyors and opened to the public in 1940. The Mystery Spot has amazed and perplexed hundreds of thousands of visitors from all over the world, and many return time and time again to experience these puzzling variations of gravity, perspective, and height. Some speculate that cones of metal were secretly brought here and buried in our earth as guidance systems for their spacecraft. Some think that it is in fact the spacecraft itself buried deep within the ground. Other theories include carbon dioxide permeating from the earth, a hole in the ozone layer, a magma vortex, the highest dielectric biocosmic radiation known anywhere in the world, and radiesthesia. Whatever the cause is, it remains a mystery.

name: Horseshoe Bend

Although the desert hike is relatively easy, you won’t encounter much shade, so be sure to bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. name: Grand Casino Beograd
description: The entry staff is pretty friendly, and there are no complications on the passport check-in, they have certain countries that they allow the IDs of, but for the rest, they need passports as it's in Serbia's Government Law to have a database of people gambling from other countries (probably if you win big, but I don't think it's the case).Overall the casino looks pretty nice, nothing too crazy but for an Easter European Casino, it's pretty decent. Smoking is indeed allowed inside so if you are a non-smoker you might be a little bit uncomfortable but it's not anything too crazy (I don't smoke and wasn't that affected by it).You have the first floor with slot machines and some electric roulette for those who don't want to play Live Games, you don't have a wide variety of games on these machines and some might be a little low to mid-grade (they don't have those top-of-the-line slot machines). As expected in a casino - don't expect to win and only enter with money you can lose without repercussions as the machines don't give anything compared to other casinos I've visited.For Blackjack enthusiasts and players! I don't recommend playing at their BJ tables since they have an automated re-shuffler which means all the cards coming out are truly random so you don't even have the player advantage at the live tables. They advertise that they have smaller tables on their website (500 RSD) but you will only see the 1000RSD+ being opened (even on busy nights) with no side bets.The dealers are content, neither friendly nor rude, they feel like they are just trying to do their job and nothing else, which isn't something surprising to be fair.Soft drinks are on the house if they see you play and you have a selection of drinks that they offer for free but you need a waiter to come to you while sitting at a machine/table, all the drinks requested at the bar/restaurant are charged.Roulette follows the same principle, the smallest table opened is 1000 outside and 100 inside.You have exchange offices inside the casino and ATMs (however the "trusted" bank ones don't work and they only have the kind that takes a pretty big amount of tax per withdrawal.)All in all, it's worth it for the "rookie" experience, I wouldn't consider it a casino I would usually go to even if I lived in the area as it seems like they did all they could to increase the house odds, so if you are in it only for the heck of it - go ahead.

name: Hug Point State Park
description:
As a photographer and filmmaker from the East Coast, I’ve seen my fair share of breathtaking landscapes, but nothing could have prepared me for the sheer magnificence of Oregon’s coast. My recent trip to Hug Point State Park and Cannon Beach left me completely in awe—the natural beauty, the light, and the atmosphere were unlike anything I had ever experienced.

I was visiting an old high school friend, and after a long, rewarding hike through Arch Cape with his dog, we decided to head down to the beach, cooler full of IPAs in hand, and settle in for what would become one of the most unforgettable evenings of my life.

The beach was vast, pristine, and lively—filled with beachgoers soaking up the warm glow of an Indian summer day in the fall. There was a bonfire crackling in the distance, kids running along the shore, and couples walking hand in hand as the sun began to dip toward the horizon.

And then came the sunset—a masterpiece in real-time. I have never seen colors so rich, so surreal, stretching across the sky and reflecting off the ocean like liquid fire. It was the kind of scene that makes you forget everything else and just exist in the moment.

This trip also gave me the perfect chance to test out my new Canon R6 mirrorless camera, and it delivered in ways I couldn’t have imagined. Every shot—whether of the waves crashing against the cliffs, the silhouettes of beachgoers against the golden sky, or the raw joy of my friend’s dog chasing the tide—became a slice-of-life masterpiece.

If you’ve never been to Hug Point or Cannon Beach, do yourself a favor and go. Whether you’re a photographer, nature lover, or just someone seeking a place that feels truly magical, this part of Oregon will blow your mind. I came expecting a beautiful beach—I left with an experience I’ll never forget.

Highly, highly recommended.

name: Miami Riverwalk Trail
description: Miami has one of the best urban walks of any city.  In addition to the river, you can continue to walk along long sections of Biscayne Bay in the Brickell district. From our hotel in Brickell district, we were easily able to reach the Bay before sunrise and have an incredible walk.  In addition to the walk along the bay and river, there are several parks that have other features as well as lots of public art.  The walk along the bay in Brickell south of the river is approximately 1.25 miles with most of that on the water.  The walk to Bayfront Park north of the river is nearly 0.75 miles with most of that walk also on the water.The views of the bay, the skyscrapers and the marine activity both natural and man-made is amazing and an attraction itself.  In fact, this is one of my favorite activities from our time in Miami.  At some point during your stay, you need to walk the waterfront of Miami.  It is truly beautiful, maybe the most beautiful of any city.

description:
Plentiful market stalls with some great summer clothes, belts, bags, toys, towels.
I purchased 3 tops and a pair of cotton trousers in the first aisle alone.
Be prepared to barter and don't be cohersed into buying by some of the strong willed stall holders.
Bought more ladies clothes down the 4th and 5th aisle and also 2 leather belts for my son.
Had to stop there as wouldn't be able to get anything else in my holdall.
Go early as around 11.00am it starts to get really busy.
I went at 9.30am and it was really busy at 11.30am when I left.
Great morning out.

name: Playa Lagun
description: When searching for beaches be aware that the bigger ones are usually very busy and have restrictions on chair use, etc. The quieter beaches are farther west on the island but are situated in coves and therefore quite small. These can be busy as well depending on the time of day.

name: The Corniche
description:
We borrowed an electric scooter and drove along the water. 
Very annoying is that you are approached by so many people to participate in the boat trip.

But a boat trip at night is an absolute recommendation: about 40 QR for two people (15-20 min.)

name: Mamutik Island
description:
The island is very pretty and could be even more so if it was run better. Unfortunately, every day hordes of rowdy Chinese tourists arrive who unfortunately are not very polite and often leave rubbish lying around. Moreover, most of them, barely afloat, jump unconsciously into the sea with lifebuoys and often to rest they stand on corals.
Apart from that you can find nice and quiet corners, away from the pier.
The seabed is rather gray and has a damaged coral reef but nevertheless snorkeling is still pleasant; I found angelfish, parrot, crossbow, trumpet, staff sergeants, a sea snake, small moray eels, many anemones with clownfish and others.
The island can be reached in about 20 minutes from Jesselton Pier with the ferry service that departs continuously; the boats are a little run down and run a lot, Recommendation to ask to decrease the speed. Look at the weather forecast because in the afternoon it often rains and in ten minutes heavy thunderstorms arrive with which it is not pleasant to go to sea to return to KK.

name: Mahogany Beach
description:
Mahogany Beach is a great place to watch the day go by. It's a beautifully tranquil beach. There is a small fee to enter, but it is a small price to pay for such a well staffed beach. 

On the site, there is a gift shop and regular stalls for the locals to sell their crafts and wares. The bar serves full food, and the drinks are well stocked. The staff are friendly and happy to accommodate off menu cocktails. There is plenty of seating located throughout the beach.

The sea bed is a bit rocky in places, but the sand is soft underfoot everywhere else. Apparently, there are mineral pockets in the sea, so be prepared to experience warm spots throughout the area.
 
I don't know if you can still access it, but there is a little entrance to the side of the cave where you can have a nice adventurous climb back up to the road.

What's great about this beach is that you can enjoy a full day here. You can turn up and spend the day just lounging or you can hop on a catamaran trip or participate in the many watersports  (subject to booking availability) or you could just enjoy full access to the beach.

What's not so great, the resident dog family. They are so sweet and passive, but I'm just not a fan. Despite this, I enjoy this beach so much that I'm going to let that one slide.

name: Historic Galveston Ghost Tours
description: Welcome to Historic Galveston Ghost Tours - the #1 Rated Tour! 10,000 souls lost their lives in one night and they're still dying to meet you. Filled with horror, Galveston's history is unmatched with episodes of murder, suicide, pirates, ghosts and visions that will plaque your very soul. Unworldly visions that cannot be rationally explained. The true stories that you'll hear explain why they won't stay dead. Be brave!

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

description: I went there yesterday with my 2 kids and my niece. We paid over $100 for 2 adults and 2 minor children, plus an additional $16 for 2 robes. The place is falling apart, boards on benches with peeling paint, dusty, dirty corners around each area of the pools. The water inside each of the pools was full of debris and dirt. The women’s locker room was so bad I can’t describe how gross I felt changing there it made me want to throw up. Piles of dirty towels and robes piled up to almost the ceiling!! There were 3 staff members working at the front desk but nobody was checking on the bathrooms. There was no place to put your baggage, the lockers are tiny and so people’s bags were all over the locker room floor, you could barely walk. They do not limit the amount of people at one time so it was very overcrowded and they were not prepared with staff. We left after 30 minutes. Biggest waste of money and I will never be back.

name: Lake Bled
description: Discover the magic of the lake that attracts travellers from near and far. The current unique shape of the year did not emerge coincidentally. A tectonic hole made by the Bohinj glacier through the years, was once at the location of the present lake. Its path was obstructed by a huge rock which was so persistently scraped that the only thing that remained was the present island. The ice melted and the basin was filled with water, thus Lake Bled emerged, which is in some places up to 30 metres deep and quite popular amongst divers. 19 species of fish live in the lake, including carp, sheatfish and lake trout. Ducks and swans as well as diverse plants also swim and thrive on its surface.

name: Howth Cliff Walk
description: We started the walk opposite the dart station. I would not recommend doing this as it is a long incline (1 hour of climbing) on a path through the back of housing estates. There’s nothing particularly nice about it. Once you get to the cliffs it is beautiful! However, that beautiful part is quite short (about 20 mins) and then back on the road heading down town again. The town itself is lovely with a nice harbour. We had fish and chips in Beshoffs which was superb. If I was going again I would start the walk by walking from dart station through the pretty town and then up to the cliffs from there. There are signs for the start of each level of walk as you walk past and beyond the harbour. You could do the loop and return down opposite the dart station. Personally, I would just go up to the cliffs from the town and back down again and then walk back to the dart station via the pretty town and of course stopping at Beshoffs for fish and chips.

name: Garner State Park
description:
It’s a pretty drive getting to the park, kind of a rollercoaster at times with all the hills and curves. Old Baldy Trail is a short trail, about half mile, but feels way longer as it’s very steep and rocky. Along the way you can get a bird’s-eye view of the Frio River canyon. The last part of the trail gets steeper and more difficult but at the summit you are rewarded with 360 views of the whole area. It’s a fun hike, but challenging, and watch for loose rocks. 
White Rock Cave Trail leads to part of the Bridges Trail which ultimately leads to the Crystal Cave Trail. It is a couple of miles with some very steep and rocky parts. Some areas were very challenging due to the steepness of the trails. The panoramic views and scenery along the way make up for the hard trek. There are also caves along the way to explore. 
Lots to do and explore in the day use campgrounds and Frio River area. It’s a nice park with several hiking trails, including a leisurely half mile nature trail. There are outdoor things to do and plenty of spots to camp out for a day. It can be as relaxing or as extreme as you want.

name: Valley Shepherd Creamery
description: For all the critics complaining about the "cheap" experience that is "expensive", please keep in mind the Creamery is a family artisan cheese business started by a couple who risked everything to do something amazing when no one else was.  There is an actual cheese cave, built by the owners, and it is the most incredible cheese you will ever experience. I take every single guest to New Jersey of mine to the cheese shop. When the season allows, we take the tour. In the fall, we take our picnic basket with a bottle of wine, buy bread, cheese, sausage, and then go to the apple orchard nearby for apples and other goodies, and find a spot to picnic either on the orchard or a nearby creek. Give a small family business a break, people, this is back-breaking 24/7 work for approximately 20 years.  I only buy cheese at the Creamery (it's REAL goat and sheep cheese!), or when I'm eating my way through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx where I get my Italian cheeses. It is worth the price. The animals are shepherded into a merry-go-round they designed and had shipped in pieces from Italy, and they are doing what they love, which is RARE. I often ship boxes or stock up my suitcase to take to my family. One time the staff even packed my order and left it for me to pick up after hours so I could make my flight. The first time I stumbled upon the Creamery I was driving by and thought I was in England because the sheep were in the the roadside pasture.  Sometimes the animals are there for your viewing, or petting at the fence - just like at the Zoo when you can't see the animal you most expected - do you criticize the Zookeeper for not giving you what you paid for? I am your biggest cheerleader, Valley Shepherd Creamery!

description: The cruise itself was quite nice.However, we had a major problem as the speakers were incredibly loud, especially damaging was the vocal volume.The singing itself was quite nice, but the volume was ear piercing, at dangerous levels. We had to cover our ears to protect them, but unfortunately the damage was done.My wife had severe ear pain for the next 3 days and my ear was also quite sore for a few hours after leaving the vessel.I reported the issue to the captain and his staff .Although I am a foreigner here in Vietnam, I speak fluent Vietnamese so communciation was not an issue.. I also mentioned it to the singer, I told her the music was excellent, but the volume was dangerously loud.She laughed and thought it was funny as did the other members of staff.I then called the company the next day to report the issue in order to protect future customers and they basically ignored my report.Two weeks later. I contacted them again and they denied that it was possible for someone's hearing to be damaged by high volume on speakers.I have worked with sound for over 20 years and it is certainly possible (common knowledge in fact).It is not safe to play music at this volume particularly when live vocals are involved.It's a shame because the cruise has a lot of potential but I would strongly warn against going on this Cruise unless you bring ear protection.Very disappointing.Saigon is lovely though as his Vietnam. name: Tallink Silja Line
description:
This is a great way to get from Helsinki to Stockholm without flying. It sails between the two cities leaving Helsinki at 5pm local and arrives at Stockholm at 10am local time. 

The terminal where the ship departs from Helsinki has a tram stop in front of it which is useful if you need to get there and do not have any transfers or do not want to walk.

The check in process was simple and easy, I scanned a QR code and collected my boarding pass (which doubled as my room key) as well as two tickets, one for a restaurant and one for a bus transfer at Stockholm. 

I paid for an A suite with a sea view, however the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the suite itself is quite dated. I tried to move one of the beds to make a double bed but the wall and the floor under the bed were dirty so I decided against that. This was disappointing as the suite was one of the more expensive options.

The ship itself departed and arrived on time and the facilities on board were great otherwise. Another reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that wifi is only available in the COMMON AREAS of the ship and not in the suites (unless you pay for the very expensive suites).

name: Löyly Sauna
description:
After researching extensively, Loyly was heavily suggested, and it was one of the few saunas which were open on Monday and allowed mixed genders, so we decided to book before we came to Helsinki.
We booked our slot from 20:00-22:00, we arrived just before 20:00 and were served by two friendly ladies who explained where everything was and handed us our towels and locker keys. The locker rooms are unbelievably small given the number of lockers they have, so it’s slightly difficult to navigate getting changed and getting to your locker when there’s a few people in there. I dread to think what it’s like on the weekend!
There were only two saunas open instead of three but after reading the reviews this seems to be a common occurrence. The two saunas which were open were decent but for the size of the establishment and how busy it can get, I was expecting bigger saunas as even we noticed that sometimes they were both full. Beware some people (guessing they’re locals) will come in and pour water over the rocks without asking, this didn’t bother me because I have a high tolerance to heat; but if you don’t, be prepared to move out quickly.
There are communal showers with hot and cold water available. There’s a jetty with two rails which take you directly to the Baltic Sea. The water is very shallow with large, sharp rocks, so make sure you don’t run and jump in! It’s nice that the sauna is separate from the restaurant and outdoor dining area as I would’ve felt uncomfortable wandering around half naked whilst people were eating. I’d suggest bringing another towel with you, as we found after getting in the water we’d use the towels to dry off, but when we went to shower then get changed, the towels were still wet.
They have multiple seating inside and out if you fancy a break from the heat. They also have a log fire with comfy sofas and tap water available to keep you hydrated. You also have the option to set up a tab, if you’d like to have any soft or alcohol drinks.
Overall, a brilliant experience to immerse yourself into the finish culture. Slightly let down that only two saunas were available and that the locker rooms were very small.

name: German Village
description: A highway bridge over Interstate 70 is all that separates the German Village Historic District from downtown Columbus, but as one looks east from the interstate, the difference between old and new is glaring. A 20+ story structure sits just north of the interstate bridge, and just south, in German Village, no structure is higher than three stories. Five blocks south, the spire of St. Mary Church stands 197’ off the sidewalk and towers over everything around it. Structures and sidewalks are orange masonry, and many streets (about half) are still brick pavers. German Village does not have a recreated sense of history or kitschy Bavarian feel ~ rather, it is a neighborhood with architecture dating from the 1840s-1890s that has been preserved, and its use as a shared residential and commercial neighborhood has been maintained. People walk to their destinations, park on the street due to the overwhelming absence of driveways, and live life at a very pedestrian level. The neighborhood is extremely dense ~ very often only inches separate neighboring structures, and many structures were built for multi-family use. German Village is notably different because its appearance has changed so little.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

description: Went for Greenday, Simple plan, Avril and Sum 41..I really wanted to see them (Sum have announced that, after this year, they will no longer do anything) and so it was worth it just because they were bands that UNFORTUNATELY we will not see often in Italy..but this organization deserves to fail. Yesterday, July 9, I went mainly for Simple, but due to motorway accident + Milan exit that sucks as always, we delayed the arrival by an hour, that is at 5 pm (gate opening at 4 pm from schedule) and the thing was "resolved" with queue of two and a half hours, missing the entire repertoire of Simple Plan + half of Avril. One access, VIP access with security people twiddling their thumbs and passing the time laughing and joking. I'm talking about yesterday, because they made me miss a gig and a half, but in June, with Greenday it was still bad. Audio-wise probably a bluetooth speaker would have made more, the output is not even noteworthy, packed and squeezed into some kind of funnel and I just wonder if there had been an emergency, how could we have ever quickly escaped from that place. Of course now there are these fantastic Tokens or whatever they are called: 10 euros for 5 of the latter, embarrassing I would say. Which, I find absurd, if you want water and you walk past the station that sells it, you can't take it. So do 300/400 meters to go to the cash register where you can exchange your money for these tokens, queue, exchange money, do another 300/400 meters, another line and maybe finally after 1 hour you can order a bottle of water without a cap. Anzi no! Water finished, beer and spritz all you want, but water not, while in the background speaks the Guide voice of the concert that says "I recommend! Drink a lot to avoid fainting." You deserve to fail, none of our comments will change anything unfortunately because here we navigate in very very large organizations, but I just hope to save some poor innocent soul who would just like to enjoy music, but would only end up queuing up long and going home disappointed and with at least 100 euros less in their wallet. Grazie I Days, grazie Live Nation, a mai più!

name: Turtle Conservation Center
description: The Turtle Rescue and Rehabilitation Center or Phang Nga Coastal Fisheries Research and Development Center (PCFRDC), Thai name ศูนย์วิจัยและพัฒนาประมงชายฝั่งพังงา is located in the city of Thai Mueang (30 minutes drive from Phuket from the exit to the mainland in Phang Nga from the Sarasin Bridge). The center breeds turtles and releases adult individuals into the wild.The territory of this center is quite large, there are 6 large covered pavilions, marked with the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, on which there are concrete vessels with taps from which sea water is poured as needed (the location next to the beach of Tai Muang allows you not to limit yourself in sea water, which is very convenient). In appearance, the vats for turtles do not look glamorous, of course, but the contents of these concrete boxes are amazing and diverse, this is definitely worth seeing for everyone interested in marine fauna. There are practically no people on the territory, we walked around several pavilions, an exhibition and pools with fish, only near the turtles we met a group of volunteers. One of them spoke English quite well (the guy graduated from the economics faculty and came to the center for the rescue of turtles to volunteer), he told us about the center. Entrance to the territory is free.The rehabilitation center in halls A and B houses clownfish, jellyfish, sea urchins and young turtles (it turns out there are as many as 28 species of clownfish, 11 of which are bred at the PCFRDC). The fish reproduce well even in captivity, they are actually fed with plankton grown especially for them, and then sold to other aquariums and oceanariums throughout Thailand. Further on there is a section where you can see rescued, but already injured turtles - both green and olive, which are unlikely to be able to live in normal marine conditions. Young turtles become prey for various predators, ready to bite off their back leg or a piece of shell. Plus, fishermen with their nets and chains also add to the sad statistics in the number of injured beauties.The turtles at the rehabilitation center have been provided with conditions for laying eggs (there is a special white sand area where they can crawl out and bury their eggs).Turtles are very beautiful!

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…
