name: Little Tokyo
description: Lots of Asian restaurants. Chosen for Bibimcup, Korean. Delicious. Good atmosphere, neat. We got there around 6pm, after that it became very busy.

name: Quay Street
description:
I would never stop walking back and forth along this street, the beating heart of the city: here you can breathe the real Ireland, the one that speaks Gaelic (when it goes from the countryside to the city) and that sings stories of emigration, of cows, of sheep and green.
Very colourful, full of pubs and enriched by the goldsmiths of the famous Claddagh ring and the Aran knitwear shops: it is not a place for nightlife because life shuts down - except for a handful of clubs - no later than 11pm.
But truly a delightful place!

name: Klondike Park
description: We rented out all 6 cabins as well as some of the campsites for a group camping trip with friends. I had a hard time finding much info on the cabins, so I thought I would share what I can.  Based on the park map I chose cabin B for myself as it appears to be very close to the showerhouse/bathrooms.  What the map doesn't show is that cabins are sort of on a bluff and the campsites and bathrooms/showers are located at the bottom of that. In order to reach the bathrooms you must walk through all the cabins and down a set of stairs that is near cabin D. Then walk back the direction you came. Soooo.. if you're like me and want convenient bathroom trips, none of the cabins are close, but cabin D is your best choice.  The cabins themselves were a step above camping in that you don't have to set up a tent, but the beds were a similar level of comfort as sleeping on the ground.  All 6 cabins had hundreds of stinkbugs inside of them when we arrived.  That didn't bother me a huge amount as I expect to encounter bugs when in nature, but not everyone was so thrilled about it. I loved how the cabins were grouped together since we had rented them all to spend time with friends, but if you're looking for a secluded spot, this is probably not for you. We had a great time, but I'm not sure this is someplace we will stay again.

name: Mauna Kea Oceanfront Luau
description: The setting is on a beautiful resort. Entry was supposed to be at 5:10 however it wasn’t until 5:30 when guests started getting checked in. We paid for general seating so we received a black lei (premium seating got white leis) and our mai tai. Once everyone was seated the premium guests received some chips and dip. Then we were invited to get up and walk over to the pit with the pig yo watch the pig get unearthed. Then we were invited to plate up. The food was very good. While we’re eating the show started. Which was a good show. I would conclude this by saying I wouldn’t recommend this luau due to the price and what is (isn’t) included. I think adding maybe some activities and a memorabilia like a glass to take home would make it worth it to me.

name: SAHARA Las Vegas
description: Las Vegas Strip, a neon wonderland that never sleeps, is the epicenter of thrill and entertainment. This glittering neighborhood boasts some of the world's most opulent casinos, luxury hotels, and awe-inspiring performances, all spread along a 4-mile stretch. The iconic Bellagio Fountains, the Eiffel Tower at Paris Las Vegas, and the High Roller Ferris Wheel are among the captivating landmarks that dot the skyline. Food lovers can relish a diverse range of culinary experiences, from high-end dining at restaurants run by celebrity chefs to casual eateries. With an efficient monorail system and abundant taxis, navigating The Strip is a breeze for visitors.

name: Boston's "Politically Incorrect" North End Food Tour
description: Boston’s “Politically Incorrect North End Food Tours Boston's "North End" is a pocket-sized Italian neighborhood teaming with history and charm. Among the narrow streets, hidden alleyways and park benches you will find The Paul Revere House, and The Old North Church. Absorbing the history and folklore of the North End cannot be done properly without coupling it with the culinary lining of the neighborhood. As home to over eighty restaurants and countless wine shops, bakeries, and Italian salumerias. It is safe to say you won’t leave hungry because I will take you to many of these shops where you will endulge on some of the best foods Little Italy has to offer . The great food goes hand and hand with the great stories Anthony, your local guide,will tell you . Anthony is the only Italian speaking guide born and raised in the neighborhood .Many tours go through this neighborhood and everyone proclaims how local they are . NOT TRUE . Most tour guides are college kids with a summer job .

name: De'Ricci Cantine Storiche
description:
We started our tour at the vineyard just outside of Montepulciano, we were welcome by Fred who explained the history of the winery with a very pleasant manner. We were then introduced to the table where we sat for a fabulous lunch of simple but delicious food coupled with what should have been 4 wines but ended up being 5. During our tasting Fred explained with great passion each wine, he is very knowledgeable and loves his job.
 
We were also introduced to the owner’s son who was very humble and had a nice way about him.
 
After lunch we visited the cellars in Montepulciano where again Fred explained in great depth the history of the building followed by another 2 tastings. After the tour finished with sat with Fred at a local bar and share more wine and stories with him. We have done a lot of wine tastings and this is the best one in terms of explaining the wines and giving the whole experience.

You will enjoy this trip to the harmony of clip clopping, the rolling wheels and the tinkling sounds of the harness. name: XQ Sài Gòn
description: XQ Silk is one of those unsung craft heroes that are trying to keep alive the beautiful traditions of silk embroidering in Vietnam. The shop is easy to find. It is about 150m past Binh Tanh marketon the same side of Le Lai Street. It looks a bit like a private gallery, but inside are some of the most beautiful embroidery works you will ever see. They use embroidery like oil colour paintings with the ability to capture light variations and depth of field. Why this really does stand out is because to be honest most of the stuff sold in markets in Vietnam is just tourist crap. This is the real thing, with a weaving school in Dalat and lots of pictures that the art is indeed truly Vietnamese as it is often pictured being given to visiting dignitaries. Costs for this quality are actually quite low ranging form around US$40 to $300. Staff are all beautifully attired in Ao Dai, the stunning traditional costume for women. Truly this is a breathe of fresh air for those who want to get away from the copy watches, cheap sunglasses and Lonely Planet clutching backpackers.

name: L'Apothiquaire Spa
description: The original L'Apothiquaire branch is ideally situated in the heart of downtown, close to the main hotels and offering the perfect urban sanctuary and spa. Housed in a quaint, lovingly restored century-old French townhouse. L'Apothiquaire features high ceilings, original tiling, an exposed brick wall and wooden stairs. The antique furniture enhances the old world charm which transports you away from the hectic pace of modernity. Upon entering, L'Apothiquaire is a boutique with traditional wooden cabinets - resembling a 17th century French Apothecary. Along the cabinets is an array of the comprehensive range of L'Apothiquaire's beautifully packaged organic body and face oils, scrubs, bath salts, organic soaps and organic herbal blends, from France. An intimate foot-care room overlooks a small courtyard featuring a gargoyle and orchids. Upstairs are seven private & semi-private treatment rooms draped with luxurious, velvet curtains. An elegant suite featuring a private Jacuzzi. Treatments follow the L'Apothiquaire philosophy of using only the finest, natural and organic ingredients to offer a delicate but effective healing process for mind and body. Trained beauty consultants will put you at ease, tailor a treatment to suit your individual needs and recommend an going program to ensure your renewed radiance is maintained. L'Apothiquaire Artisan Beaute opened in 2005 and was voted 'Best Beauty Salon' in the same year. It offers the ultimate in body care and facials, a unique experience not to be missed.

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

name: Hot Sulphur Springs Resort & Spa
description: I went there yesterday with my 2 kids and my niece. We paid over $100 for 2 adults and 2 minor children, plus an additional $16 for 2 robes. When we stepped out of the front entrance into the outdoor pool area it was disgusting!! The place is falling apart, boards on benches with peeling paint, dusty, dirty corners around each area of the pools. The water inside each of the pools was full of debris and dirt. The women’s locker room was so bad I can’t describe how gross I felt changing there it made me want to throw up. Piles of dirty towels and robes piled up to almost the ceiling!! There were 3 staff members working at the front desk but nobody was checking on the bathrooms. There was no place to put your baggage, the lockers are tiny and so people’s bags were all over the locker room floor, you could barely walk. They do not limit the amount of people at one time so it was very overcrowded and they were not prepared with staff. We left after 30 minutes. Biggest waste of money and I will never be back.

name: Lake Bled
description: Discover the magic of the lake that attracts travellers from near and far. The current unique shape of the year did not emerge coincidentally. A tectonic hole made by the Bohinj glacier through the years, was once at the location of the present lake. Its path was obstructed by a huge rock which was so persistently scraped that the only thing that remained was the present island. The ice melted and the basin was filled with water, thus Lake Bled emerged, which is in some places up to 30 metres deep and quite popular amongst divers. 19 species of fish live in the lake, including carp, sheatfish and lake trout. Ducks and swans as well as diverse plants also swim and thrive on its surface.

The town itself is lovely with a nice harbour. We had fish and chips in Beshoffs which was superb. If I was going again I would start the walk by walking from dart station through the pretty town and then up to the cliffs from there. Personally, I would just go up to the cliffs from the town and back down again and then walk back to the dart station via the pretty town and of course stopping at Beshoffs for fish and chips.

name: Garner State Park
description:
It’s a pretty drive getting to the park, kind of a rollercoaster at times with all the hills and curves. Old Baldy Trail is a short trail, about half mile, but feels way longer as it’s very steep and rocky. Along the way you can get a bird’s-eye view of the Frio River canyon. The last part of the trail gets steeper and more difficult but at the summit you are rewarded with 360 views of the whole area. It’s a fun hike, but challenging, and watch for loose rocks. 
White Rock Cave Trail leads to part of the Bridges Trail which ultimately leads to the Crystal Cave Trail. It is a couple of miles with some very steep and rocky parts. Some areas were very challenging due to the steepness of the trails. The panoramic views and scenery along the way make up for the hard trek. There are also caves along the way to explore. 
Lots to do and explore in the day use campgrounds and Frio River area. It’s a nice park with several hiking trails, including a leisurely half mile nature trail. There are outdoor things to do and plenty of spots to camp out for a day. It can be as relaxing or as extreme as you want.

name: Valley Shepherd Creamery
description: For all the critics complaining about the "cheap" experience that is "expensive", please keep in mind the Creamery is a family artisan cheese business started by a couple who risked everything to do something amazing when no one else was.  There is an actual cheese cave, built by the owners, and it is the most incredible cheese you will ever experience. I take every single guest to New Jersey of mine to the cheese shop. When the season allows, we take the tour. In the fall, we take our picnic basket with a bottle of wine, buy bread, cheese, sausage, and then go to the apple orchard nearby for apples and other goodies, and find a spot to picnic either on the orchard or a nearby creek. Give a small family business a break, people, this is back-breaking 24/7 work for approximately 20 years.  I only buy cheese at the Creamery (it's REAL goat and sheep cheese!), or when I'm eating my way through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx where I get my Italian cheeses. It is worth the price. The animals are shepherded into a merry-go-round they designed and had shipped in pieces from Italy, and they are doing what they love, which is RARE. I often ship boxes or stock up my suitcase to take to my family. One time the staff even packed my order and left it for me to pick up after hours so I could make my flight. The first time I stumbled upon the Creamery I was driving by and thought I was in England because the sheep were in the the roadside pasture.  Sometimes the animals are there for your viewing, or petting at the fence - just like at the Zoo when you can't see the animal you most expected - do you criticize the Zookeeper for not giving you what you paid for? I am your biggest cheerleader, Valley Shepherd Creamery!

name: Löyly Sauna
description:
After researching extensively, Loyly was heavily suggested, and it was one of the few saunas which were open on Monday and allowed mixed genders, so we decided to book before we came to Helsinki.
We booked our slot from 20:00-22:00, we arrived just before 20:00 and were served by two friendly ladies who explained where everything was and handed us our towels and locker keys. The locker rooms are unbelievably small given the number of lockers they have, so it’s slightly difficult to navigate getting changed and getting to your locker when there’s a few people in there. I dread to think what it’s like on the weekend!
There were only two saunas open instead of three but after reading the reviews this seems to be a common occurrence. The two saunas which were open were decent but for the size of the establishment and how busy it can get, I was expecting bigger saunas as even we noticed that sometimes they were both full. Beware some people (guessing they’re locals) will come in and pour water over the rocks without asking, this didn’t bother me because I have a high tolerance to heat; but if you don’t, be prepared to move out quickly.
There are communal showers with hot and cold water available. There’s a jetty with two rails which take you directly to the Baltic Sea. The water is very shallow with large, sharp rocks, so make sure you don’t run and jump in! It’s nice that the sauna is separate from the restaurant and outdoor dining area as I would’ve felt uncomfortable wandering around half naked whilst people were eating. I’d suggest bringing another towel with you, as we found after getting in the water we’d use the towels to dry off, but when we went to shower then get changed, the towels were still wet.
They have multiple seating inside and out if you fancy a break from the heat. They also have a log fire with comfy sofas and tap water available to keep you hydrated. You also have the option to set up a tab, if you’d like to have any soft or alcohol drinks.
Overall, a brilliant experience to immerse yourself into the finish culture. Slightly let down that only two saunas were available and that the locker rooms were very small.

name: German Village
description: A highway bridge over Interstate 70 is all that separates the German Village Historic District from downtown Columbus, but as one looks east from the interstate, the difference between old and new is glaring. A 20+ story structure sits just north of the interstate bridge, and just south, in German Village, no structure is higher than three stories. Five blocks south, the spire of St. Mary Church stands 197’ off the sidewalk and towers over everything around it. Structures and sidewalks are orange masonry, and many streets (about half) are still brick pavers. German Village does not have a recreated sense of history or kitschy Bavarian feel ~ rather, it is a neighborhood with architecture dating from the 1840s-1890s that has been preserved, and its use as a shared residential and commercial neighborhood has been maintained. People walk to their destinations, park on the street due to the overwhelming absence of driveways, and live life at a very pedestrian level. The neighborhood is extremely dense ~ very often only inches separate neighboring structures, and many structures were built for multi-family use. German Village is notably different because its appearance has changed so little.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

One access, VIP access with security people twiddling their thumbs and passing the time laughing and joking. I'm talking about yesterday, because they made me miss a gig and a half, but in June, with Greenday it was still bad. Audio-wise probably a bluetooth speaker would have made more, the output is not even noteworthy, packed and squeezed into some kind of funnel and I just wonder if there had been an emergency, how could we have ever quickly escaped from that place. Of course now there are these fantastic Tokens or whatever they are called: 10 euros for 5 of the latter, embarrassing I would say. Which, I find absurd, if you want water and you walk past the station that sells it, you can't take it. So do 300/400 meters to go to the cash register where you can exchange your money for these tokens, queue, exchange money, do another 300/400 meters, another line and maybe finally after 1 hour you can order a bottle of water without a cap. Anzi no! Water finished, beer and spritz all you want, but water not, while in the background speaks the Guide voice of the concert that says "I recommend! Drink a lot to avoid fainting." You deserve to fail, none of our comments will change anything unfortunately because here we navigate in very very large organizations, but I just hope to save some poor innocent soul who would just like to enjoy music, but would only end up queuing up long and going home disappointed and with at least 100 euros less in their wallet. name: Turtle Conservation Center
description: The Turtle Rescue and Rehabilitation Center or Phang Nga Coastal Fisheries Research and Development Center (PCFRDC), Thai name ศูนย์วิจัยและพัฒนาประมงชายฝั่งพังงา is located in the city of Thai Mueang (30 minutes drive from Phuket from the exit to the mainland in Phang Nga from the Sarasin Bridge). The center breeds turtles and releases adult individuals into the wild.The territory of this center is quite large, there are 6 large covered pavilions, marked with the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, on which there are concrete vessels with taps from which sea water is poured as needed (the location next to the beach of Tai Muang allows you not to limit yourself in sea water, which is very convenient). In appearance, the vats for turtles do not look glamorous, of course, but the contents of these concrete boxes are amazing and diverse, this is definitely worth seeing for everyone interested in marine fauna. There are practically no people on the territory, we walked around several pavilions, an exhibition and pools with fish, only near the turtles we met a group of volunteers. One of them spoke English quite well (the guy graduated from the economics faculty and came to the center for the rescue of turtles to volunteer), he told us about the center. Entrance to the territory is free.The rehabilitation center in halls A and B houses clownfish, jellyfish, sea urchins and young turtles (it turns out there are as many as 28 species of clownfish, 11 of which are bred at the PCFRDC). The fish reproduce well even in captivity, they are actually fed with plankton grown especially for them, and then sold to other aquariums and oceanariums throughout Thailand. Further on there is a section where you can see rescued, but already injured turtles - both green and olive, which are unlikely to be able to live in normal marine conditions. Young turtles become prey for various predators, ready to bite off their back leg or a piece of shell. Plus, fishermen with their nets and chains also add to the sad statistics in the number of injured beauties.The turtles at the rehabilitation center have been provided with conditions for laying eggs (there is a special white sand area where they can crawl out and bury their eggs).Turtles are very beautiful!

name: Mystery Spot
description: The Mystery Spot is a gravitational anomaly located in the redwood forests just outside of Santa Cruz, California. It is a circular area of effect around 150 feet or 46 meters in diameter. Within the Mystery Spot you will be stunned as your perceptions of the laws of physics and gravity are questioned. But don't take our word for it, come and decide for yourself! The Mystery Spot was discovered in 1939 by a group of surveyors and opened to the public in 1940. The Mystery Spot has amazed and perplexed hundreds of thousands of visitors from all over the world, and many return time and time again to experience these puzzling variations of gravity, perspective, and height. Some speculate that cones of metal were secretly brought here and buried in our earth as guidance systems for their spacecraft. Some think that it is in fact the spacecraft itself buried deep within the ground. Other theories include carbon dioxide permeating from the earth, a hole in the ozone layer, a magma vortex, the highest dielectric biocosmic radiation known anywhere in the world, and radiesthesia. Whatever the cause is, it remains a mystery.

Although the desert hike is relatively easy, you won’t encounter much shade, so be sure to bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. name: Grand Casino Beograd
description: The entry staff is pretty friendly, and there are no complications on the passport check-in, they have certain countries that they allow the IDs of, but for the rest, they need passports as it's in Serbia's Government Law to have a database of people gambling from other countries (probably if you win big, but I don't think it's the case).Overall the casino looks pretty nice, nothing too crazy but for an Easter European Casino, it's pretty decent. Smoking is indeed allowed inside so if you are a non-smoker you might be a little bit uncomfortable but it's not anything too crazy (I don't smoke and wasn't that affected by it).You have the first floor with slot machines and some electric roulette for those who don't want to play Live Games, you don't have a wide variety of games on these machines and some might be a little low to mid-grade (they don't have those top-of-the-line slot machines). As expected in a casino - don't expect to win and only enter with money you can lose without repercussions as the machines don't give anything compared to other casinos I've visited.For Blackjack enthusiasts and players! I don't recommend playing at their BJ tables since they have an automated re-shuffler which means all the cards coming out are truly random so you don't even have the player advantage at the live tables. They advertise that they have smaller tables on their website (500 RSD) but you will only see the 1000RSD+ being opened (even on busy nights) with no side bets.The dealers are content, neither friendly nor rude, they feel like they are just trying to do their job and nothing else, which isn't something surprising to be fair.Soft drinks are on the house if they see you play and you have a selection of drinks that they offer for free but you need a waiter to come to you while sitting at a machine/table, all the drinks requested at the bar/restaurant are charged.Roulette follows the same principle, the smallest table opened is 1000 outside and 100 inside.You have exchange offices inside the casino and ATMs (however the "trusted" bank ones don't work and they only have the kind that takes a pretty big amount of tax per withdrawal.)All in all, it's worth it for the "rookie" experience, I wouldn't consider it a casino I would usually go to even if I lived in the area as it seems like they did all they could to increase the house odds, so if you are in it only for the heck of it - go ahead.

name: Hug Point State Park
description:
As a photographer and filmmaker from the East Coast, I’ve seen my fair share of breathtaking landscapes, but nothing could have prepared me for the sheer magnificence of Oregon’s coast. My recent trip to Hug Point State Park and Cannon Beach left me completely in awe—the natural beauty, the light, and the atmosphere were unlike anything I had ever experienced.

I was visiting an old high school friend, and after a long, rewarding hike through Arch Cape with his dog, we decided to head down to the beach, cooler full of IPAs in hand, and settle in for what would become one of the most unforgettable evenings of my life.

The beach was vast, pristine, and lively—filled with beachgoers soaking up the warm glow of an Indian summer day in the fall. There was a bonfire crackling in the distance, kids running along the shore, and couples walking hand in hand as the sun began to dip toward the horizon.

And then came the sunset—a masterpiece in real-time. I have never seen colors so rich, so surreal, stretching across the sky and reflecting off the ocean like liquid fire. It was the kind of scene that makes you forget everything else and just exist in the moment.

This trip also gave me the perfect chance to test out my new Canon R6 mirrorless camera, and it delivered in ways I couldn’t have imagined. Every shot—whether of the waves crashing against the cliffs, the silhouettes of beachgoers against the golden sky, or the raw joy of my friend’s dog chasing the tide—became a slice-of-life masterpiece.

If you’ve never been to Hug Point or Cannon Beach, do yourself a favor and go. Whether you’re a photographer, nature lover, or just someone seeking a place that feels truly magical, this part of Oregon will blow your mind. I came expecting a beautiful beach—I left with an experience I’ll never forget.

Highly, highly recommended.

name: Mamutik Island
description:
The island is very pretty and could be even more so if it was run better. Unfortunately, every day hordes of rowdy Chinese tourists arrive who unfortunately are not very polite and often leave rubbish lying around. Moreover, most of them, barely afloat, jump unconsciously into the sea with lifebuoys and often to rest they stand on corals.
Apart from that you can find nice and quiet corners, away from the pier.
The seabed is rather gray and has a damaged coral reef but nevertheless snorkeling is still pleasant; I found angelfish, parrot, crossbow, trumpet, staff sergeants, a sea snake, small moray eels, many anemones with clownfish and others.
The island can be reached in about 20 minutes from Jesselton Pier with the ferry service that departs continuously; the boats are a little run down and run a lot, Recommendation to ask to decrease the speed. Look at the weather forecast because in the afternoon it often rains and in ten minutes heavy thunderstorms arrive with which it is not pleasant to go to sea to return to KK.

name: Mahogany Beach
description:
Mahogany Beach is a great place to watch the day go by. It's a beautifully tranquil beach. There is a small fee to enter, but it is a small price to pay for such a well staffed beach. 

On the site, there is a gift shop and regular stalls for the locals to sell their crafts and wares. The bar serves full food, and the drinks are well stocked. The staff are friendly and happy to accommodate off menu cocktails. There is plenty of seating located throughout the beach.

The sea bed is a bit rocky in places, but the sand is soft underfoot everywhere else. Apparently, there are mineral pockets in the sea, so be prepared to experience warm spots throughout the area.
 
I don't know if you can still access it, but there is a little entrance to the side of the cave where you can have a nice adventurous climb back up to the road.

What's great about this beach is that you can enjoy a full day here. You can turn up and spend the day just lounging or you can hop on a catamaran trip or participate in the many watersports  (subject to booking availability) or you could just enjoy full access to the beach.

What's not so great, the resident dog family. They are so sweet and passive, but I'm just not a fan. Despite this, I enjoy this beach so much that I'm going to let that one slide.

name: Historic Galveston Ghost Tours

Filled with horror, Galveston's history is unmatched with episodes of murder, suicide, pirates, ghosts and visions that will plaque your very soul. Unworldly visions that cannot be rationally explained. The true stories that you'll hear explain why they won't stay dead. Be brave!

Very colourful, full of pubs and enriched by the goldsmiths of the famous Claddagh ring and the Aran knitwear shops: it is not a place for nightlife because life shuts down - except for a handful of clubs - no later than 11pm.

name: Klondike Park
description: We rented out all 6 cabins as well as some of the campsites for a group camping trip with friends. I had a hard time finding much info on the cabins, so I thought I would share what I can.  Based on the park map I chose cabin B for myself as it appears to be very close to the showerhouse/bathrooms.  What the map doesn't show is that cabins are sort of on a bluff and the campsites and bathrooms/showers are located at the bottom of that. In order to reach the bathrooms you must walk through all the cabins and down a set of stairs that is near cabin D. Then walk back the direction you came. Soooo.. if you're like me and want convenient bathroom trips, none of the cabins are close, but cabin D is your best choice.  The cabins themselves were a step above camping in that you don't have to set up a tent, but the beds were a similar level of comfort as sleeping on the ground.  All 6 cabins had hundreds of stinkbugs inside of them when we arrived.  That didn't bother me a huge amount as I expect to encounter bugs when in nature, but not everyone was so thrilled about it. I loved how the cabins were grouped together since we had rented them all to spend time with friends, but if you're looking for a secluded spot, this is probably not for you. We had a great time, but I'm not sure this is someplace we will stay again.

Then we were invited to get up and walk over to the pit with the pig yo watch the pig get unearthed. Then we were invited to plate up. The food was very good. While we’re eating the show started. They use embroidery like oil colour paintings with the ability to capture light variations and depth of field. Why this really does stand out is because to be honest most of the stuff sold in markets in Vietnam is just tourist crap. This is the real thing, with a weaving school in Dalat and lots of pictures that the art is indeed truly Vietnamese as it is often pictured being given to visiting dignitaries. Costs for this quality are actually quite low ranging form around US$40 to $300. Staff are all beautifully attired in Ao Dai, the stunning traditional costume for women. Truly this is a breathe of fresh air for those who want to get away from the copy watches, cheap sunglasses and Lonely Planet clutching backpackers.

name: Suytun Cenote
description: Located outside the charming town of Valladolid in southeast Mexico, Suytun Cenote is a breathtaking natural sinkhole that attracts many travelers. The highlight is the middle platform of the cenote, which offers a stunning photo op, especially when rays of sunlight shine through the cave opening above. Just remember to bring a camera that can handle the low light. You can also take a dip into the turquoise waters (but not before wearing a life vest) and marvel at the beautiful stalactites hanging from the ceiling. Get there early in the day to beat the crowds. Consider exploring some of the other beautiful cenotes in Yucatan on a private tour. – Tripadvisor

name: Rail Bike Adventures
description: Watch where you are going.  I ran right into the bike in front of us.  PSA, taking pictures while being the person on the break is not a good idea.  Don’t worry, everyone was ok.My wife, 10 year old daughter, and I went and had an enjoyable time.  The views are pretty and it is really cool going over the bridge just for trains.  Great views of the lake and lots of trees.  Though, I am not sure what the future holds as there is a subdivision going up right along the path.  I guess it will be ok, but being out on the trail without seeing the houses is enjoyable.It is an out and back trip.  They turn the bikes around at the end of the trip and you get about 10 minutes rest.  There are benches.  There are no bathrooms at the turn around point.  I honestly felt the ride back was faster than the ride there.  Likely fear of unknown.I felt this was a fun activity but might be better with a kid that can reach the peddles.   Our daughter certainly met the 48 inch height minimum but if felt like she could not really peddle.  It could be another child at same height could.  That meant my wife and I were peddling the three of us on a 4 person bike.  Our legs were tired at the end.  Don’t not go and try, it is worth it, but just wanted you to know that some kids might not be able to reach the peddles.  The front seats can reach closer to the peddles than the back seats.  The front right rider has control of the hand break.The staff had excellent communication between the station and each other as they approached intersections.  Even when the active train car was at the station, there was great communication so everyone knew we were approaching the station.  There did not seem any risk that an active train could be on our track, but you can feel good that the people supervising us were trained, knowledgeable and formal with their communication.  They were not goof offs.The give good instructions, but it is hard to hear them if you are in the last bike like we were.  There is a single restroom at the station so come a little early.  Plus you will need to complete the waiver.  At the end of the ride, they spray each seat with disinfectant.   Cool.We very much enjoyed the activity.  We are in good shape, but our legs were tired at the end.  Enjoy.

Treatments follow the L'Apothiquaire philosophy of using only the finest, natural and organic ingredients to offer a delicate but effective healing process for mind and body. Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

The women’s locker room was so bad I can’t describe how gross I felt changing there it made me want to throw up. Piles of dirty towels and robes piled up to almost the ceiling!! There were 3 staff members working at the front desk but nobody was checking on the bathrooms. There was no place to put your baggage, the lockers are tiny and so people’s bags were all over the locker room floor, you could barely walk. The ice melted and the basin was filled with water, thus Lake Bled emerged, which is in some places up to 30 metres deep and quite popular amongst divers. 19 species of fish live in the lake, including carp, sheatfish and lake trout. The town itself is lovely with a nice harbour. We had fish and chips in Beshoffs which was superb. If I was going again I would start the walk by walking from dart station through the pretty town and then up to the cliffs from there. There are signs for the start of each level of walk as you walk past and beyond the harbour. You could do the loop and return down opposite the dart station. Personally, I would just go up to the cliffs from the town and back down again and then walk back to the dart station via the pretty town and of course stopping at Beshoffs for fish and chips.

name: Megali Petra Beach
description:
Personally it did not seem like the paradise described in the other reviews.

Beautiful sea for goodness sake, but between the inconvenience of access, parking and even services honestly I was not so impressed.

I state that with two small children perhaps it is more complex because the beach being surrounded by rocks has a sea that soon becomes deep and this perhaps affects the review, but the road to the beach is really uncomfortable.
We arrived at 9:30 in the morning and already the parking lots were almost full (10 € full day seems correct to me), on the return with the cars parked even along the narrow return routes it is practically a challenge to pass if in front of you find another car in the opposite direction.

The sea is beautiful, as it is beautiful throughout the island. Maybe for a long holiday it is still worth spending a day there, but really in Lefkada there is much better.

Recommendation to bring water and food to face the day

With great love & pride of Saigon, our mission is to create 360* experience from exploring how Vietnamese handcrafted products creatively 'breath in' traditional-mixed-trendy elements and enjoying local culinary delights under relaxing retro atmosphere. Each product conveys a story about the process of skillful local workmanship making it with care and patience, about geographical origin of natural materials, and about how our Vietnamese and international designers bring creativity and their inspiration to life. name: William Heise County Park
description: For years, I've driven past the turnoff to this park as I was headed to Julian from the Cuyamacas.As I've explored the usual sites & trails in the San Diego backcountry, I thought I've give the park a try.  (Hiking, picnicking, not camping).First, we got our picnic lunch from a alt-health grocery store in Alpine, then drove to the Lagunas, enjoying the scenic highway towards Julian.I spotted the turnoff sign and navigated the slow, winding road, 3-4 miles to the park.  It's longer than I expected, but the distance from the road provides total silence upon reaching the entrance.There's a nominal fee, and the person in the booth will provide a map and directions, if needed.  We parked near the picnic area.  There's a bathroom nearby, at least two.  (Showers, too, for campers).The picnic area is 1-2 minutes away, with benches.Facing the nearby hills, feeling the sun on my shoulders, watching the clouds, it's a gentle reminder why I love San DIego County.

Explore the historic, water-powered cider mill where you can indulge in freshly pressed apple cider, craft beverages and artisanal products. Visit the expansive Mill Store Marketplace loaded with gourmet specialty foods including extra-sharp New York Cheddar, Mill-made fudge, salsas and barbeque sauces. The Tasting Room offers flights of ciders, wines, spirits and craft beers overlooking the tranquil Millpond. Savor the flavors of Cooperstown at the on-site restaurant, where farm-fresh pot roast sandwiches and mac & cheese take center stage. More than just a destination, the Mill embodies the essence of Cooperstown - a blend of natural beauty, rich history, and warm hospitality. Whether you're a local resident or a visitor you are invited to taste, tour and explore the best that Cooperstown has to offer at the Fly Creek Cider Mill.

name: Glasgow Christmas Markets
description:
Today we visited Glasgow Christmas Market after visiting Edinburgh Christmas Market which we have attended many times over the years. We were so excited to visit Glasgow as it looked and sounded fantastic. We took our little dog with us who wore her little reindeer hat and so many people stopped to stroke her and take photo's. Everyone was very friendly. 

We thought the town centre looked lovely, very clean and tidy. Lots of beautiful old buildings. We visited both the Christmas markets but to be honest we were very disappointed with both. There were to many food stalls and not enough craft/gift stalls which was a shame. We don't have children so for us all the fair rides were a little boring for us walking round but it was nice to see their happy faces. We only spent a few hours in Glasgow and only purchased an over priced Glasgow fridge magnet at £10. Glad we visited but would not return to the Christmas market again sorry.

name: Alton Hauntings Tours
description: Looking for the real story of why Alton, Illinois, is know as one of the most haunted small towns in America? Come along on one of the award-winning Alton Hauntings Tours! Based on the book by author Troy Taylor, it has been called the "most authentic" tour in the region and after almost 20 years, we take you behind the scenes of the most haunted places in town. According to legend, author Mark Twain once called Alton a "dismal little river town," largely thanks to the dark history that the city had already endured prior to its heyday as a thriving river port. From those days, through the early 1900s, Alton saw more than its share of death, disease, disaster, violence, murder, and even the scars of the Civil War. Today, come see how the events of the past have created the hauntings of what is now being called "one of the most haunted small towns in America." Our tour is an entertaining, often spine-tingling trip back in town to discover the true story of why our little town has become so haunted over the years! See the calendar for upcoming dates and join us on the eerie streets for Alton for a tour!

name: Garner State Park
description:
It’s a pretty drive getting to the park, kind of a rollercoaster at times with all the hills and curves. Old Baldy Trail is a short trail, about half mile, but feels way longer as it’s very steep and rocky. Along the way you can get a bird’s-eye view of the Frio River canyon. The last part of the trail gets steeper and more difficult but at the summit you are rewarded with 360 views of the whole area. It’s a fun hike, but challenging, and watch for loose rocks. 
White Rock Cave Trail leads to part of the Bridges Trail which ultimately leads to the Crystal Cave Trail. It is a couple of miles with some very steep and rocky parts. Some areas were very challenging due to the steepness of the trails. The panoramic views and scenery along the way make up for the hard trek. There are also caves along the way to explore. 
Lots to do and explore in the day use campgrounds and Frio River area. It’s a nice park with several hiking trails, including a leisurely half mile nature trail. There are outdoor things to do and plenty of spots to camp out for a day. It can be as relaxing or as extreme as you want.

name: Valley Shepherd Creamery
description: For all the critics complaining about the "cheap" experience that is "expensive", please keep in mind the Creamery is a family artisan cheese business started by a couple who risked everything to do something amazing when no one else was.  There is an actual cheese cave, built by the owners, and it is the most incredible cheese you will ever experience. I take every single guest to New Jersey of mine to the cheese shop. When the season allows, we take the tour. In the fall, we take our picnic basket with a bottle of wine, buy bread, cheese, sausage, and then go to the apple orchard nearby for apples and other goodies, and find a spot to picnic either on the orchard or a nearby creek. Give a small family business a break, people, this is back-breaking 24/7 work for approximately 20 years.  I only buy cheese at the Creamery (it's REAL goat and sheep cheese!), or when I'm eating my way through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx where I get my Italian cheeses. It is worth the price. The animals are shepherded into a merry-go-round they designed and had shipped in pieces from Italy, and they are doing what they love, which is RARE. I often ship boxes or stock up my suitcase to take to my family. One time the staff even packed my order and left it for me to pick up after hours so I could make my flight. The first time I stumbled upon the Creamery I was driving by and thought I was in England because the sheep were in the the roadside pasture.  Sometimes the animals are there for your viewing, or petting at the fence - just like at the Zoo when you can't see the animal you most expected - do you criticize the Zookeeper for not giving you what you paid for? I am your biggest cheerleader, Valley Shepherd Creamery!

description: The cruise itself was quite nice.However, we had a major problem as the speakers were incredibly loud, especially damaging was the vocal volume.The singing itself was quite nice, but the volume was ear piercing, at dangerous levels. It was extremely uncomfortable for myself my wife and her parents.I reported the issue to the staff not once not twice, but three times. They said they would do something about it, but they did not. We had to cover our ears to protect them, but unfortunately the damage was done.My wife had severe ear pain for the next 3 days and my ear was also quite sore for a few hours after leaving the vessel.I reported the issue to the captain and his staff .Although I am a foreigner here in Vietnam, I speak fluent Vietnamese so communciation was not an issue.. I also mentioned it to the singer, I told her the music was excellent, but the volume was dangerously loud.She laughed and thought it was funny as did the other members of staff.I then called the company the next day to report the issue in order to protect future customers and they basically ignored my report.Two weeks later. I contacted them again and they denied that it was possible for someone's hearing to be damaged by high volume on speakers.I have worked with sound for over 20 years and it is certainly possible (common knowledge in fact).It is not safe to play music at this volume particularly when live vocals are involved.It's a shame because the cruise has a lot of potential but I would strongly warn against going on this Cruise unless you bring ear protection.Very disappointing.Saigon is lovely though as his Vietnam. I've lived here for 8 years and love it.

description:

The check in process was simple and easy, I scanned a QR code and collected my boarding pass (which doubled as my room key) as well as two tickets, one for a restaurant and one for a bus transfer at Stockholm. 

I paid for an A suite with a sea view, however the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the suite itself is quite dated. I tried to move one of the beds to make a double bed but the wall and the floor under the bed were dirty so I decided against that. This was disappointing as the suite was one of the more expensive options.

The ship itself departed and arrived on time and the facilities on board were great otherwise. Another reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that wifi is only available in the COMMON AREAS of the ship and not in the suites (unless you pay for the very expensive suites).

name: Löyly Sauna
description:
After researching extensively, Loyly was heavily suggested, and it was one of the few saunas which were open on Monday and allowed mixed genders, so we decided to book before we came to Helsinki.
We booked our slot from 20:00-22:00, we arrived just before 20:00 and were served by two friendly ladies who explained where everything was and handed us our towels and locker keys. The locker rooms are unbelievably small given the number of lockers they have, so it’s slightly difficult to navigate getting changed and getting to your locker when there’s a few people in there. I dread to think what it’s like on the weekend!
There were only two saunas open instead of three but after reading the reviews this seems to be a common occurrence. The two saunas which were open were decent but for the size of the establishment and how busy it can get, I was expecting bigger saunas as even we noticed that sometimes they were both full. Beware some people (guessing they’re locals) will come in and pour water over the rocks without asking, this didn’t bother me because I have a high tolerance to heat; but if you don’t, be prepared to move out quickly.
There are communal showers with hot and cold water available. There’s a jetty with two rails which take you directly to the Baltic Sea. The water is very shallow with large, sharp rocks, so make sure you don’t run and jump in! It’s nice that the sauna is separate from the restaurant and outdoor dining area as I would’ve felt uncomfortable wandering around half naked whilst people were eating. I’d suggest bringing another towel with you, as we found after getting in the water we’d use the towels to dry off, but when we went to shower then get changed, the towels were still wet.
They have multiple seating inside and out if you fancy a break from the heat. They also have a log fire with comfy sofas and tap water available to keep you hydrated. You also have the option to set up a tab, if you’d like to have any soft or alcohol drinks.
Overall, a brilliant experience to immerse yourself into the finish culture. Slightly let down that only two saunas were available and that the locker rooms were very small.

name: German Village
description: A highway bridge over Interstate 70 is all that separates the German Village Historic District from downtown Columbus, but as one looks east from the interstate, the difference between old and new is glaring. A 20+ story structure sits just north of the interstate bridge, and just south, in German Village, no structure is higher than three stories. Five blocks south, the spire of St. Mary Church stands 197’ off the sidewalk and towers over everything around it. Structures and sidewalks are orange masonry, and many streets (about half) are still brick pavers. German Village does not have a recreated sense of history or kitschy Bavarian feel ~ rather, it is a neighborhood with architecture dating from the 1840s-1890s that has been preserved, and its use as a shared residential and commercial neighborhood has been maintained. People walk to their destinations, park on the street due to the overwhelming absence of driveways, and live life at a very pedestrian level. The neighborhood is extremely dense ~ very often only inches separate neighboring structures, and many structures were built for multi-family use. German Village is notably different because its appearance has changed so little.

name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
description:
21st Feb 25
There's a small parking area and a few vendors selling drinks etc,.you can even rent shoes.
After paying 20k kip to join the trail, the challenge begins,it is not a hike,. it's a climb, scramble or as someone wrote bouldering. We arrived about 3:45 and there were a few people coming down but I found the trail less busy than expected. It's mainly narrow and sheltered within the trees so passing people can be tricky as there isnt many places to stop. Don't wear flipflops, wear trainers or hiking boots, expect to get dusty and dirty and you will use your hands a lot as you scramble. Some of the stepping requires flexibility and stamina, some people will definitely not be able to do this. At the top there is a rest area and of course the 2 motorbikes, getting onto them is not for the feint hearted.  We were at the top about 4:20 and there was a small cheerful crowd waiting turns to get "the photograph". I can imagine some groups of people would hog this photo op.with endless poses and retakes. When we headed down definitely lot more people coming up, perhaps in readiness for sunset, large groups would make it difficult if not dangerous as there is limited safe space to stand.  Getting down feels more difficult and there is a real danger of slipping or sliding and being injured.

Review of KLCC Park

KLCC Park is a beautiful urban oasis in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, perfect for a relaxing stroll or a break from the city’s hustle. The park is well-maintained, with lush greenery, scenic walking paths, and a fantastic view of the iconic Petronas Towers.

name: Turtle Conservation Center
description: The Turtle Rescue and Rehabilitation Center or Phang Nga Coastal Fisheries Research and Development Center (PCFRDC), Thai name ศูนย์วิจัยและพัฒนาประมงชายฝั่งพังงา is located in the city of Thai Mueang (30 minutes drive from Phuket from the exit to the mainland in Phang Nga from the Sarasin Bridge). The center breeds turtles and releases adult individuals into the wild.The territory of this center is quite large, there are 6 large covered pavilions, marked with the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, on which there are concrete vessels with taps from which sea water is poured as needed (the location next to the beach of Tai Muang allows you not to limit yourself in sea water, which is very convenient). In appearance, the vats for turtles do not look glamorous, of course, but the contents of these concrete boxes are amazing and diverse, this is definitely worth seeing for everyone interested in marine fauna. There are practically no people on the territory, we walked around several pavilions, an exhibition and pools with fish, only near the turtles we met a group of volunteers. One of them spoke English quite well (the guy graduated from the economics faculty and came to the center for the rescue of turtles to volunteer), he told us about the center. Entrance to the territory is free.The rehabilitation center in halls A and B houses clownfish, jellyfish, sea urchins and young turtles (it turns out there are as many as 28 species of clownfish, 11 of which are bred at the PCFRDC). The fish reproduce well even in captivity, they are actually fed with plankton grown especially for them, and then sold to other aquariums and oceanariums throughout Thailand. Further on there is a section where you can see rescued, but already injured turtles - both green and olive, which are unlikely to be able to live in normal marine conditions. Young turtles become prey for various predators, ready to bite off their back leg or a piece of shell. Plus, fishermen with their nets and chains also add to the sad statistics in the number of injured beauties.The turtles at the rehabilitation center have been provided with conditions for laying eggs (there is a special white sand area where they can crawl out and bury their eggs).Turtles are very beautiful!

name: Mystery Spot
description: The Mystery Spot is a gravitational anomaly located in the redwood forests just outside of Santa Cruz, California. It is a circular area of effect around 150 feet or 46 meters in diameter. Within the Mystery Spot you will be stunned as your perceptions of the laws of physics and gravity are questioned. But don't take our word for it, come and decide for yourself! The Mystery Spot was discovered in 1939 by a group of surveyors and opened to the public in 1940. The Mystery Spot has amazed and perplexed hundreds of thousands of visitors from all over the world, and many return time and time again to experience these puzzling variations of gravity, perspective, and height. Some speculate that cones of metal were secretly brought here and buried in our earth as guidance systems for their spacecraft. Some think that it is in fact the spacecraft itself buried deep within the ground. Other theories include carbon dioxide permeating from the earth, a hole in the ozone layer, a magma vortex, the highest dielectric biocosmic radiation known anywhere in the world, and radiesthesia. Whatever the cause is, it remains a mystery.

name: Hug Point State Park
description:
As a photographer and filmmaker from the East Coast, I’ve seen my fair share of breathtaking landscapes, but nothing could have prepared me for the sheer magnificence of Oregon’s coast. My recent trip to Hug Point State Park and Cannon Beach left me completely in awe—the natural beauty, the light, and the atmosphere were unlike anything I had ever experienced.

I was visiting an old high school friend, and after a long, rewarding hike through Arch Cape with his dog, we decided to head down to the beach, cooler full of IPAs in hand, and settle in for what would become one of the most unforgettable evenings of my life.

The beach was vast, pristine, and lively—filled with beachgoers soaking up the warm glow of an Indian summer day in the fall. There was a bonfire crackling in the distance, kids running along the shore, and couples walking hand in hand as the sun began to dip toward the horizon.

And then came the sunset—a masterpiece in real-time. I have never seen colors so rich, so surreal, stretching across the sky and reflecting off the ocean like liquid fire. It was the kind of scene that makes you forget everything else and just exist in the moment.

This trip also gave me the perfect chance to test out my new Canon R6 mirrorless camera, and it delivered in ways I couldn’t have imagined. Every shot—whether of the waves crashing against the cliffs, the silhouettes of beachgoers against the golden sky, or the raw joy of my friend’s dog chasing the tide—became a slice-of-life masterpiece.

If you’ve never been to Hug Point or Cannon Beach, do yourself a favor and go. Whether you’re a photographer, nature lover, or just someone seeking a place that feels truly magical, this part of Oregon will blow your mind. I came expecting a beautiful beach—I left with an experience I’ll never forget.

Highly, highly recommended.

name: Grand Casino Beograd
description: The entry staff is pretty friendly, and there are no complications on the passport check-in, they have certain countries that they allow the IDs of, but for the rest, they need passports as it's in Serbia's Government Law to have a database of people gambling from other countries (probably if you win big, but I don't think it's the case).Overall the casino looks pretty nice, nothing too crazy but for an Easter European Casino, it's pretty decent. Smoking is indeed allowed inside so if you are a non-smoker you might be a little bit uncomfortable but it's not anything too crazy (I don't smoke and wasn't that affected by it).You have the first floor with slot machines and some electric roulette for those who don't want to play Live Games, you don't have a wide variety of games on these machines and some might be a little low to mid-grade (they don't have those top-of-the-line slot machines). They advertise that they have smaller tables on their website (500 RSD) but you will only see the 1000RSD+ being opened (even on busy nights) with no side bets.The dealers are content, neither friendly nor rude, they feel like they are just trying to do their job and nothing else, which isn't something surprising to be fair.Soft drinks are on the house if they see you play and you have a selection of drinks that they offer for free but you need a waiter to come to you while sitting at a machine/table, all the drinks requested at the bar/restaurant are charged.Roulette follows the same principle, the smallest table opened is 1000 outside and 100 inside.You have exchange offices inside the casino and ATMs (however the "trusted" bank ones don't work and they only have the kind that takes a pretty big amount of tax per withdrawal.)All in all, it's worth it for the "rookie" experience, I wouldn't consider it a casino I would usually go to even if I lived in the area as it seems like they did all they could to increase the house odds, so if you are in it only for the heck of it - go ahead.

name: Hopkinton State Park
description: Had a lovely Sunday here, it was a perfect halfway meet up spot. The Main beach was closed, making the upper beach area more crowded. People set up to spend all day here. There are charcoal grills at the picnic tables. Lifeguards monitoring the swimming area, however the swimming area was very small. You can rent kayaks not too far away, although not familiar on the price. We bought our own paddleboards and there are several inlets along the water to load/unload the paddleboards.The beach area was crowded and all the picnic tables in this area was taken so we didn’t get a chance to take advantage of those but that’s ok we spent most of the day out on the water and then a short walk around the area. There seems to be quite a few hiking trail options as well, something to consider another time.Parking for out of state residents is $30!! Which is a lot, MA residents only $8 for all day parking.

name: Green Grotto Caves
description: We got here when they first opened due to being on an excursion booked locally instead of through the cruise ship and as a result only had our family and one other in the group. While on the tour the shop tour arrived with 40 people, would not recommend seeing the caves that way. Our guide was Chedd and he was great. He made sure to interact with the kids in our family and the other. He gave them each turns to be the leader and made sure to engage them when imparting his knowledge of the caves. The caves have a lot of openings to the outside along the way so they are not cool like caves that go deep into the earth and as a result if it hot and muggy outside it will be less hot but still muggy in the caves. The history and the restoration they are doing is great and the kids will have a good time while on the visit. Overall this is a great excursion from the cruise ship.

name: Shin Lim: LIMITLESS
description: Shin Lim, the Canadian-born, American-raised Asian-Pacific magician who stunned viewers on “America’s Got Talent,” has attracted nearly 1 million fans across more than 800 shows with no signs of slowing down as he reimagines his Las Vegas residency at his new home at The Palazzo Theatre at The Venetian Resort Las Vegas. Shin Lim has redefined the way close-up magic is presented by performing carefully self-choreographed routines. CBS Sunday Morning notes he is “one of the most astonishing illusionists ever, with dexterity that has earned him accolades from such legends as Penn & Teller,” and James Patterson notes in his new book, “What Really Happens In Vegas,” Lim is “the new superstar of Las Vegas magicians.” “We’re honored to move Limitless to the larger and newly renovated Palazzo Theatre and to have an opportunity to build a new set after so many amazing years getting to entertain fans at The Mirage,” Lim shares proudly.

name: Horseshoe Bend
description: This horseshoe-shaped incised meander of the Colorado River is just a short hike from the beginning of Grand Canyon National Park. The overlook point, which can be accessed via the town of Page, is particularly popular during sunset when the landscape is at its most vibrant, and the iconic turquoise bend glows against the orange cliffs. Although the desert hike is relatively easy, you won’t encounter much shade, so be sure to bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. To maximize your time here, join a tour that includes other picturesque sights like Glen Canyon Dam and Antelope Canyon.

name: Miami Riverwalk Trail
description: Miami has one of the best urban walks of any city.  In addition to the river, you can continue to walk along long sections of Biscayne Bay in the Brickell district.  I had the opportunity to walk here twice in the morning and see 2 incredible sunrises.We visited in March just after the time sprung forward so sunrise was around 7:30AM. From our hotel in Brickell district, we were easily able to reach the Bay before sunrise and have an incredible walk.  In addition to the walk along the bay and river, there are several parks that have other features as well as lots of public art.  The walk along the bay in Brickell south of the river is approximately 1.25 miles with most of that on the water.  The walk to Bayfront Park north of the river is nearly 0.75 miles with most of that walk also on the water.The views of the bay, the skyscrapers and the marine activity both natural and man-made is amazing and an attraction itself.  In fact, this is one of my favorite activities from our time in Miami.  At some point during your stay, you need to walk the waterfront of Miami.  It is truly beautiful, maybe the most beautiful of any city.

description: Commonly known as “the Village” to New Yorkers, it was here in Greenwich Village that both 1960’s counter culture and the LGBT movement were born. Famous for its bohemian past, head to Washington Square Park to get a feel for this diverse and energetic neighborhood. You’ll find NYU students, street performers, skateboarders, kids frolicking in the fountain, and locals relaxing and playing chess. Stroll the streets to discover a mix of majestic town homes and hidden bars and restaurants that give this neighborhood an old-school residential feel. When the sun goes down, check out one of the famous jazz or comedy clubs that still packs them in every night.

name: Mamutik Island
description:
The island is very pretty and could be even more so if it was run better. Unfortunately, every day hordes of rowdy Chinese tourists arrive who unfortunately are not very polite and often leave rubbish lying around. Moreover, most of them, barely afloat, jump unconsciously into the sea with lifebuoys and often to rest they stand on corals.
Apart from that you can find nice and quiet corners, away from the pier.
The seabed is rather gray and has a damaged coral reef but nevertheless snorkeling is still pleasant; I found angelfish, parrot, crossbow, trumpet, staff sergeants, a sea snake, small moray eels, many anemones with clownfish and others.
The island can be reached in about 20 minutes from Jesselton Pier with the ferry service that departs continuously; the boats are a little run down and run a lot, Recommendation to ask to decrease the speed. Look at the weather forecast because in the afternoon it often rains and in ten minutes heavy thunderstorms arrive with which it is not pleasant to go to sea to return to KK.

name: Playa Lagun
description: When searching for beaches be aware that the bigger ones are usually very busy and have restrictions on chair use, etc. The quieter beaches are farther west on the island but are situated in coves and therefore quite small. These can be busy as well depending on the time of day.

name: Mahogany Beach
description:
Mahogany Beach is a great place to watch the day go by. It's a beautifully tranquil beach. There is a small fee to enter, but it is a small price to pay for such a well staffed beach. 

On the site, there is a gift shop and regular stalls for the locals to sell their crafts and wares. The bar serves full food, and the drinks are well stocked. The staff are friendly and happy to accommodate off menu cocktails. There is plenty of seating located throughout the beach.

The sea bed is a bit rocky in places, but the sand is soft underfoot everywhere else. Apparently, there are mineral pockets in the sea, so be prepared to experience warm spots throughout the area.
 
I don't know if you can still access it, but there is a little entrance to the side of the cave where you can have a nice adventurous climb back up to the road.

What's great about this beach is that you can enjoy a full day here. You can turn up and spend the day just lounging or you can hop on a catamaran trip or participate in the many watersports  (subject to booking availability) or you could just enjoy full access to the beach.

What's not so great, the resident dog family. They are so sweet and passive, but I'm just not a fan. Despite this, I enjoy this beach so much that I'm going to let that one slide.

Our seal couple are some of the most romantic animals you will see. They love to display their affection for each other and meet new people, too. name: Quay Street
description:
I would never stop walking back and forth along this street, the beating heart of the city: here you can breathe the real Ireland, the one that speaks Gaelic (when it goes from the countryside to the city) and that sings stories of emigration, of cows, of sheep and green.
Very colourful, full of pubs and enriched by the goldsmiths of the famous Claddagh ring and the Aran knitwear shops: it is not a place for nightlife because life shuts down - except for a handful of clubs - no later than 11pm.
But truly a delightful place!

name: Klondike Park
description: We rented out all 6 cabins as well as some of the campsites for a group camping trip with friends. I had a hard time finding much info on the cabins, so I thought I would share what I can.  Based on the park map I chose cabin B for myself as it appears to be very close to the showerhouse/bathrooms.  What the map doesn't show is that cabins are sort of on a bluff and the campsites and bathrooms/showers are located at the bottom of that. In order to reach the bathrooms you must walk through all the cabins and down a set of stairs that is near cabin D. Then walk back the direction you came. Soooo.. if you're like me and want convenient bathroom trips, none of the cabins are close, but cabin D is your best choice.  The cabins themselves were a step above camping in that you don't have to set up a tent, but the beds were a similar level of comfort as sleeping on the ground.  All 6 cabins had hundreds of stinkbugs inside of them when we arrived.  That didn't bother me a huge amount as I expect to encounter bugs when in nature, but not everyone was so thrilled about it. I loved how the cabins were grouped together since we had rented them all to spend time with friends, but if you're looking for a secluded spot, this is probably not for you. We had a great time, but I'm not sure this is someplace we will stay again.

name: Mauna Kea Oceanfront Luau
description: The setting is on a beautiful resort. Entry was supposed to be at 5:10 however it wasn’t until 5:30 when guests started getting checked in. We paid for general seating so we received a black lei (premium seating got white leis) and our mai tai. Once everyone was seated the premium guests received some chips and dip. Then we were invited to get up and walk over to the pit with the pig yo watch the pig get unearthed. Then we were invited to plate up. The food was very good. While we’re eating the show started. Which was a good show. I would conclude this by saying I wouldn’t recommend this luau due to the price and what is (isn’t) included. I think adding maybe some activities and a memorabilia like a glass to take home would make it worth it to me.

name: De'Ricci Cantine Storiche
description:
We started our tour at the vineyard just outside of Montepulciano, we were welcome by Fred who explained the history of the winery with a very pleasant manner. We were then introduced to the table where we sat for a fabulous lunch of simple but delicious food coupled with what should have been 4 wines but ended up being 5. During our tasting Fred explained with great passion each wine, he is very knowledgeable and loves his job.
 
We were also introduced to the owner’s son who was very humble and had a nice way about him.
 
After lunch we visited the cellars in Montepulciano where again Fred explained in great depth the history of the building followed by another 2 tastings. After the tour finished with sat with Fred at a local bar and share more wine and stories with him. We have done a lot of wine tastings and this is the best one in terms of explaining the wines and giving the whole experience.

This glittering neighborhood boasts some of the world's most opulent casinos, luxury hotels, and awe-inspiring performances, all spread along a 4-mile stretch. The iconic Bellagio Fountains, the Eiffel Tower at Paris Las Vegas, and the High Roller Ferris Wheel are among the captivating landmarks that dot the skyline. Food lovers can relish a diverse range of culinary experiences, from high-end dining at restaurants run by celebrity chefs to casual eateries. With an efficient monorail system and abundant taxis, navigating The Strip is a breeze for visitors.

You can also take a dip into the turquoise waters (but not before wearing a life vest) and marvel at the beautiful stalactites hanging from the ceiling. Get there early in the day to beat the crowds. name: Rail Bike Adventures
description: Watch where you are going.  I ran right into the bike in front of us.  PSA, taking pictures while being the person on the break is not a good idea.  Don’t worry, everyone was ok.My wife, 10 year old daughter, and I went and had an enjoyable time.  The views are pretty and it is really cool going over the bridge just for trains.  Great views of the lake and lots of trees.  Though, I am not sure what the future holds as there is a subdivision going up right along the path.  I guess it will be ok, but being out on the trail without seeing the houses is enjoyable.It is an out and back trip.  They turn the bikes around at the end of the trip and you get about 10 minutes rest.  There are benches.  There are no bathrooms at the turn around point.  I honestly felt the ride back was faster than the ride there.  Likely fear of unknown.I felt this was a fun activity but might be better with a kid that can reach the peddles.   Our daughter certainly met the 48 inch height minimum but if felt like she could not really peddle.  It could be another child at same height could.  That meant my wife and I were peddling the three of us on a 4 person bike.  Our legs were tired at the end.  Don’t not go and try, it is worth it, but just wanted you to know that some kids might not be able to reach the peddles.  The front seats can reach closer to the peddles than the back seats.  The front right rider has control of the hand break.The staff had excellent communication between the station and each other as they approached intersections.  Even when the active train car was at the station, there was great communication so everyone knew we were approaching the station.  There did not seem any risk that an active train could be on our track, but you can feel good that the people supervising us were trained, knowledgeable and formal with their communication.  They were not goof offs.The give good instructions, but it is hard to hear them if you are in the last bike like we were.  There is a single restroom at the station so come a little early.  Plus you will need to complete the waiver.  At the end of the ride, they spray each seat with disinfectant.   Cool.We very much enjoyed the activity.  We are in good shape, but our legs were tired at the end.  Enjoy.
