Plus, you can enjoy the hotel’s premium amenities, including a Spa, Swimming Pool, and Fitness Club, for the ultimate relaxation and entertainment experience.

name: Henna Art By Kim
description: PLEASE MAKE AN APPOINTMENT before you come! Henna Tattoo Service - Whilst you are visiting Saigon, experience the true Henna Art experience. In modern culture, henna art is treated as just another form of body art, a fashionable, temporary tattoo which will fade... But henna art is about so much more. Henna has been used since antiquity to dye skin, hair and fingernails, as well as fabrics including silk, wood and leather. Henna art tells the story of thousands of years of Indian culture and its use spread wide across the world to Arabia, North Africa and South East Asia along the old spice trade routes. Through my store I look to continue to spread the messages behind the art. At Henna Art by Kim, I only do traditional henna designs using natural henna dye. I have a true passion in sharing the culture and messages of henna art. Nothing makes me happier then spreading these messages and seeing the joy that comes through people wearing my bespoke artwork, whether this is for a special occasion, such as in traditional bridal art or for a festival, or in day to day wearing and enjoyment of the artform. Whilst the art is only temporary, I hope that the messages will last a lot longer. I look forward to meeting and sharing this with you soon too!

name: The Observatory
description: The Observatory is a nightclub focusing on electronic music and a rooftop lounge and bar. It is located at the 10th floor of 85 Cách Mạng Tháng 8, District 1. Hosting a large range of both international and local acts, from DJs to live electronic musicians and bands, it's a place to enjoy the power of sound and music. To this we added a rooftop lounge, an exclusive view on the Saigon skyline, cocktails, wine and more to come. Stay tuned.

name: Yello Vietnam Travel
description: I booked our tour with the Yello vietnam tour agency and I have to say, they were informal, patient and made our safety come first. Our tour guide was really professional and gave detailed information about every Location we visited. The lunch at the end of the tour felt like fine dining at an open restaurant to the Mekong delta and nature. I will definitely recommend this tour with this agency to friends and family and especially for those who are seeking to explore the beauty of Vietnam!

name: Lush
description: Lush is one of the longest running nightlife establishments in Ho Chi Minh City, opening it's doors to the public on June 15, 2004. It's always played a leading role in the Saigon nightlife culture, having hosted some the best local, international DJs, and other talents and being frequented by the top trendsetters of the country.

name: Tori Spa
description: Hi, I’m Matt, the owner of Tori Spa. I created my spa for gay men so you could enjoy a relaxing environment and have a brief respite from the hustle and bustle outside. Located in a secluded and peaceful lane in the heart of Hanoi’s famous Old Quarter and near Saigon’s famous Bui Vien Street, Tori Spa Hanoi and Tori Spa Saigon are the perfect places to relax and rejuvenate. Our trained male therapists provide friendly and professional services for men who want to look great and feel healthy. We look forward to welcoming you at Tori Spa soon.​All the best, Matt

name: VINBACCO - Wine With A Story
description: A cozy wine bar and store with city views in the heart of Saigon's district 1. Sharing exclusive, high-quality Italian wines with Vietnam. VINBACCO - Wine With A Story is Tucked away on the third floor of the Catinat building. Constructed between 1926 and 1927 for the Société Urbaine Foncière Indochinoise (SUFIC) and is located at the intersection of Dong Khoi and Ly Tu Trong (opposite Vincom Center). We can't wait for you to try our 32 hand-selected premium bottles of wine from one of the five different Italian regions we source from, all of which have either IGT, DOC, or DOCG classification.

name: Truc Lam Tailor
description: I’ve just had three linen shortsleeved shirts made here and I’m very pleased with the results.I took in a shirt I really like and asked for it to be copied x 3. I chose three separate linen fabrics (linen is a great fabric to wear in the SE Asia climate) and paid a deposit. The shirts were ready 36 hours later and are a perfect fit and so well made. Total cost was approx £50 which I thought very reasonable for the quality and fast turnaround.Truc did an excellent job and I will definitely visit her again the next time I visit HCMC.

name: Cu Chi Tunnels
description: On your guided tour of the Cu Chi Tunnels, you’ll learn about the history of this underground system. The tunnels were dug during the Vietnam War by Viet Cong soldiers as a way to move undetected and launch surprise attacks. Experience the tight squeeze firsthand by crawling through the tunnels, and fire assault rifles at the shooting range after. Pack bug spray and dress for hot and humid weather, arriving earlier in the day to beat the crowds and the afternoon sun. It's not recommended to visit the tunnels after a downpour, as the area will get very muddy.

name: Bui Vien Street
description: Head to Bui Vien Street for a wild night out along one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most iconic streets. Also known by locals as the “Backpacker District” or “Western Street” for its popularity amongst travelers, this street is lined with tons of bars, restaurants, coffee shops and street food stalls that beckon with their flashing lights, thumping music and fragrant aromas of Vietnamese cuisine. It'll be daybreak before you know it. Sign up for a night tour of Ho Chi Minh, which often includes a stop at Bui Vien Street and nightlife spots in Saigon. – Tripadvisor

name: Central Post Office
description: This post office also houses a useful office center with phones and fax lines.

name: War Remnants Museum
description: War Remnants Museum is a unit under the Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism Ho Chi Minh City. Located in the museum system of Vietnam, the museum for world peace and a member of the World Council of Museums (ICOM), the War Remnants Museum, the Museum of thematic research, collection , storage, preservation and display of the material, photographs, artifacts on the evidence of the crime and the consequences of the war that the invasion force has caused to Vietnam.Museum store more than 20,000 documents, exhibits and films, in which more than 1,500 documents, artifacts, films have been applied to introduce in eight thematic exhibition frequently. In 35 years, the Museum has welcomed over 15 million visitors at home and abroad. Currently with about 500,000 visitors each year, the War Remnants Museum is one of the only cultural tourism to attract high public credibility at home and abroad.

name: Bitexco Financial Tower
description: Bitexco Financial Tower at a height of 262 meters is the tallest building in Ho Chi Minh City up to date. With design concept is taken from the shape of a lotus bud, the Vietnam national flower, Bitexco Financial Tower is not merely a building which is covered in glass and steel, but also a symbol of beauty and the rapid development of Ho Chi Minh City economy, a key economic region in Vietnam. Bitexco Financial Tower is a typical example for creativity and unique design. One of the tower highlights is the first observation in the city at 49th floors. Saigon Skydeck has opened for all visitors from January 1, 2011. With a full range of services and facilities for visitors, the Skydeck has officially opened to welcome visitors both domestic and international visitors since July, 2011. Visitors have the opportunity to visit Saigon Skydeck, not only enjoy the full sight of the Ho Chi Minh City and Saigon River, but also have the chance to use the facilities and services at this Skydeck. With many activities will be held at the Skydeck during this year, with special offer prices for different customer groups, the Skydeck will be an attractive destination in the journey of Ho Chi Minh City's for both domestic and international tourists.

name: A O Show - Lune Production
description: À Ố Show is one of Vietnamese Bamboo Circus performances. À Ố - derives from Làng Phố, which means ‘village and city’. À Ố Show tells a captivating story of the transition from the peaceful life of the countryside to the fast-paced metropolitan life of modern Southern Vietnam. The soul of village life and, in stark contrast, familiar scenes from the city, are beautifully brought to life -- with bamboo! The stunning simplicity of the bamboo props frames an awe-inspiring circus featuring acrobatics, contortion, juggling, and stunting. Throughout the show, both traditional and modern music harmonize richly, performed live with 17 musical instruments. À Ố Show has become a world-renowned circus, critically acclaimed in 11 countries.

name: Sai Gon Square
description: Quite a polite market. Higher quality goods than usual, but not all. A lot of replica products, but also quite OK quality local fashion clothes. The rooms are air-conditioned and the sellers are not as pushy as in the neighbouring Ben Thanh Market. Some merchants are not willing to negotiate on the price at all, but with some you can even negotiate the price for half the price. As always in such places, you need to know in advance the price of the goods you want to buy or first try to negotiate the price with a couple of merchants and see what price they are willing to sell for. description: There’s lots to see and do here and definitely some unique sites. There are street performers, cafes, interactive exhibits and art in various forms. Visually the surrounding architecture is memorable and includes a unique, well lit 9 floor commercial and cultural complex (42 Nguyen Hue) that has individual lighted stores beckoning you.. Go to the rooftop terrace to see panoramic views. This was a memorable experience, well worth my time there.

name: Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater
description: Generations ago, Vietnamese puppeteers performed for their rural communities in waist-deep water, bringing to life legends and stories about their region. Water puppetry theaters like Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater continue that tradition into the modern day and are a fun, family-friendly way to experience a hallmark of traditional Vietnamese culture.water puppet show, which is closely associated with the spiritual life of Vietnamese people, especially in the countryside. The show’s chosen stage is the surface of a water pool. The puppeteers present their clever skills in managing puppets by long bamboo rods and string mechanism under the surface. A traditional Vietnamese orchestra is an excellent music accompaniment. The puppets depict the story from the songs during the show, which reflects the peaceful life of the Vietnamese countryside, so it is not too difficult to understand it.

name: Ho Chi Minh City's Book Street
description:
Ho Chi Minh Book Street, also known as "Đường Sách Thành Phố Hồ Chí Minh", is a unique destination in downtown Ho Chi Minh City that is a must-visit for book lovers. Located in District 1, near Saigon Central Post Office and Notre-Dame Cathedral, this area combines literary culture with a dynamic city atmosphere.

Book Street has a calm and friendly atmosphere, despite being in the middle of the hustle and bustle of the city. The street is lined with shady trees, providing shade for visitors. There are various modern book stalls that are aesthetically designed, creating a relaxing atmosphere for reading and exploring the book collection. Its strategic location makes it easily accessible to both local and foreign tourists.

Along this street, you will find various bookstores offering a variety of collections. Starting from books in Vietnamese, English, to other languages, are available here. The collections offered include fiction, non-fiction, children's books, to academic books. Some stalls also sell rare books and special editions, making it a collector's paradise.

One of the main attractions is its inspiring atmosphere. This street not only sells books but also celebrates the culture of reading and literacy. There are small book-themed statues and interesting decorations for photo spots. Some stalls also sell literacy merchandise, such as stationery, posters, and souvenirs.

description:
This is a nice and clean shopping centre, has a decent range of shops. The food area located 2 floors below is very good but very busy. You’ve got a very good range of different food places and each place has its own seating area. 

We had food at Mac Donald’s which I have to say is miles better than the UK. The staff here are so much more friendly and customer service is at the forefront. The food in Mac Donald’s again miles better than the UK. It’s all served up fresh and brought to the table hot. The French fries here they know how to fill the box up and bring them to you hot. The fried chicken is excellent and very tasty. Good to see that Mac Donald’s offer this in Vietnam. 

You have to visit Beard Papa’s the cream puffs are AMAZING the best I have tried. The Vanilla cream and Tiramisu Cream is absolutely delicious. 

Overall a good shopping centre with AC and indoors, if you’re looking for a bargain you won’t find it here but you will find some amazing food places.

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

name: Hot Sulphur Springs Resort & Spa
description: I went there yesterday with my 2 kids and my niece. We paid over $100 for 2 adults and 2 minor children, plus an additional $16 for 2 robes. When we stepped out of the front entrance into the outdoor pool area it was disgusting!! The place is falling apart, boards on benches with peeling paint, dusty, dirty corners around each area of the pools. The water inside each of the pools was full of debris and dirt. The women’s locker room was so bad I can’t describe how gross I felt changing there it made me want to throw up. Piles of dirty towels and robes piled up to almost the ceiling!! There were 3 staff members working at the front desk but nobody was checking on the bathrooms. There was no place to put your baggage, the lockers are tiny and so people’s bags were all over the locker room floor, you could barely walk. They do not limit the amount of people at one time so it was very overcrowded and they were not prepared with staff. We left after 30 minutes. Biggest waste of money and I will never be back.

name: Piazza della Signoria
description: This historic plaza is the political heart of the city and home to significant monuments like the Palazzo Vecchio, Loggia dei Lanzi, and Uffizi Gallery.

name: South Carolina Aquarium
description: Discover the wonder of water, wildlife and wild places at the South Carolina Aquarium. Overlooking the Charleston Harbor, the Aquarium connects you with nearly 5,000 amazing animals and learn how you can protect them. Come face-to-face with sick and injured sea turtles in rehabilitation in our Sea Turtle Care Center ™ and follow their journeys from rescue to rehab to release. Visit our two touch tanks for a hands-on experience with stingrays, sharks, horseshoe crabs, sea stars and urchins. Learn fascinating details about the natural world at daily dive shows and animal encounters.

name: Lake Bled
description: Discover the magic of the lake that attracts travellers from near and far. The current unique shape of the year did not emerge coincidentally. A tectonic hole made by the Bohinj glacier through the years, was once at the location of the present lake. Its path was obstructed by a huge rock which was so persistently scraped that the only thing that remained was the present island. The ice melted and the basin was filled with water, thus Lake Bled emerged, which is in some places up to 30 metres deep and quite popular amongst divers. 19 species of fish live in the lake, including carp, sheatfish and lake trout. Ducks and swans as well as diverse plants also swim and thrive on its surface.

name: Ocean Vodka Organic Farm and Distillery
description: Situated on 80-acres of breathtaking views from the slopes of Haleakala, is Ocean Organic Farm and Distillery, the home of Ocean Organic Vodka. Centrally located and an easy drive from Maui’s International Kahului Airport, as well as the island’s world-famous resorts. Come visit us and learn about our company’s commitment to producing some of the worlds finest spirits. Visit our Farm Store where you'll find our full collection of premium spirits and apparel. Then, stop by our Café and take in the stunning bicoastal views while enjoying locally inspired fare along with one of our signature cocktails. The Café also features live music daily starting at 4:30pm. Guided personal tastings are also available. Tastings include the history of Ocean Organic Farm and Distillery, and the unique processes that go into producing our award-winning spirits. Tastings are offered every half hour from 11am to 5pm and include a lineup of 5 of our spirits for $18.

name: Be Happy Museum Warszawa
description: If someone is looking for an atmospheric place to take photos, Be Happy Museum will be a great place. It is not a museum in the classic sense of the word, there are no historical exhibits with descriptions on tablets. It is supposed to be a place where you can take interesting photos in a beautiful setting and I think it fulfills its role 100%. The set design is well-thought-out and works well together, the interior design is something between the world of Barbie and the Pin-up style. Another advantage is good light for photos that actually come out on their own. The staff is very helpful and helps in taking photos, I recommend it :)

name: Wild Horse Adventure Tours
description: Feel the ocean breeze and taste the salty air! See the wild horses of the Outer Banks and whip through beach, dune, and forest trails with Hummer Adventure Tours. Discover some of the most unique sights the Outer Banks has to offer. Our friendly and knowledgeable tour guides take you onto pristine northern beaches that are accessible only with a 4x4 off-road vehicle. With more terrain, no two tours are ever the same; so if you like history, ecology, adventure, and quick-witted comedy, we have you covered.

name: Howth Cliff Walk
description: We started the walk opposite the dart station. I would not recommend doing this as it is a long incline (1 hour of climbing) on a path through the back of housing estates. There’s nothing particularly nice about it. Once you get to the cliffs it is beautiful! However, that beautiful part is quite short (about 20 mins) and then back on the road heading down town again. The town itself is lovely with a nice harbour. We had fish and chips in Beshoffs which was superb. If I was going again I would start the walk by walking from dart station through the pretty town and then up to the cliffs from there. There are signs for the start of each level of walk as you walk past and beyond the harbour. You could do the loop and return down opposite the dart station. Personally, I would just go up to the cliffs from the town and back down again and then walk back to the dart station via the pretty town and of course stopping at Beshoffs for fish and chips.

Take shoes that can get wet and lots of fluid.I would say this is at least moderate as a hike. It took us 3 hours with some time spent in the water.The fall wasn’t that impressive due to the lack of rainfall/water. Although so worth it. The sights on the way are unbelievable and really breathtaking!

name: Megali Petra Beach
description:
Personally it did not seem like the paradise described in the other reviews.

Beautiful sea for goodness sake, but between the inconvenience of access, parking and even services honestly I was not so impressed.

I state that with two small children perhaps it is more complex because the beach being surrounded by rocks has a sea that soon becomes deep and this perhaps affects the review, but the road to the beach is really uncomfortable.
We arrived at 9:30 in the morning and already the parking lots were almost full (10 € full day seems correct to me), on the return with the cars parked even along the narrow return routes it is practically a challenge to pass if in front of you find another car in the opposite direction.

The sea is beautiful, as it is beautiful throughout the island. Maybe for a long holiday it is still worth spending a day there, but really in Lefkada there is much better.

Recommendation to bring water and food to face the day

name: The House of Saigon
description: Saigon - where colors by diverse aspects of both Vietnamese and international culture. Saigon - where bears dynamic & hectic pace of life that time to slow down is desirable. And these are the reasons for The House of Saigon to come in. With great love & pride of Saigon, our mission is to create 360* experience from exploring how Vietnamese handcrafted products creatively 'breath in' traditional-mixed-trendy elements and enjoying local culinary delights under relaxing retro atmosphere. Each product conveys a story about the process of skillful local workmanship making it with care and patience, about geographical origin of natural materials, and about how our Vietnamese and international designers bring creativity and their inspiration to life. name: William Heise County Park
description: For years, I've driven past the turnoff to this park as I was headed to Julian from the Cuyamacas.As I've explored the usual sites & trails in the San Diego backcountry, I thought I've give the park a try.  (Hiking, picnicking, not camping).First, we got our picnic lunch from a alt-health grocery store in Alpine, then drove to the Lagunas, enjoying the scenic highway towards Julian.I spotted the turnoff sign and navigated the slow, winding road, 3-4 miles to the park.  It's longer than I expected, but the distance from the road provides total silence upon reaching the entrance.There's a nominal fee, and the person in the booth will provide a map and directions, if needed.  We parked near the picnic area.  There's a bathroom nearby, at least two.  (Showers, too, for campers).The picnic area is 1-2 minutes away, with benches.Facing the nearby hills, feeling the sun on my shoulders, watching the clouds, it's a gentle reminder why I love San DIego County.

name: Fly Creek Cider Mill & Orchard
description: Fly Creek Cider Mill & Orchard offers a quintessential experience in Cooperstown, NY. Explore the historic, water-powered cider mill where you can indulge in freshly pressed apple cider, craft beverages and artisanal products. Visit the expansive Mill Store Marketplace loaded with gourmet specialty foods including extra-sharp New York Cheddar, Mill-made fudge, salsas and barbeque sauces. The Tasting Room offers flights of ciders, wines, spirits and craft beers overlooking the tranquil Millpond. Savor the flavors of Cooperstown at the on-site restaurant, where farm-fresh pot roast sandwiches and mac & cheese take center stage. More than just a destination, the Mill embodies the essence of Cooperstown - a blend of natural beauty, rich history, and warm hospitality. Whether you're a local resident or a visitor you are invited to taste, tour and explore the best that Cooperstown has to offer at the Fly Creek Cider Mill.

name: Glasgow Christmas Markets
description:
Today we visited Glasgow Christmas Market after visiting Edinburgh Christmas Market which we have attended many times over the years. We were so excited to visit Glasgow as it looked and sounded fantastic. We took our little dog with us who wore her little reindeer hat and so many people stopped to stroke her and take photo's. Everyone was very friendly. 

We thought the town centre looked lovely, very clean and tidy. Lots of beautiful old buildings. We visited both the Christmas markets but to be honest we were very disappointed with both. There were to many food stalls and not enough craft/gift stalls which was a shame. We don't have children so for us all the fair rides were a little boring for us walking round but it was nice to see their happy faces. We only spent a few hours in Glasgow and only purchased an over priced Glasgow fridge magnet at £10. Glad we visited but would not return to the Christmas market again sorry.

There are tennis courts, a small water park/splash pad, picnic areas, a playground, and a small flower garden, so there's something for everyone of all ages.  The playground is accessible for kids of all abilities.  There's plenty of parking and trash cans as well.  The entrance was a bit hard to find at first, as we initially thought that it was just the entrance for the tennis courts, so we had to turn around after passing it.

name: Alton Hauntings Tours
description: Looking for the real story of why Alton, Illinois, is know as one of the most haunted small towns in America? Come along on one of the award-winning Alton Hauntings Tours! Based on the book by author Troy Taylor, it has been called the "most authentic" tour in the region and after almost 20 years, we take you behind the scenes of the most haunted places in town. According to legend, author Mark Twain once called Alton a "dismal little river town," largely thanks to the dark history that the city had already endured prior to its heyday as a thriving river port. From those days, through the early 1900s, Alton saw more than its share of death, disease, disaster, violence, murder, and even the scars of the Civil War. Today, come see how the events of the past have created the hauntings of what is now being called "one of the most haunted small towns in America." Our tour is an entertaining, often spine-tingling trip back in town to discover the true story of why our little town has become so haunted over the years! See the calendar for upcoming dates and join us on the eerie streets for Alton for a tour!

There are also plenty of restaurants, bars, vegetarian eateries, and shopping centers near Shinrin. Super convenient—you won’t have to go far for anything, hahaha. Give it a try, it’s totally worth it!

name: Garner State Park
description:
It’s a pretty drive getting to the park, kind of a rollercoaster at times with all the hills and curves. Old Baldy Trail is a short trail, about half mile, but feels way longer as it’s very steep and rocky. Along the way you can get a bird’s-eye view of the Frio River canyon. The last part of the trail gets steeper and more difficult but at the summit you are rewarded with 360 views of the whole area. It’s a fun hike, but challenging, and watch for loose rocks. 
White Rock Cave Trail leads to part of the Bridges Trail which ultimately leads to the Crystal Cave Trail. It is a couple of miles with some very steep and rocky parts. Some areas were very challenging due to the steepness of the trails. The panoramic views and scenery along the way make up for the hard trek. There are also caves along the way to explore. 
Lots to do and explore in the day use campgrounds and Frio River area. It’s a nice park with several hiking trails, including a leisurely half mile nature trail. There are outdoor things to do and plenty of spots to camp out for a day. It can be as relaxing or as extreme as you want.

name: Valley Shepherd Creamery
description: For all the critics complaining about the "cheap" experience that is "expensive", please keep in mind the Creamery is a family artisan cheese business started by a couple who risked everything to do something amazing when no one else was.  There is an actual cheese cave, built by the owners, and it is the most incredible cheese you will ever experience. I take every single guest to New Jersey of mine to the cheese shop. When the season allows, we take the tour. In the fall, we take our picnic basket with a bottle of wine, buy bread, cheese, sausage, and then go to the apple orchard nearby for apples and other goodies, and find a spot to picnic either on the orchard or a nearby creek. Give a small family business a break, people, this is back-breaking 24/7 work for approximately 20 years.  I only buy cheese at the Creamery (it's REAL goat and sheep cheese!), or when I'm eating my way through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx where I get my Italian cheeses. It is worth the price. The animals are shepherded into a merry-go-round they designed and had shipped in pieces from Italy, and they are doing what they love, which is RARE. I often ship boxes or stock up my suitcase to take to my family. One time the staff even packed my order and left it for me to pick up after hours so I could make my flight. The first time I stumbled upon the Creamery I was driving by and thought I was in England because the sheep were in the the roadside pasture.  Sometimes the animals are there for your viewing, or petting at the fence - just like at the Zoo when you can't see the animal you most expected - do you criticize the Zookeeper for not giving you what you paid for? I am your biggest cheerleader, Valley Shepherd Creamery!

description: The cruise itself was quite nice.However, we had a major problem as the speakers were incredibly loud, especially damaging was the vocal volume.The singing itself was quite nice, but the volume was ear piercing, at dangerous levels. It was extremely uncomfortable for myself my wife and her parents.I reported the issue to the staff not once not twice, but three times. They said they would do something about it, but they did not. We had to cover our ears to protect them, but unfortunately the damage was done.My wife had severe ear pain for the next 3 days and my ear was also quite sore for a few hours after leaving the vessel.I reported the issue to the captain and his staff .Although I am a foreigner here in Vietnam, I speak fluent Vietnamese so communciation was not an issue.. I also mentioned it to the singer, I told her the music was excellent, but the volume was dangerously loud.She laughed and thought it was funny as did the other members of staff.I then called the company the next day to report the issue in order to protect future customers and they basically ignored my report.Two weeks later. I contacted them again and they denied that it was possible for someone's hearing to be damaged by high volume on speakers.I have worked with sound for over 20 years and it is certainly possible (common knowledge in fact).It is not safe to play music at this volume particularly when live vocals are involved.It's a shame because the cruise has a lot of potential but I would strongly warn against going on this Cruise unless you bring ear protection.Very disappointing.Saigon is lovely though as his Vietnam. I've lived here for 8 years and love it.

description:

The terminal where the ship departs from Helsinki has a tram stop in front of it which is useful if you need to get there and do not have any transfers or do not want to walk.

The check in process was simple and easy, I scanned a QR code and collected my boarding pass (which doubled as my room key) as well as two tickets, one for a restaurant and one for a bus transfer at Stockholm. 

I paid for an A suite with a sea view, however the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the suite itself is quite dated. I tried to move one of the beds to make a double bed but the wall and the floor under the bed were dirty so I decided against that. This was disappointing as the suite was one of the more expensive options.

The ship itself departed and arrived on time and the facilities on board were great otherwise. Another reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that wifi is only available in the COMMON AREAS of the ship and not in the suites (unless you pay for the very expensive suites).

name: Löyly Sauna
description:
After researching extensively, Loyly was heavily suggested, and it was one of the few saunas which were open on Monday and allowed mixed genders, so we decided to book before we came to Helsinki.
We booked our slot from 20:00-22:00, we arrived just before 20:00 and were served by two friendly ladies who explained where everything was and handed us our towels and locker keys. The locker rooms are unbelievably small given the number of lockers they have, so it’s slightly difficult to navigate getting changed and getting to your locker when there’s a few people in there. I dread to think what it’s like on the weekend!
There were only two saunas open instead of three but after reading the reviews this seems to be a common occurrence. The two saunas which were open were decent but for the size of the establishment and how busy it can get, I was expecting bigger saunas as even we noticed that sometimes they were both full. Beware some people (guessing they’re locals) will come in and pour water over the rocks without asking, this didn’t bother me because I have a high tolerance to heat; but if you don’t, be prepared to move out quickly.
There are communal showers with hot and cold water available. There’s a jetty with two rails which take you directly to the Baltic Sea. The water is very shallow with large, sharp rocks, so make sure you don’t run and jump in! It’s nice that the sauna is separate from the restaurant and outdoor dining area as I would’ve felt uncomfortable wandering around half naked whilst people were eating. I’d suggest bringing another towel with you, as we found after getting in the water we’d use the towels to dry off, but when we went to shower then get changed, the towels were still wet.
They have multiple seating inside and out if you fancy a break from the heat. They also have a log fire with comfy sofas and tap water available to keep you hydrated. You also have the option to set up a tab, if you’d like to have any soft or alcohol drinks.
Overall, a brilliant experience to immerse yourself into the finish culture. Slightly let down that only two saunas were available and that the locker rooms were very small.

The Museum’s encyclopedic collections of nearly 70,000 objects cover world cultures dating from antiquity to the present and include in-depth holdings of American art, European paintings, Pre-Columbian and African gold, decorative arts and design, photography, prints and drawings, 20th- and 21st-century painting and sculpture, and Latin American art.

name: L'Apothiquaire Spa
description: The original L'Apothiquaire branch is ideally situated in the heart of downtown, close to the main hotels and offering the perfect urban sanctuary and spa. Housed in a quaint, lovingly restored century-old French townhouse. L'Apothiquaire features high ceilings, original tiling, an exposed brick wall and wooden stairs. The antique furniture enhances the old world charm which transports you away from the hectic pace of modernity. Upon entering, L'Apothiquaire is a boutique with traditional wooden cabinets - resembling a 17th century French Apothecary. Along the cabinets is an array of the comprehensive range of L'Apothiquaire's beautifully packaged organic body and face oils, scrubs, bath salts, organic soaps and organic herbal blends, from France. An intimate foot-care room overlooks a small courtyard featuring a gargoyle and orchids. Upstairs are seven private & semi-private treatment rooms draped with luxurious, velvet curtains. An elegant suite featuring a private Jacuzzi. Treatments follow the L'Apothiquaire philosophy of using only the finest, natural and organic ingredients to offer a delicate but effective healing process for mind and body. Trained beauty consultants will put you at ease, tailor a treatment to suit your individual needs and recommend an going program to ensure your renewed radiance is maintained. L'Apothiquaire Artisan Beaute opened in 2005 and was voted 'Best Beauty Salon' in the same year. It offers the ultimate in body care and facials, a unique experience not to be missed.

name: Elegant Silk
description:
So far this has been the highlight of our trip to Vietnam!  

Arthur was reluctant to go, but I persuaded him to, on the basis that I wanted my favourite dress copied.  

We walked away five days later with two suits for him, some trousers, shirts and even a tie, cuff-link and pocket square combination that was a gift from them.  

Our only regret is that trying to pack lightly in view of the 10 flights on this trip, he didn’t pack a smart pair of shoes, so he cannot wear any of his lovely new outfits until we get back home.  

If you find that ready-to-wear never fits, this is the place to come. 

We met some great people from Houston Texas whilst we were collecting our things and they recommended some great places to visit during the rest of our trip.

The service from Hein and her colleagues was truly outstanding.

When we read the guidebooks on our flights out, we were disappointed that we didn’t have longer in Hoi An, as that seems to be the best place to get things tailored in Vietnam. However, it turned out to be to our benefit.  Hoi An is apparently a prime example of over-tourism spoiling a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The lovely folk we met from Houston have a nephew who’s lived in South-East Asia for 12 years (not Vietnam) and he recommended Elegant Silk to them as the best there is.

This has proved to be the case - we will be back!  

From going in on Monday night at 8pm quite trepidatious that we were in the right place, they were having some renovations done, so there was no front window in, it was just open to the street and everything was covered in sheets.  There was no evidence that they even did anything for men. When we collected yesterday, it was a transformed shop, crowded with at least four other couples/friends all collecting or being fitted at the same time.

Everything fitted perfectly…

name: Fujikyu Highland Permanently Closed
description: Do you like more scream? Free entry to Fuji-Q Highland from July 14 ! If you come to travel near by Mt. Fuji, without any money that you can get inside the park and enjoy the fantastic view. Fuji-Q is best known for its thrilling, record-breaking roller coasters and elaborate, anime- themed rides and attractions. There are numerous “Guiness-level” attractions, including “EEJANAIKA,” the roller coasting boasting the highest total number of spins in the world, “FUJIYAMA” “DODODONPA”, and famous of “ Super Scary Labyrinth of Fear” and “Ultimate Fort3” that can challenge your courage and intelligence. There are also popular character theme-parks such as “Thomas Land” and “Lisa and Gaspard Town”. Fuji-Q Highland is bound to amuse all ranges of visitors, from youths to families. 5-6-1 Shin-nishihara, Fujiyoshida, Yamanashi Website (http://www.fujiq.jp/en)

name: Hot Sulphur Springs Resort & Spa
description: I went there yesterday with my 2 kids and my niece. We paid over $100 for 2 adults and 2 minor children, plus an additional $16 for 2 robes. When we stepped out of the front entrance into the outdoor pool area it was disgusting!! The place is falling apart, boards on benches with peeling paint, dusty, dirty corners around each area of the pools. The water inside each of the pools was full of debris and dirt. The women’s locker room was so bad I can’t describe how gross I felt changing there it made me want to throw up. Piles of dirty towels and robes piled up to almost the ceiling!! There were 3 staff members working at the front desk but nobody was checking on the bathrooms. There was no place to put your baggage, the lockers are tiny and so people’s bags were all over the locker room floor, you could barely walk. They do not limit the amount of people at one time so it was very overcrowded and they were not prepared with staff. We left after 30 minutes. Biggest waste of money and I will never be back.

name: South Carolina Aquarium
description: Discover the wonder of water, wildlife and wild places at the South Carolina Aquarium. Come face-to-face with sick and injured sea turtles in rehabilitation in our Sea Turtle Care Center ™ and follow their journeys from rescue to rehab to release. name: Lake Bled
description: Discover the magic of the lake that attracts travellers from near and far. The current unique shape of the year did not emerge coincidentally. A tectonic hole made by the Bohinj glacier through the years, was once at the location of the present lake. Its path was obstructed by a huge rock which was so persistently scraped that the only thing that remained was the present island. The ice melted and the basin was filled with water, thus Lake Bled emerged, which is in some places up to 30 metres deep and quite popular amongst divers. 19 species of fish live in the lake, including carp, sheatfish and lake trout. Ducks and swans as well as diverse plants also swim and thrive on its surface.

Come visit us and learn about our company’s commitment to producing some of the worlds finest spirits. Visit our Farm Store where you'll find our full collection of premium spirits and apparel. name: Howth Cliff Walk
description: We started the walk opposite the dart station. I would not recommend doing this as it is a long incline (1 hour of climbing) on a path through the back of housing estates. There’s nothing particularly nice about it. Once you get to the cliffs it is beautiful! However, that beautiful part is quite short (about 20 mins) and then back on the road heading down town again. The town itself is lovely with a nice harbour. We had fish and chips in Beshoffs which was superb. If I was going again I would start the walk by walking from dart station through the pretty town and then up to the cliffs from there. There are signs for the start of each level of walk as you walk past and beyond the harbour. You could do the loop and return down opposite the dart station. Personally, I would just go up to the cliffs from the town and back down again and then walk back to the dart station via the pretty town and of course stopping at Beshoffs for fish and chips.

name: Wulong Tiankeng Three Bridges
description: Wulong was our very first stop in our 8-day Chongqing tour. Wulong's attractions are mainly natural scenery, and many are listed at World Natural Heritages. There are four main famous natural attractions in Wulong: the Three Natural Bridges, Furong Cave, Fairy Mountain, and Longshuixia Gap (龙水峡地缝). Our itinerary covered two of them, and our very first destination was this Three Natural Bridges (天生三桥).Nature travels fascinate people like me who are attuned to the hustle and bustle of a modern city life. In Hamlet, William Shakespeare articulated: There are more things in heaven than there are dreams in your philosophy.  At this Nature Three Bridges, it is a pristine world of calmness and peace and far from the madding crowd of our materialistic world. What the eyes see are the sculpture world of Nature: canyon, caves, looming mountain, sinkholes, emerald lakes, waterfalls; no concrete jungle, no polluted air or toxic noise that existed in our world.The Three Natural Bridges (天生三桥) is named as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2007. It became famous due to the filming of the Chinese film Curse of the Golden Flower (满城尽带黄金甲) and followed by the filming of Transformers 4: Age of Extinction The Director Michael Bay probably left the dinosaur autobot at the filming site for remembrance.The karst landscape is amazing and spectacular. The weather is cold, but I lost myself in the nature wonderland as I hiked for 2.5 km to discover the 3 bridges:  天龙桥; 青龙桥" and 黑龙桥. It was a bit challenging for the elderly before one reached the Black Dragon Bridge (黑龙桥) with some stairs to climb, but after this bridge, it is plain walking for the other two dragon bridges.When I hiked to Tianfu Postal House (天福驿站), I found it very photogenic. It looks different and unique with a Chinese architecture postal house surrounded by the karst landscape. I climbed up to a higher platform from the adjacent karst hill and took an iconic photo of this landmark. 天福驿站 was a transmission stop built during the Tang Dynasty for communication between two provinces.I was attracted by an emerald, green lake not far from the end of the trail. A small boat lies in the middle of the lake. The scenery looks very poetic, and in bitter cold winter, it would remind me of the Tang poem (江雪):千山鸟飞绝，万径人踪灭。孤舟蓑笠翁，独钓寒江雪。Our tour guide warned us that this trip covering the Three Bridges is just an appetizer, a warmup exercise. The more challenging hike will be at the Enshi Grand Canyon (恩施 大峡谷) which would be 3 times more challenging than this.Which would a be better hiking attraction: 天生三桥 or 恩施 大峡谷?

name: Fishing Excursions
description: I booked the 7 to 9 am fishing trip on a nitro to be picked up at the grand Floridian. Arrived at 6:30. Went to the boat launch and waited until 7:10. No boats or staff arrived, so I called and was advised that there was an issue with the boat and that they would be at the grand Floridian to pick me up shortly. At 7:30 I was still waiting and called again. This operator put me through to the grand Floridian boat launch and no one picked up. At 7:40 I approached the grand Floridian customer services. I advised the staff member of the situation and he called boat rental. The staff member advised me that the boat is currently on its way to the grand Floridian and if I had just been patient I would probably be on the boat right now. T thanked him and proceeded back to the boat launch. At 8:10 the boat still had not shown up so I called again. The operator was very helpful and after a while, she discovered that the boat believed I was at the contemporary. They did not find me there and went back to their base. The operator had guest service respond to my location to speak with me. Upon their arrival, they advised me that I would be refunded for my trip and I could still use the boat for the remaining half hour of my trip. When I agreed, they reached out and to boat rental and then advised that by the time the boat arrived, my time slot will have ended. They did not have any other time slots available to offer me. They promised me a refund, but provided me with no compensation for my lost time. Terrible experience and extremely disappointing for an avid fisherman such as myself.

If you take photos, you will not have a bunch of other tourists bumping around, shoulder to shoulder, like at the more well-known slot canyons. No hipster instagram people or selfie takers clogging up the place. We were by ourselves for all but 10 minutes of the 3 hour tour!

On this three hour photo tour, we had Shane as our guide. He was extremely friendly and helpful and is also interested in photography. His whole attitude was relaxed and eager to help with getting photos the way you want them. He even played his Indian fluted inside one of the two slot canyon we went through. There was no feeling of being rushed.

This place is only 10 minutes outside of Page and is very convenient. Avoid the crowds and see a couple of beautiful slot canyons in peace.

Peek down side streets such as Annagasse and Weihburggasse, and Graben’s Seilergasse and Habsburggasse, to get a feel for the center. description: Built between 1609-1616, this impressive mosque has six minarets. Why is it called "Blue Mosque?" The village is a magical world where they can enjoy Christmas music, amazing lighting, roasting s'mores, and see live reindeer. children also have the opportunity to visit Santa and deliver their letters to his Elf aboard our over the top decorated U.S. Postal vintage mail car. Food and drink are also available for purchase. The train operates on a line that was originally constructed in 1867. name: Bigfoot Discovery Expedition
description: My family did the Bigfoot Discovery Expedition July 2021.  Everyone had a good time until the end.  Loved feeding the cows and looking at the scenery.  We do not see how the ending fit with finding Bigfoot.The truck drove into a building, the lights were turned out, a foggy mist was released and hot air blown at you from what felt like a heat lamp that was turned on high. In addition to this, monitors played a scene from a drug raid with people kneeling to be executed.  There was shouting, shooting and bombs going off.  It was extremely violent.  This lasted 10-15 minutes.  ave gonWe had a 6 and 8 year old with us who got scared.  Unfortunately we didn't read other reviews under the Big Foot Fun Park that mentioned this ending and were not provided this information prior to purchasing tickets and boarding the truck. If we had, we would not have gone.It totally ruined the fun we had been having. Prior to this, I said I’d do it again with another family member.  After sitting through the end, none of us will go back.If they want to continue with this violent ending, I suggest giving participants the choice of sitting through this ordeal or choosing a fun ending that’s actually related to Big Foot.  Even if it’s just seeing some Big Foot cutouts/statues, that would have been preferable.

description:
Burriana Beach can be a challenge for anyone who has problems walking - not when you are down on the promenade but walking down the hill(and back up again) can take a real effort.  There is limited parking near the sea front but a multi story a little further behind the main area.

Once on the promenade the beach area is flat and backed by a number of bars restaurants and shops (with parking if you are lucky to get a space) so it makes for a pleasant walk.  The beach itself is made up of sand and small gravel/pebbles and is well sheltered so waves are not too high in normal conditions. On an evening around about 6 to 7pm I noticed more parking spaces on the street behind the promenade if you intend to eat there.

name: St. Kitts Scenic Railway
description: The narrow gauge St. Kitts scenic railway is one of the most beautiful train rides in the world. Originally built in 1912 to deliver sugarcane from the fields to the sugar mill in Basseterre, the "Last Railway in the West Indies" now provides a fascinating way for visitors to see the island from the comfort of modern passenger train cars and sightseeing buses. The railway hugs the Northeastern coastline where spectacular vistas of ocean, surf, cliffs, and lush vegetation surround you. The train rolls across tall steel bridges spanning deep ""ghuts"", or canyons, and winds through small villages and farms. Dark green rainforests are skirted by rippling fields of sugar can, with the volcanic cone of Mt. Liamuiga rising above the railway. This unique rail and highway experience allows visitors the opportunity to see the island in a very short period of time. Your guide will point out all the sights as the train passes old sugar estates with abandoned windmills and chimneys.

name: Indiana Dunes State Park
description: Indiana Dunes State Park consists of 2,182 acres of primitive, beautiful, historic and unique Hoosier landscape. It lies at the north end of State Road 49 in Porter County, and includes more than three miles of beautiful beach along Lake Michigan’s southern shore. In the early 1900s scientists, recreationists and nature enthusiasts, recognizing the value and potential of the Indiana dunes area, fought to have the region preserved. As a result, in 1925, the state park was established.Large sand dunes, located beyond the entire shoreline, have taken thousands of years to form, and tower nearly 200 feet above Lake Michigan. A wide range of habitats and plant species are found in the park, with vegetation stabilizing some of the sand. These habitats provide homes for many types of plants and animals. The lake also provides habitat for many aquatic species, as well as a constantly changing fishery.Indiana Dunes State Park features a wide variety of habitats, including beach, sand dunes, black oak forest, wooded wetlands, and a button-bush marsh. Together, these areas contain some of the most diverse flora and fauna in the Midwest. Botanists from across the country enjoy studying the unusual collection of plant life. Other interesting features include “tree graveyards” (places where forests have been buried by sand and then, more recently, re-exposed by wind erosion). “Tree graveyards” can be seen in Big Blowout, near Trail 10. The Indiana Dunes area also is renowned throughout the Midwest for its birding. Visit the Nature Center to ask about good birding locations.Indiana Dunes State Park is surrounded by Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore, a federally administered park comprising approximately 15,000 acres.

We both agreed that this is the best vortex attraction, by far, compared to the others we have experienced. This one, for some reason, feels more real. Maybe it is because the trees grow in a bent direction or maybe they had more effective demonstrations. There were far more things to try at this vortex than the others, which mainly focus on height changes. Some of the hands on activities are more engaging than others, but there is a wide variety. The guides are also great. They have a lot of enthusiasm and really sell the mystique. The hours can be a little confusing as there is not much information online. It seems the last tour is usually somewhere in the 4:00 hour, so I would say plan to arrive by 4 if you want to catch a tour. This is a ton of fun and should be the number one attraction in your planned time outside of Glacier. Check it out.

name: Shri Trimbakeshwar Temple
description:
Trimbakeshwar Mahadev Temple:

Located in the picturesque town of Trimbak, Maharashtra, the Trimbakeshwar Mahadev Temple is a revered and sacred site dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, which makes it an immensely significant pilgrimage destination for Hindus.

The temple is set against the backdrop of the Sahyadri mountain range, offering visitors a serene and peaceful environment. The temple complex is beautifully constructed with intricate carvings and a rich architectural style that reflects ancient Hindu temple designs. The main sanctum houses the Trimbakeshwar Shivling, which is unique because it has three faces representing Lord Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. This distinctive feature adds to the temple's spiritual importance.

The temple is not just an architectural marvel but is also surrounded by a tranquil atmosphere, making it a place for reflection and prayer. Visitors can also take a holy dip in the nearby Brahmagiri River, which is believed to purify one’s soul. The temple is located close to the source of the Godavari River, adding to its spiritual significance.

The priests and staff at the temple are warm and helpful, guiding pilgrims through the rituals and offering a complete spiritual experience. The temple is usually crowded, especially during festivals like Mahashivaratri, so planning a visit during less busy times could provide a more peaceful experience.

One unique ritual at the temple is the "Trimbak" puja, which is performed to seek blessings for health, wealth, and prosperity. It is a must-visit for those seeking divine blessings or exploring India's rich spiritual heritage.

Conclusion:
The Trimbakeshwar Mahadev Temple is not just a place of worship but a sacred site brimming with history, spiritual significance, and natural beauty. Its peaceful surroundings, combined with the deep spiritual energy, make it a must-visit for devotees and travelers alike.

name: Lake Hollywood Park
description:
I lived in Los Angeles in the 90's and visit often because I have a daughter who lives in Hollywood, and I never knew this gem was here until I searched for running paths on my last visit! I was looking for a relatively flat trail since I'm from Houston, which is very flat. I drove up here, and the parking area is only about 12 minutes from Hollywood Blvd. and La Brea, where I was coming from. It feels a world away from the city below! The reservoir is a beautiful blue lake with wildlife you will easily see, including donkey deer, rabbits, and water birds. The Hollywood sign is just above the park and loop, and you will see it easily and unobstructed from parts of the path.

The loop around the reservoir is 3.3 miles, so the whole thing should be doable for those looking to run a 5k or continuing training for one, as I was. It's also a walking trail that probably takes an hour to an hour and a half to complete, depending upon your walking pace. Of course, you can also visit and only walk as far as you like, turning around to retrace your steps when you want to be halfway done.

Using GPS, put in Lake Hollywood Reservoir to get to the parking area for the trail. I used the 6381 Weidlake Dr address to a free parking area and trail entrance, although I saw there are supposed to be other entrances on Lake Hollywood Drive and Wonder View Drive.

The experience is really wonderful with incredible views of the city below, the water and wildlife, and the Hollywood sign, not to mention the pretty drive up through the Hollywood Hills to get there. I highly recommend it if you're looking for that sort of thing to change up your trip to Los Angeles and the Hollywood area, especially.

name: Wadi Shab
description:
I read a lot of reviews and appreciated the ones with tips so I will pass along my own.  

I drove myself, it’s completely doable, you don’t need to spend $$$ on a tour.  The country is very drivable.  I arrived around 11 and the parking under the bridge was full but I still found a spot with no issues. 

There’s a store/cafe near the boat ramp selling drinks and it appeared light food. I was happy to grab an extra water before the start. 

As many people said, 1 rial for the boat, kids are free.  There was a man renting life vests, selling various size wet bags, water shoes and phone dry bags.  I bought a phone dry case(3 rial)  but didn’t use it for fear it would leak and then I’d be without a phone to get back.  

We were wearing sneakers, I’ve traveled all over the world, backpacked years ago and have never need water shoes before.  For this trip if I did it again I would get the shoes.  It was about 4 minutes total (there and back) over rocks if you want to get to the cave and we did it but my feet were sore the next day.  

It was 1.90 miles one way and took myself and an active 6 year old 1 hour to get to the main event.  We wore our suits and took a backpack.  I saw the full spectrum of people, young adults in flip flops, serious hikers in full hiking boots and gear, a couple with an infant carrying dad and the mom with a toddler on her hip, elder people being assisted.  The hike isn’t hard but it’s slippery and there are times when you need 3 points of contact (feet, hands, rear) and there are points where it’s close to the edge with a narrow walk way.  We had to cross over water once on the way there. 

It’s about 10 minutes of swim, walk, swim to the cave and in late December the space was just large enough to fit a medium size adult head, you could go under and make it as well. Many adults opted not to try but it was pretty awesome when we get in.  There wasn’t many places on the way or in the cave to hold on too so if you are not a strong swimmer, then take the life vest.  

Totally worth a visit!

name: Piazza Tasso
description:
The Piazzoa Tasso sits at the centre of the town of Sorrento. If not at the exact geographic centre of this tourist town on the Sorrentine Peninsula south of Naples, then certainly close enough. It could however be considered the cultural and economic centre of Sorrento.

It is the start point for the Corso Italian, one of the main thoroughfares of the town that begins at its eastern edge. To the north down a steep cliff is the Marina Picollo one of the two harbours in the town and the terminus for the numerous ferries that ply the Bay of Naples. 

South is the tree lined Viale Enrico Caruso, and to the east of this is the Sorrento train station the terminus for the commuter train that runs to Pompeii and Naples and a transit hub for local and regional buses. Finally, to the west lies the Via San Cesareo a pedestrian only street that is the heart of the Centro Storico a tourist zone of narrow streets full of shops and attractions.

The Piazza Tasso was named after the 16th Century poet Torqueto Tasso (1544-1595) who was born in Sorrento.  A statue honouring him stands in the plaza off to the side. In the centre of the plaza stands another statue. This one dedicated to Sant Antonio or Antoninus of Sorrento the patron Saint of Sorrento. This is one of two statues to the Saint in the town, the other is in the centre of the nearby Piazza Sant’ Antonio.

On the north eastern edge of the plaza is the Santuario della Madonna del Carmine a 15th Century Church.  West of this covering the northern edge is the narrow gorge that bisects the town and leads to the seaside and port. The Via Luigi de Maio winds through this as does a series of steep steps.

The rest of the Piazza is lined with several cafes and restaurants where one may grab a meal or just a drink and kill some time people watching. It should be noted that these for the most part cater to the crowds of tourists and are priced accordingly.

name: Wulong Tiankeng Three Bridges
description: Wulong was our very first stop in our 8-day Chongqing tour. Wulong's attractions are mainly natural scenery, and many are listed at World Natural Heritages. There are four main famous natural attractions in Wulong: the Three Natural Bridges, Furong Cave, Fairy Mountain, and Longshuixia Gap (龙水峡地缝). Our itinerary covered two of them, and our very first destination was this Three Natural Bridges (天生三桥).Nature travels fascinate people like me who are attuned to the hustle and bustle of a modern city life. In Hamlet, William Shakespeare articulated: There are more things in heaven than there are dreams in your philosophy.  At this Nature Three Bridges, it is a pristine world of calmness and peace and far from the madding crowd of our materialistic world. What the eyes see are the sculpture world of Nature: canyon, caves, looming mountain, sinkholes, emerald lakes, waterfalls; no concrete jungle, no polluted air or toxic noise that existed in our world.The Three Natural Bridges (天生三桥) is named as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2007. It became famous due to the filming of the Chinese film Curse of the Golden Flower (满城尽带黄金甲) and followed by the filming of Transformers 4: Age of Extinction The Director Michael Bay probably left the dinosaur autobot at the filming site for remembrance.The karst landscape is amazing and spectacular. The weather is cold, but I lost myself in the nature wonderland as I hiked for 2.5 km to discover the 3 bridges:  天龙桥; 青龙桥" and 黑龙桥. It was a bit challenging for the elderly before one reached the Black Dragon Bridge (黑龙桥) with some stairs to climb, but after this bridge, it is plain walking for the other two dragon bridges.When I hiked to Tianfu Postal House (天福驿站), I found it very photogenic. It looks different and unique with a Chinese architecture postal house surrounded by the karst landscape. I climbed up to a higher platform from the adjacent karst hill and took an iconic photo of this landmark. 天福驿站 was a transmission stop built during the Tang Dynasty for communication between two provinces.I was attracted by an emerald, green lake not far from the end of the trail. A small boat lies in the middle of the lake. The scenery looks very poetic, and in bitter cold winter, it would remind me of the Tang poem (江雪):千山鸟飞绝，万径人踪灭。孤舟蓑笠翁，独钓寒江雪。Our tour guide warned us that this trip covering the Three Bridges is just an appetizer, a warmup exercise. The more challenging hike will be at the Enshi Grand Canyon (恩施 大峡谷) which would be 3 times more challenging than this.Which would a be better hiking attraction: 天生三桥 or 恩施 大峡谷?

name: Fishing Excursions
description: I booked the 7 to 9 am fishing trip on a nitro to be picked up at the grand Floridian. Arrived at 6:30. Went to the boat launch and waited until 7:10. No boats or staff arrived, so I called and was advised that there was an issue with the boat and that they would be at the grand Floridian to pick me up shortly. At 7:30 I was still waiting and called again. This operator put me through to the grand Floridian boat launch and no one picked up. At 7:40 I approached the grand Floridian customer services. I advised the staff member of the situation and he called boat rental. The staff member advised me that the boat is currently on its way to the grand Floridian and if I had just been patient I would probably be on the boat right now. T thanked him and proceeded back to the boat launch. At 8:10 the boat still had not shown up so I called again. The operator was very helpful and after a while, she discovered that the boat believed I was at the contemporary. They did not find me there and went back to their base. The operator had guest service respond to my location to speak with me. Upon their arrival, they advised me that I would be refunded for my trip and I could still use the boat for the remaining half hour of my trip. When I agreed, they reached out and to boat rental and then advised that by the time the boat arrived, my time slot will have ended. They did not have any other time slots available to offer me. They promised me a refund, but provided me with no compensation for my lost time. Terrible experience and extremely disappointing for an avid fisherman such as myself.

name: Kronborg Slot
description: Kronborg is a must-see! “Hamlet’s Castle” is a magnificent experience with soaring towers, a huge ballroom, damp casemates and just 40 minutes from Copenhagen. At the narrowest neck of the sound, between Denmark and Sweden, the medieval fortress merges with the magnificent Renaissance castle and there are few sites in the world where so much drama and history is gathered in one place. Mythical hero Holger the Dane’s mighty sword meets Shakespeare’s equally mighty pen, as the spirit of Hamlet glides through the castle. No wonder this extraordinary place is on UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

name: Laguna El Dudu
description: Laguna Dudu is an exciting and mostly unknown paradise located on the north east coast of the Dominican Republic. It's surrounded by natural cliffs from which to swim, snorkel or free dive into refreshing clear waters. If you love adrenaline rush then try a zip line freefall from 10 meters. You may need to take a deep breath for this adventure. Once you finally takeoff for a subjective six seconds drop in thin air, and finish with a big splash. But it's also a spot worth visiting for it offers a cave to explore, a beautiful cove with other challenging experiences. There are stairs leading down to the water which enables smooth and easy access to both lagoons. With nature to explore and plenty of photographic spots. A visit to Laguna Dudu can easily be combined with two additional beach activities since it's located within minutes between two playas (beaches) Diamante and Arroyo Salado. Your next adventure awaits you. Come, explore and show us your favorite spot.

description: We just stopped here for a short while, but did not actually swim in the spring. The water was comfortably warm (I felt it with my hand), but there is a strong odor of sulphur, which was not pleasant. There were several people swimming there when we visited -- kids and adults. They appeared to be locals. It was worth seeing, since we were already in the area, but I would not go out of my way to visit. Would I go swimming there? Maybe. But I would probably want to shower soon afterwards to wash off the malodorous sulphur-infused water.

name: Hospitalbar

Closest at hand are the Royal Palace, the quaint shops of Haalremmerdijk, the pedestrianized zones Kalverstraat and Dam Square with popular neighborhoods such as the Red Light District, and the Canal Ring hardly more than a moment’s stroll away. name: Water Holes Canyon
description:
We saw one other tour group of 8-10 people while we were there for 3 hours. If you take photos, you will not have a bunch of other tourists bumping around, shoulder to shoulder, like at the more well-known slot canyons. No hipster instagram people or selfie takers clogging up the place. We were by ourselves for all but 10 minutes of the 3 hour tour!

On this three hour photo tour, we had Shane as our guide. He was extremely friendly and helpful and is also interested in photography. His whole attitude was relaxed and eager to help with getting photos the way you want them. He even played his Indian fluted inside one of the two slot canyon we went through. There was no feeling of being rushed.

This place is only 10 minutes outside of Page and is very convenient. Avoid the crowds and see a couple of beautiful slot canyons in peace.

name: Six Flags St Louis

name: VR Park Tokyo
description: There are countless opportunities to shop in the Shibuya and Harajuku districts, especially in shops that focus on Japan's "Kawaii" culture. The trendiest areas are around Shibuya’s Center district, Harajuku's Takeshita-dori and in Omotesando. If you need to recharge from all the shopping, you can easily refresh yourself in Meiji Jingu or Sasaki Park. In contrast, Ebisu has a more grown up ambiance of calm and cool. At the Museum of Yebisu Beer you can learn about the beer that was responsible for the town’s name, and enjoy dining at the popular noodle shops in the surrounding area.

name: Tiger Kingdom Phuket
description: Tiger Kingdom Phuket is a once in a lifetime experience where you can meet, play, and have your photo taken with tigers! Watch the tigers as you kick back with some food and drink from our top-quality restaurant. You are sure to have a very memorable experience! Open daily including public holidays from 9am to 5pm.

description: In Vienna's best-known district, pedestrian boulevards Kärntner Strasse and Graben connect you with landmarks such as the Wiener Staatsoper (Vienna State Opera), Vienna’s iconic Stephansdom (St. Stephen’s Cathedral) and the vast compound of Hofburg, the Habsburgs’ former Imperial Palace. Peek down side streets such as Annagasse and Weihburggasse, and Graben’s Seilergasse and Habsburggasse, to get a feel for the center. The Imperial Apartments and the refreshingly demystifying Sissi Museum are must-dos at Hofburg. Spacious squares such as Am Hof and Freyung often host beautiful seasonal and antiques markets.

name: California Science Center
description: Welcome to the California Science Center! While Endeavour is off exhibit, we remain one of the largest science centers in the nation, with multiple hands-on galleries, unforgettable special exhibitions, and immersive IMAX movies. General admission to our permanent exhibits is FREE. ( Excludes special paid exhibits and IMAX Theater.) name: Blue Mosque
description: Built between 1609-1616, this impressive mosque has six minarets. Why is it called "Blue Mosque?" There are two stories: the first, more common one is that the interior is covered in Blue İznik tiles. The second is: many years ago, ancient sailors who sailed by the mosque on the Marmara Sea saw the blue colors of the sea reflected in the mosque.

name: Hanoi Old Quarter
categories: ['Beer Tastings & Tours in Hanoi', 'Cooking Classes in Hanoi', 'Food Tours in Hanoi', 'Breweries in Hanoi', 'Coffee & Tea Tours in Hanoi']
description: Located in the middle of Ha Noi, a rapidly developing city where changes take place every hour, Hanoi Old Quarter with its old-styled narrow streets full of antique brick houses seems to nostalgically resist the flow of time while still actively trying to adapt to the dynamic atmosphere of the modern city.

name: Arabella Cruise Bar
description: Discover the Arabella Cruise Bar: a floating monument, tested in WW2, with proven historical value. Get to know Thessaloniki from a different angle. Admire the incomparable beauty of the city, while enjoying your coffee. The beautiful sunset will fascinate you. Indulge in the rhythm of music accompanied by your loved ones, under the stars holding a unique cocktail. Arabella has been loved by the people, many events have taken place in it: such as its participation in those of the Ministry of Culture. with the theme of ancient ports in the Thermaic Gulf, photos for fashion magazines, video clips and countless receptions and parties. Mast), while its draft is 2.8 meters.

name: Midland Railway

The Snowglobe Express is a one of a kind 12 mile round trip excursion where passengers ride in decorated vintage train cars to the Snowglobe Christmas Village, where they get off the train and spend 45- 60 minutes. The village is a magical world where they can enjoy Christmas music, amazing lighting, roasting s'mores, and see live reindeer. children also have the opportunity to visit Santa and deliver their letters to his Elf aboard our over the top decorated U.S. Postal vintage mail car. Food and drink are also available for purchase. The train operates on a line that was originally constructed in 1867. Midland Railroad also offers train rides at various times through out the year, with other event type trains.

name: Bigfoot Discovery Expedition
description: My family did the Bigfoot Discovery Expedition July 2021.  Everyone had a good time until the end.  Loved feeding the cows and looking at the scenery.  We do not see how the ending fit with finding Bigfoot.The truck drove into a building, the lights were turned out, a foggy mist was released and hot air blown at you from what felt like a heat lamp that was turned on high. In addition to this, monitors played a scene from a drug raid with people kneeling to be executed.  There was shouting, shooting and bombs going off.  It was extremely violent.  This lasted 10-15 minutes.  ave gonWe had a 6 and 8 year old with us who got scared.  Unfortunately we didn't read other reviews under the Big Foot Fun Park that mentioned this ending and were not provided this information prior to purchasing tickets and boarding the truck. If we had, we would not have gone.It totally ruined the fun we had been having. Prior to this, I said I’d do it again with another family member.  After sitting through the end, none of us will go back.If they want to continue with this violent ending, I suggest giving participants the choice of sitting through this ordeal or choosing a fun ending that’s actually related to Big Foot.  Even if it’s just seeing some Big Foot cutouts/statues, that would have been preferable.

name: Sandland Adventures
description: Experience the Oregon Dunes and Family Fun Park at Sandland Adventures. Offering tours of the dunes since 1987, our professional drivers will show you a great time while you travel across an impressive natural wonder of endless shifting sand. Choose an exhilarating dune ride on our Sandrails or a relaxing tour on our Giant Dune Buggies. For those who prefer speed and excitement, try either a half hour 10 mile tour or an hour 20 mile tour. These 7 to 10 passenger Long Travel Sandrails have over 20” of suspension travel and plenty of horsepower to take you on an exhilarating ride. If you prefer a slower pace, enjoy our Giant Dune Buggy Tour with many picture opportunities. Informative, scenic and fun describes this one hour dune buggy tour covering approximately 8 miles of dunes and 2 miles of ocean beach. Climbing and descending through the most beautiful, impressive dunes will be an unforgettable experience. We are located less than one mile south of Florence on Hwy 101.

It's that passion, tempered with more than twenty five years of experience flying balloons that has helped us become the best ballooning operator in Turkey. Every flight is a fantastic adventure as we float intimately amongst the fairy chimneys and soar over the magnificent Cappadocian landscape. A flight with Kapadokya Balloons is truly "the experience of a lifetime!"

name: La Gondola
description: Experience Providence from a new perspective! Benvenuto! We invite you to revel in the sights of the City from a unique vantage point that captures the heart of Providence. Enjoy an excursion along the Woonasquatucket and Providence Rivers and witness the revitalization of the City, river walks, and waterfront parks. The railway hugs the Northeastern coastline where spectacular vistas of ocean, surf, cliffs, and lush vegetation surround you. The train rolls across tall steel bridges spanning deep ""ghuts"", or canyons, and winds through small villages and farms. Dark green rainforests are skirted by rippling fields of sugar can, with the volcanic cone of Mt. Liamuiga rising above the railway. This unique rail and highway experience allows visitors the opportunity to see the island in a very short period of time. Your guide will point out all the sights as the train passes old sugar estates with abandoned windmills and chimneys.
