name: Paris Charms & Secrets Tours
description: One of the best city tours we’ve taken.   The guide was fantastic, clearly a history buff.   Visited several off the beaten path locations.  Cannot recommend enough.

name: Elephant Jungle Sanctuary Samui
description: Elephant Jungle Sanctuary promotes a sustainable and ethical way of treating elephants and our little elephant village in Samui is a wonderful example of that. We opened our first sanctuary in 2014 in Chiang Mai with just three elephants, and now operate locations across four provinces in the Kingdom of Thailand.

name: Hon Ba Nature Reserve
description: Situated 56km SE of Nha Trang, this newly developed site includes a reconstruction of Dr Alexandre Yersin's outstation. The building contains items of original furniture transported from the Dr Yersin Museum in Nha Trang, and reproductions of several period photographs. Entrance fee to the historical site is 30,000 dong. On site parking is free.Also on site are: an open sided canteen, and five small chalets for rent at 500,000 dong per night per couple (100,000 dong per additional guest). Electricity is available, but as yet is inexplicably not connected. Hence (1) the canteen menu is limited to dried fish, dried squid and fresh chicken, killed just for you. Tea, coffee, soft drinks and non-refigerated beer are available without ice; (2) the chalets are unheated and without hot water; and (3) small kerosene hurrican lamps are used for lighting.To get here, go 17km from Nha Trang towards Saigon, turn right at Suoi Cat commune at a blue and white tourist sign "Ho Chua Nuoc Suoi Dau", after one km and turn left a market onto the Hon Ba road. Follow this road 38km to Hon Ba peak.A visit to this site would suit history buffs and those just wishing an escape from summer heat in Nha Trang. Good swimming holes are available in the stream at the bottom of the mountain, especially near the Foresty Inspection Station boom gate, 13km from the Suoi Cat turn off.

name: Nha Trang Snake Show
description: Nha Trang Snake Show - is the biggest Snake Show in Asia. The performance will take your breath away once you see our skillful snake charmers having famous cobra kiss. Other risky tricks will get you into the atmosphere of a high adrenaline level. Our professional guides will make sertain that you discover the amaizing secrets of snakes while having a tour around serpentarium.

name: Vinh Luong Market
description: We stopped by for a couple of hours at this market. Buys include sports goods, cultural stuff, food.

name: Nha Phu Bay
description: We booked through our hotel and were promised an english speaking guide aswell as no animal cruelty. However we were put on the back of the bus and given basic directions and no tour so to speak.Orchid island is basically a zoo where bears are dressed up and made to walk on hind legs and elephants and ostricts are forced to let people ride them the only nice bit was the butterfly bit but still pretty small enclosures for most animals.Monkey island consist of animal shows and the dog races are tied up with little monkeys to ride them.I would suggest never coming here if you respect animals even a little bit.

name: A&b Central Square Nha Trang
description: You shouldn't expect too much here. There are a few shops here, as well as the usual chains. Nothing extraordinary. Opposite is a "Bread Talk" and an Adidas store

name: Sunrise Gaming Club
description: One of the most luxury gaming club in Nha Trang. We are offering: Slot Machines, Roulette, Baccarat & Black Jack

name: 100 Egg Theme Park
description: Welcome to the largest, most fantastic Tourist Attraction in Nha Trang. Brace yourselves for a totally unique experience! Indulge in numerous areas, shows, activities, and services not found elsewhere in Vietnam, all the while taking you right back to nature. It's all about having a good time here at the 100 Egg Mud Bath.

name: St. Joseph's Parish Church
description: If in Nha Trang its worthwhile having a look at. Right in the middle of town and easy to get to. Very clean and tidy. Not the biggest cathedral but interesting history of how the French built it.

name: Diep Son Island
address: AddressVan Phong Bay Van Thang Commune, Van Ninh District, Nha Trang 650000 Vietnam
description: The sea water was so clear in this relaxing island area. Remember to bring the swimsuits along, since you won't be able to stop yourself from dipping into the blue water. Relaxing atmosphere and worth visit. Should come at weekdays less tourists, not weekend.

name: Charm Spa Garden Nha Trang
description: I had a great experience with the herbal shampoo here. A place with fresh and cool air, especially the yogurt is delicious. Thao gave me enthusiastic advice and helped me a lot. Will come back soon ❤️

name: Dao Yen - Hon Noi
description: It was sunny day, the island was beautiful with a small sand walking path, there were always cool wind flow over, it was fantastic feeling.Activities was simple, include of swimming, visting natural bird nest, climbing, snorkling.Water was clear & fresh, great for swimmimg however, there were a lot of rocks gave pain on my feet and the other side had a lot of coral that i needed to wear slipper to swim, if not, coral would cut my feet.On the boat to visit natural bird nest, i could see coral through glasses of boat bottom.Lunch was delicious**on the way to reach the island, it was a lot of waves, who has sea sickness should prepare yourself cause it takes 2 hours.

name: Vinh Hai Market
address: AddressHai Thang Tu Vinh Hai, Nha Trang 650000 Vietnam
description: This is a wet market caters mainly for locals. Wet market smell and not recommended for tourist. About 5km from city center. Not much souvenir or clothing shops. Mainly a wet market.

name: Clover Spa Nha Trang
description: Clover Spa is a wellness spa located in the coastal city of Nha Trang in Vietnam. The spa offers a range of services including body massage, thai massage, bamboo massage, deep massage, hotstone massage, herbal massage, foot massage, facials, body treatments. Clover spa in nha trang is a popular wellness spa offering a variety of services and using natural ingredients to enhance the experience. Clover Spa has received positive reviews from customers for its professional staff and serene atmosphere.

name: Casa Spa
description: Casa Spa is located in central Nha Trang city, you will be pampered with high standard of services includes massage, nails, waxing, facial, eyelahes. We will look after you from head to toe with our expert beauty therapist and technician.

name: Tran Phu Bridge
description: Beautiful Bridge that connects the north and south of the Mouth of the Cai Nha Trang River, which leads directly into the heart of the city, crossed several times in our stay in Nha Trang we could observe it by day and evening illuminated even more evocative. It is lined with two palm tree walkways and a beautiful park, with beautiful palm trees to frame it, on one side you can admire the Nha Trang waterfront, the white beach and the ocean, on the other side it overlooks the other Bong bridge, with views of many boats and fishing boats. Many clubs in the morning engage in many activities, from gymnastics , running , fishing , while the street is always crowded with cars and mopeds from morning to night . On the one hand, there are numerous seafood restaurants, cafes, and elegant hotels.

name: Suoi Da Hon Giao
description: Nice view however very poor meal. Pho bo soup was very light and spring rolls with ketchup??? 🤦🏼‍♀️

name: MerPerle Hon Tam Mud Bath
description: When talking about Nha Trang, everyone must recognize that “Mud Bath” has famously created a strong brand awareness for the tourism of the local province of Khanh Hoa. For this reason, MerPerle Hon Tam Mud Bath was born to contribute to the wide variety of products and services on the Island to provide guests with a unique-to-second experience. Inspired by the terrace architecture, the Mud Bath was designed in an open space of over 16,000 m2 with a great offer of various service options set available around a regulating pool in green premises which certainly create the most enjoyable moments upon entering.

name: Soi Island Recreational Park
address: AddressTri Nguyen Island, Vinh Nguyen Ward, Nha Trang 650000 VietnamReach out directlyVisit websiteCallEmail
description: "Soi Island" is apart of Tri Nguyen Island Where you could enjoy A Day Pass including Aquarium, Beautiful Beach, Water Sports, and Coral Park will be operating soon !

name: NY Vape Store Nha Trang
description: Ny Vape Store (Nyvapepod) is a Vape store in Nha Trang, providing genuine electronic cigarettes, essential oils, Vape bodies, burners, accessories, Pods, Vape in Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa, many other locations in Viet Nam

name: Shop Bao Cao Su - Drloves Nha Trang
description: The shop specializes in products for adults. Full range of products to support tourists here to experience wonderful moments such as: condoms, gels, adult toys for men and women, along with other enhancement products...

name: Ba Ho Waterfall
address: AddressNinh Ich, Ninh Hoa, Nha Trang 57000 Vietnam
description:
We met Mr Lam of Vietnam Motor Tours by chance on the street in Na Trang and went on a half day tour, the highlight of which without question was definitely the Ba Ho Waterfall.
Firstly, the additional 40,000 dong for return trip from facility reception to the falls by electric buggy was the best money I've ever spent, and I would have gladly paid multiple times that just for the trip back. Seriously, I can see no sense in taking on such an unnecessary arduous walk.
The falls are spectacular located within an equally spectacular forest setting with loads of clean facilities,  toilets, and childrens play areas.
The hike from the viewing bridge to the falls pulling yourself over rocks by using guide ropes is arduous, to say the least, but oh, so worth it. Most young and old will make it, but it is a little dicey here and there.
There are 3 ascending pools. However, on the day of our visit, only 2 were open due to a huge run of water following on from inclement weather. Something my sweat soaked overweight body was extremely grateful for at the time.
Even though we didn't get to swim, i would highly ighly recommend a visit to its value for time and money.
Mr Lam, our guide was fantastic

name: VinWonders Nha Trang
description:
With a long history since 2006, VinWonders Nha Trang is a must-visit of Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa. The amusement park is located in the integrated resort complex Vinpearl on the poetic island of Hon Tre. 

VinWonders Nha Trang (previously named Vinpearl Land Nha Trang) is an all-in-one amusement park with 6 primary areas, offering memorable experiences to visitors of all ages and nationalities.

name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
description: The Po Nagar Tower is the name of the main temple in a complex of Cham towers on a knoll at the river-mouth of the Cai River, 2km north of Nha Trang City. Nowadays, the name Po Nagar is usually used to refer to the whole complex.

name: Nha Trang Beach
description:
Nha Trang Beach is one of the best known and most popular beaches in southern Vietnam, on the one hand it has some pros and cons. The beach is kilometre long with fine white sand, when we were there in December and January the sea was quite rough and the sky covered with clouds, however the weather was great with 27/28 degrees , with pleasant breeze , for this reason not all the Beach clubs were open and there were never many people on the beach and I also found it clean. Behind the beach there is a beautiful well-kept seafront, with beautiful gardens and trees, very high palm trees to frame as in a postcard , monuments , benches , fountains and restaurants on the sea, all along a wide main road quite busy between scooters and cars , buses , behind Luxury Hotels , Skyscrapers and Malls overlooking the bay . On the one hand in Nha Trang there is everything one could want with so many restaurants both upmarket and local, ditto the shops, banks, the market, some attractions to visit and bathing establishments, and frankly we have been lucky to find little rubbish around , however , for those looking for tranquility, I recommend the beaches of Doc Let an hour’s drive and Cam Ranh about half an hour away because I dare not imagine in the busy period how many people there are on the beach. 
From the end of January to August dry season, are the best months for a seaside holiday with gentle waves and possibility to reach the Islets opposite by boat was now impossible for us.
However scenographically it is very beautiful , and at Christmas time , the city and the promenade are a blaze of festoons , lights , concerts , events .

name: Long Son Pagoda
description: There are only a few real sights in Nha Trang and this is one of them. The Pagoda, The Buddha, The Bell and the Lying Buddha are the main items. Quite a testing walk up the steps to the top but well worth it as you get a good view of Nha Trang and the main Buddha. There is a small temple under the Buddha so make sure you have your shoulders covered if you want to visit

name: Paradise Cable Car
description: Wonderful experience, the view from the top is beautiful and the park is stunning, Better to go in the afternoon to have a good view of the sunset

name: Long Thanh Photo Studio
description: Long Thanh's photographic repertoire is unique as its wide-ranging. His landscapes are often moody, contrasting the natural beauty of Vietnam with the continuing struggle in people's daily lives, while Long Thanh's portraiture captures the essence of the Vietnamese people, especially his high-contrast pictures of old people who have witnessed more than their fair share of tradegy over the generations.

name: Doc Let Beach
description: Paradise on earth... Zocled beach is the perfect place for a fantastic holiday. Pure sea, gentle sand...locations for photos

name: Bãi Tắm Hòn Chồng
description: i visited this place two weeks ago when i had one day tour in Nha Trang. this is the first stop of my trip. after buying ticket, i entered a traditional building, then i had a seat there, to listen to traditional vietnamese music. after that i walked  to the back of the building. stepping down lots of stairs,then reached Hon Chong beach. there are many rocks there. after lots of climbing, i saw a boulder which facing the ocean, on the boulder, there is a giant five-fingered hand on it. According to a folktale,long time ago, a giant man was fishing here, suddenly a giant fish swallowed the bait and pulled him away. The man tried to pull himself back, he used one hand holding the fishing-rod, and one hand pressing against the boulder, so he left his five-fingered imprint on it. it is the IG spot, many tourist taking pics with it. but be careful, the place is rather dangerous, don't stand at the edge of the rocks. besides this, there is another IG spot, before you reaching the five-finger imprint boulder, you will see two rocks standing upright with another big rock stuck in between that looks like a big stone gate.quite interesting. that time i visited Hon Chong, the weather very hot, so better prepare sunglasses and sunscreen, and avoid visiting here at noon time.

name: Nha Tho Nui
description:
During a tour from Nha Trang we went to visit this Cathedral , the main one of the city, a reference point for the large Catholic Christian community present in the province of Khanh Hoa, located in a large square on top of a hill from where you can admire a beautiful view. We went at 12:00 but it was closed and we returned at 14:00 when it opens in the afternoon, beware because you will find at the entrance before the gate a guy asking for money not really an offer but more an imposition , instead the Cathedral you can visit for free. 
The Catholic Church was built by the French and inaugurated by Father Louis Valley in 1933 in neo-Gothic style, with large arches and beautiful soaring stained windows and the clock tower with an imposing square-shaped bell tower placed at the entrance. To access it you have to take off your shoes , when we were , much of the interior was delimited is inaccessible , so we sat in the back without being able to admire the altar and the interior details more closely , too bad !!! Outside there were two Nativity scenes, one in the square where there is a statue of the Virgin Mary. Outside the church there are several gravestones including that of Father louis Valley and Bishop Marcel Piquet.
Definitely to see among the activities of Nha Trang , although I was not particularly surprised.

name: Nha Trang Center
description: I'm not a fan of shopping malls, but since it was raining we visited two of them, this one is 50 meters from the sea, in a densely populated area. The center is well done multi-storey dedicated to different sections, clothing, accessories, souvenirs and jewelry, luggage, appliances, electronics, supermarket and a food court with many restaurants, Chinese, Vietnamese, Buffet, European, Cafe. There is also a play area. Cute to buy something original , there are several fashion and sports brands . Beautiful view from the top floor of Nha Trang Bay, the islands and the Vinpearl.

name: Alexandre Yersin Museum
description: I usually don't like the museums.Nut here I spent almost an hour alone there.The museum is small. Just one big room with several sections.But the story of Yersin was so fascinating for me I didn't even notice how an hour passed.

name: Khu du lịch Đảo Khỉ
description: The animal circus was a terrible experience.The dogs were terrifying.These people are abusing the monkeys, dogs, pig.Don't go there. They need to stop abusing these poor animals!

name: Bùn Khoáng nóng I-Resort Nha Trang
description: Great experienceA must do whilst staying in Nha TrangInclude a massage, it’s worth itStaff we’re all lovelyOur tourists were pushy and rude

name: Hon Mieu Island
description: The tour is very interesting and educational, thank you very much to our guide ARTHUR!!! Cove with beautiful landscape, small waterfalls, very beautiful flowers.

name: Hon Mun Island
description: Fair amount of fish if you feed them. No coral or any other life there. Not allowed to use snorkel. So it’s swimming with a mask. Asked a guide and he claimed people were drowning thru the snorkel and no one could tell because they were lying face down. Better going to other island were there is still some coral

name: National Oceanographic Museum of Vietnam
description: Actually felt disgusted with myself when I left this place. We’ve visited aquariums and sea life centres all over the world and they all have one thing in common and that is CONSERVATION !!!!!This place is grotesque, the size of the fish and turtles cramped into tiny little pools is horrible, even the tunnel they advertise is only about a foot wide either side and has lots of sad looking sharks and rays sat on the bed not moving.Everywhere else is just plastic models of fish or dead ones which I presume have died there in their sickening tiny tanks.We went here because we were on a tour but I had to get out because it was so sad.If the owners of this place ever read the reviews people leave then please get a dictionary and look up the words MARINE CONSERVATION !!!!!

name: Suoi Do Pagoda
description: Very nice temple and cool buddha statue. Very glad we went here! Was a very nice view at the top by the statue too. Can be recomended

name: Bãi biển Nha Trang
description: Very calm and quiet beach with very small crowd of people when I visited this month of December. There both paid and free parking along the beach. beautiful walk way and soft sand. I really love swimming and taking walks here.

name: Thap Ba Mud Bath
description: Thap Ba Mud Bath opened in 1999, the first of its kind in the NhaTrang city. We have now become a popular stop for locals and travelers looking for relaxation and therapeutic cleansing of the body. Not only is mud thought to have many medicinal healing properties, but it is also fun.

name: Lotte Mart
address: Address58 Street 23/10, Nha Trang 650000 VietnamReach out directlyVisit websiteCall
description: Great Korean grocery store. Based on the department store in South Korea. Fresh meat and fish and daily groceries. Lots of fresh bread

name: Gold Coast Shopping  Mall
description: Located in the heart of Nha Trang city center, Gold Coast Mall is the first and largest international standard shopping mall in Nha Trang, providing customers with new and exciting shopping and entertainment experiences. Gold Coast Mall Nha Trang, with its unique design, is home of over 100 top domestic and international brands, ideal destination for locals and tourists to visit and go shopping.

name: Thap Tram Huong
description:
This Tower - Particular Sculpture , is located in a privileged position, on the main street Tran Phu on one side with its Restaurants and bars, malls , Luxury Hotels and on the other directly overlooking the beautiful beach of NhaTrang with its white beach and tall palm trees. The Tower when we were there was closed to visitors so we only admired it from the outside , inside it has 4 floors , inside it is presented the history of the Provincial Committee of Khanh Hoa , along with characteristic images of the place such as , birds nest , agar wood , fishing festival , sea festival . 
On the day we visited it near there were scaffolding for an event as there was a concert , however we managed to pass and take some pictures . The Tower was built in 2004 is officially inaugurated in 2008 , over the years it has had more renovations the last in 2023 , the Tower is designed to represent a Lotus Flower , but also remembers the morning on top of a burning incense stick and the evening illuminated with numerous LEDs recalls a torch or a lighthouse on the sea, much more fascinating in the evening than during the day. The white enchants with the Blue windows that stand out and blend with the color of the sea... too bad that the weather in January was always cloudy ...

name: Tong Lam Lo Son Temple Lot
description: Simply amazing place! A huge statue of Buddha in full growth on the outskirts of the city. Silence and very few tourists. Nearby a pagoda and a cemetery under construction, there are monks. You can climb to the base of the statue, the entrance is open from the butt, do not forget to take off your shoes before you enter. There is a view of the cemetery, beautiful roofs of tombs, rice fields and mountains.

name: Binh Ba Island
description: I think it could a perfect place for one day short and fast trip but in the end you will surprise badly as possible. This place is closed for foreign people at all

name: Robinson Beach Nha Trang
description: Robinson Beach Nha Trang, a hidden gem at the edge of Nha Trang Bay, offers a perfect retreat for relaxation and adventure. With pristine white sands and crystal-clear waters, the island promises unique experiences like kayaking, snorkeling, floating bars, water sports, and fresh seafood. Cozy villas with 24/7 butler service ensure comfort and luxury. Discover nature's beauty, indulge in thrilling activities, and create unforgettable memories. Book your escape to paradise today!

name: Vincom Plaza Nha Trang
description: Many vacant locations in the mall. The Win-mart supermarket had the best selections. My time was spent just walking around and having a decent milky coffee.

name: Nha Trang Night Market
description: Night markets with restaurants and shopping, close to the main beach road

name: ĐÓ THEATRE
description: Inspired by "Cái Đó," a popular traditional fishing tool used by Vietnamese people to catch fish and shrimp, Đó - Đó Theatre is designed and built as a giant "Cái Đó" located on the coast of Bãi Tiên. Combining traditional and futuristic architecture with modern structures around, Đó Theatre promises to evoke the complete emotions of Vietnamese folk art and world art. It is poised to become a beloved theatre for many domestic and international artists, as well as a "must-visit" art destination for local and international tourists.

name: Diamond Bay Gaming Club
description: The Top One Casino in Nha Trang City. Game : Slot Machines, Roulette, Baccarat & Black Jack, Sic Bo. Free Show : Live bands, Hot Dance, DJ Music. Free for players : Cocktails, Beer, Coffee, Juice, Soju, Snacks.

name: Tampa Cable Car
description: The Tâmpa cable car or Tâmpa Cable Car or Telecabina Tâmpa takes users to the local mountain of Brasov. The return ticket costs only 35 RON and the train runs daily except on Monday between 9:30 and 16:30. The 2 cabins have about 20 seats and the journey takes only 2.5 minutes. From the mountain you have a quite good view, but could be better. The paths and the mountain station have certainly seen better times.

name: Gatlinburg Space Needle
description: The Gatlinburg Space Needle is an all steel observation tower served by two elevators with a capacity of 20 persons each. Ride our safe and comfortable glass elevators over 400’ to observation deck for 360° view of the Great Smoky Mountains and the resort city of Gatlinburg. The view is a panorama of beauty without equal year round. Enjoy Higher Learning, an educational experience from the Space Needle’s perspective, with free view finders!

name: Naminoue Beach
description: It is a man-made beach that spreads under the cliffs of Namikami no Miya. It is the only beach in Naha city, but the surrounding environment with a highway overhead and the city in the background may be unusual. I visited in mid-May, before the rainy season even in Okinawa, and several beachgoers visited.

name: Rio Grande Gorge Bridge
description: Great views of the gorge from the bridge and nice views of the bridge from the western parking area. Take care on the narrow pavements on the bridge.  Vendors in the parking area actually have some very nice and reasonably priced artwork. They are not at all pushy, so check them out. This is well worth a significant detour but is not really a destination in itself.

name: Quabbin Reservoir
description: So happy to have found this gem! Very uncrowded, tons of spots to picnic, nice walks, well-maintained, and absolutely free! My friend is immunocompromised, so we were trying to find a place to picnic and hang out where it was easy to not be near other folks, and this was perfect. You can park in one of the several lots or anywhere on the shoulder of the wide roads, and walk and picnic anywhere (definitely poison ivy in lots of places, so stay on paths and be alert!) Lovely views from the tower hill and other spots--stop by the visitors' center for a map or print the one on their website. No swimming or boating allowed in the crystal clear water, but hiking, biking, scootering, playing frisbee are all good, and the history is fascinating! (Nice displays in the visitors' center)

name: Walter White’s House
description: I was driving through Albuquerque and decided to stop by my old house lol J/K. As I was leaving the tour buss showed up, it was pretty cool to see all the fans.

name: Moyenne Island
description:
What a place for tortoise lovers! 
Literally a small island that takes 40 minutes to walk around with tortoises everywhere roaming free 
The red waking trial is quite up and down but worth it! 
 There’s a bar and toilets at start of island and you can also see a tortoise nursery with all the baby’s too

name: Ed Smith Stadium
description: Great stadium. We came to see the Pirates play the Orioles in spring training. Liked Ed Smith more than Lecom. We chose seats in left field. We lucked out that it was cloudy because I’m sure you’d bake out there in the sun. However it’s great seating because you have a chair (not normal stadium seating) and have quite a bit of room beside you as well as a lot in front/behind.Liked the concourses, plenty of dining options. We didn’t eat but the food looked/smelled good. Restrooms were clean even when leaving in the top of the 9th.Plenty of parking in the area. We parked diagonally across the street from home plate for $20. Easy in and out.

name: Bathtub Reef Beach
description: Parking is free, but limited.  For all practical purposes, arrived before 10:00AM on weekends and holidays. One can argue it is the “Best” beach in Martin County.  Ironically, the beach is not listed on Google Maps.It is known as “Bathtub” since a reef is close to shore forming shallow waters during low tide.  For small children, it is a fun playground.  You are asked not to go on the reef since it is fragile.Bathtub Reef Beach is easy to find. Turn south by the Marriott Resort on MacArthur Blvd. The distance is about 3 miles.  You will come across the House of Refuge, the oldest house in Martin County since 1876.  The beach is before you enter the Sailfish Point guard gate.  No problem if you miss the turn as there is a roundabout before the guard gate.Martin County spent millions of dollars to refurbish this beach destroyed by storms in 2024.  The gazebo that went out on the beach is now gone.  For the most part, the refurbishment is much welcomed.  There is a new bathroom at the southern end.  All they need to do now is to place a shower somewhere near the bathroom.The St. Lucie Inlet is but a tad more than a mile from Bathtub Beach heading south.  It makes for a pleasing walk or run.  Across the inlet is the St. Lucie Inlet Preserve State Park.Sailfish Point complex is unobtrusive to the beach area.  This area was known as “Seminole Shores.”  The original developer was James Rand who built a pier that lasted for many years, now gone.  The peninsula was mostly filed with Australian Pines, now homes and a golf course for Sailfish Point.In the 1970’s there was an unofficial nudist area down by the inlet.  There was even a movie in 1976 filmed along that beach called, “Empire of the Ants.” It was a low budget film.Just north of Bathtub Beach is a popular area where surfers like to catch waves caused by the reef below.On a rainy day going to the Elliot Museum and or House of Refuge is not a bad idea.If you found this review to be “helpful” in any way, please click the “thumbs-up” icon to let me know.

name: Barrio Getsemani
description: What a great neighborhood to spend some time wandering and exploring. There are lots of great restaurants! You could spend several hours here. Several vendors sell street food and artwork. If you get hot, stop at Belcanto restaurant for some affogato, beer and/or empanadas. It's a tiny space, but it's a nice stop for a bite and some jazz music. We visited Getsemani several times while in Cartagena.

name: Stonehenge Guided Tours
description: we were totally on the fence of whether we should spend part of our day going out there. We were not disappointed this ended up being a really great trip. The bus boards at 8:30.  it leaves at 8:30 sharp. I would get there a little bit earlier because we ended up leaving for people because they did not arrive on time.The drive out there is pretty easy, after a little nap you barely realize it and you are there.    I read some reviews at some people were feeling a little bit rushed. I did not feel that way. I felt two hours was more than enough time we used about an hour 40..    but we also went in December, which is considered the off-season and it was not very crowded at allYou arrive to the visitor station and they shuttle you directly to Stonehenge. I recommend that you do that first and then come back and do the visitor center.Download  the audio guide and it's very helpful if you have AirPods or something like that to listen.     We got home at 2 PM and the trip cost about $80.The biggest issue for us is where we going to take a train, Rent-A-Car, or do this tour and this was the way to go.

name: Osaka Free Walking Tour
description: Join the official Osaka Free Walking Tour! Explore Japan's foodie capital with us & find out why Osaka is called the “Kitchen of Japan”. You will learn about the unique Otaku culture and will travel back in time to the beginning of the 20th century visiting the old New World of Osaka.

name: Rhodes Town Tourist Train
description: The train has not been running all year, the waiter of the opposite cafe told me....I thought it was strange (like me) that you didn't notice this, the last review is from 5 years ago....

name: Smoky Mountains Jeep Tours
description: Experience the beauty of the Smoky Mountains on your family vacation. We provide you with the best views and some of the trails even include a short potion of off-road rugged terrain. Let us take you on a journey to experience the breathtaking views of Smoky Mountain National Park from your comfortable Jeep.

name: Nami Island
description: No matter the season, Nami Island is a beautiful destination to visit all year round. Known for appearing in many Korean dramas, the island has numerous lanes lined with pine trees, gingko trees, redwood giants and more. Take a scenic walk along the wooden riverside path and snap a photo with the Winter Sonata statue in Gongsaengwon Garden. You can get to the island via ferry or one of the longest ziplines in Korea. Alternatively, join a popular day trip from Seoul which includes Nami Island, Petite France and Garden of Morning Calm. Some tours include attractions like Mount Seorak or Gangchon Rail Bike as well.

name: Paris Charms & Secrets Tours
description: One of the best city tours we’ve taken.   The guide was fantastic, clearly a history buff.   Visited several off the beaten path locations.  Cannot recommend enough.

name: Portland Schooner Co.

name: Hon Ba Nature Reserve
description: Situated 56km SE of Nha Trang, this newly developed site includes a reconstruction of Dr Alexandre Yersin's outstation. The building contains items of original furniture transported from the Dr Yersin Museum in Nha Trang, and reproductions of several period photographs. Entrance fee to the historical site is 30,000 dong. On site parking is free.Also on site are: an open sided canteen, and five small chalets for rent at 500,000 dong per night per couple (100,000 dong per additional guest). Electricity is available, but as yet is inexplicably not connected. Hence (1) the canteen menu is limited to dried fish, dried squid and fresh chicken, killed just for you. Tea, coffee, soft drinks and non-refigerated beer are available without ice; (2) the chalets are unheated and without hot water; and (3) small kerosene hurrican lamps are used for lighting.To get here, go 17km from Nha Trang towards Saigon, turn right at Suoi Cat commune at a blue and white tourist sign "Ho Chua Nuoc Suoi Dau", after one km and turn left a market onto the Hon Ba road. Follow this road 38km to Hon Ba peak.A visit to this site would suit history buffs and those just wishing an escape from summer heat in Nha Trang. Good swimming holes are available in the stream at the bottom of the mountain, especially near the Foresty Inspection Station boom gate, 13km from the Suoi Cat turn off.

name: Ba Ho Waterfall
address: AddressNinh Ich, Ninh Hoa, Nha Trang 57000 Vietnam
description:
We met Mr Lam of Vietnam Motor Tours by chance on the street in Na Trang and went on a half day tour, the highlight of which without question was definitely the Ba Ho Waterfall.
Firstly, the additional 40,000 dong for return trip from facility reception to the falls by electric buggy was the best money I've ever spent, and I would have gladly paid multiple times that just for the trip back. Seriously, I can see no sense in taking on such an unnecessary arduous walk.
The falls are spectacular located within an equally spectacular forest setting with loads of clean facilities,  toilets, and childrens play areas.
The hike from the viewing bridge to the falls pulling yourself over rocks by using guide ropes is arduous, to say the least, but oh, so worth it. Most young and old will make it, but it is a little dicey here and there.
There are 3 ascending pools. However, on the day of our visit, only 2 were open due to a huge run of water following on from inclement weather. Something my sweat soaked overweight body was extremely grateful for at the time.
Even though we didn't get to swim, i would highly ighly recommend a visit to its value for time and money.
Mr Lam, our guide was fantastic

name: Cat Cat village
description:
This whole place is a massive Instagram trap of a location.
We went to cat cat village after a sapa trek just to wind down the day, and boy is it interesting. You start by going down a significant amount of stairs lined to brim with souvenir shops trying to sell you knick knacks. When you finally get to the main attraction you can see the whole place is gorgeous but just to the surface level where it consistently provides you with Instagram worthy photograph locations. Here you can show off your "traditional" Vietnamese outfits or just enjoy seeing the domestic tourists going through their own photo shoots. Every location is named in a very "on the nose" way such as "ancient hydroelectric plant (1918)", or "happy bridge", and "love waterfall" to name a few. There are live performances on the hour that you can sit across the river to watch while being distracted by the many photo ops going on simultaneously. Once you get past the main attraction you will see there are more "traditional style" buildings being made with stainless steel. After a small amount of stairs, you reach the end and find yourself either paying a small fee to be driven up a hill that is technically walkable, but looks very unpleasant to anyone with bad knees or recently trecked the mountainside. Once at the top you can then catch a cab back up the hill and back to your hotel or alternatively to a bar where you recount the bizarre theme park that you just visited. 
Would absolutely recommend anyone go to cat cat village just to experience the atmosphere it encourages.

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
Our family visit to Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa during the second week of June 2024 was an unforgettable experience. The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Thac Bac Waterfall (Silver Falls)
description:
Went to the waterfall today and as it had been raining it was very impressive!
Apparently it's the water source for Sapa, very clean water.
The stairs could be slippery so care was needed to ensure no slips.
The drive up was interesting seeing where the people grow the vegetables, very big area.
Worth having a look.

name: Ta Phin Village
description: Went to the village with a tour organised through the SaPa Tourist Information Centre, in SaPa. We were fortunate enough to have Ju as our tour guide. She took us around SaPa market first, at our request. It was great to understand more about the foods and items for sale.We then were driven to Ta Phin village, as it was a foggy day the surrounding views were limited. We walked through the village, and were accompanied by some very charming local women, selling wares. We stopped for one of their marvellous herbal baths, had a lovely lunch, and then walked up to the cave.The time spent with Ju was very special, to get a young village women’s perspective on different aspects of life gave us a richer experience and appreciation of Vietnam. Highly recommend a tour with these wonderful guides.

name: Glass Bridge
description: We absolutely loved our visit to Cau Kinh Rong May Sapa! As someone personally quite scared of heights, I was incredibly proud that I managed to conquer my fear while we were there. Standing high up, the wind blowing strongly against you definitely added to the thrill – honestly, for a moment, it felt like you could be blown right off the edge, which was both terrifying and exhilarating! (Hahaha). But even more powerful than the adrenaline rush, the thing we truly adored was the view. It was simply breathtaking, almost beyond description in that moment. The surrounding landscape, with the layers of mountains and perhaps clouds drifting by, looked exactly like a scene from a traditional Japanese painting – so serene and majestic. I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting on a clear, sunny day if possible; the visibility will allow you to appreciate the stunning panorama even more fully.

name: Terraced Rice Fields in Shin Chai Village
description: Sapa Landscapes is an international destination and the spirit is in between landscapes and local culture. The team is composed by youngsters of several families from the villages around. The difference is that it is possible for the visitors to communicate directly with the villagers, travel with ethnic people who will become local guides, because they are extremely knowledgeable about local cultures, history and the environment, learn English and French from tourists. However the spirit remains the same; we favorise the cultural exchanges by sharing all the natural moments of a day, meals, discovery activities, cooking, drinks, sometimes ceremonies, and even some everyday work like handcart. If there is a request, we can hire local artists for some simple representations, but most of the time, we interact with the local culture more than “watch it”.

The majority of the women still wear traditional colourful outfits and provide photographers with many opportunities for good shots. Although very busy there are far fewer foreign tourists than at the markets in Bac Ha and Sa Pa. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience

description: We went for a hike into the valley to visit local villages. The views were lovely and the villages were interesting but there isn’t much by way of cultural education or opportunities to learn about the local people so you just get to pass through and peek at their lives.

name: Sapa Trekking Mama Zuzu
description: Sapa Trekking is a family owned business that provides hikes through Sapa’s beautiful landscape. We are Black Hmong and grew up in the area. Our tours are led by one of the women in our family, who will share our culture as you trek through the hills and rice fields of Sapa. Tour are 5-6 hours and include lunch but can be customized to fit your needs. Call or WhatsApp +84 0388521891 OR message us on our Facebook page “Sapa Trekking Mama Zuzu” to schedule trek.

description: Very small lake in the centre of sapa. We really only visited to fill our time as sapa is such a small place. Nice enough to wander around but nothing special

name: Sapa Culture Museum
description: I lowered my expectations based on earlier reviews,  but felt it was an indoor activity worth seeing during down time (it's free). I was pleasantly surprised at the caliber of exhibits and design.The Sapa Museum is mainly in the top building where the tourism offices are located. The museum was clean and informative with explanations in Vietnamese,  French and English. It primarily explained the history of the area as a recreational respite for the French military and the 5 ethnic groups residing in the area. The floor below has a handicraft shop, but also an area where you can watch the workers in action. There is a garden too.In the lowest building is an interpretation center of the area's tourism. The French bombed their original town buildings in 1952 rather than have them taken by the NVA, and the area basically laid dormant until the 1990s. Gave me a better understanding of Sa Pa and how tourism operates.

description: We are proud to be the first point of contact for all tourists when they visit Sapa, offering them quality and comprehensive service from our professional staff and volunteers. Our facility in Sapa is conveniently located in the centre of Sapa, we have also ones near Lao Cai Station and in Bac Ha. Our friendly staff are able to assist with a wide range of tourist questions about Sapa - Lao Cai and the surrounding areas: Lai Chau, Dien Bien, Son La, Ha Giang, Cao Bang... As you step into Eden Central Massage & Spa, you are greeted by a tranquil atmosphere that instantly transports you away from the stresses of daily life. Park is home to Castaway Island water park, a full-hookup RV campground with Wi-Fi, 13 picnic shelters, an abundance of open picnic areas, and a large, open field suitable for a variety of family activities. Especially popular with our health-conscious patrons is the two-mile loop of paved pathways for walking, jogging, skating, and biking. Join our walking club and register your miles to earn incentives. NEW FITNESS ZONE! Located in downtown Calistoga, the 56-room hotel and spa was completely redesigned with a contemporary spa inspired look and feel. The eighteen month long renovation has touched all aspects of the property including a redesign of the guestrooms with spa-inspired bedding, honed Italian porcelain tile showers, kitchenettes with microwave ovens and modern conveniences such as full High Definition LED televisions. The focal points of the renovation are the four-geothermal heated mineral pools. name: Into The Wild Elephant Camp
description: Established in 2016, Into the Wild is an ethical elephant camp in the south of Chiang Mai. Our mission is to give our retired and rescued elephants a sustainable home that is safe and secure, yet they are able to roam freely and live as naturally as possible. Located in Chiang Mai’s Mae Wang District, our ethical and sustainable camp is surrounded by lush tropical jungle where our elephants can go foraging for food on their own and enjoy bathing in the river that flows through the camp. All elephants at our camp are those that have been with our family for generations. After years of supporting our ancestors in the logging and tourism industries, our elephants have become our family members and it is our responsibility to provide safe and ethical care for them.

name: Cat Cat village
description:
This whole place is a massive Instagram trap of a location.
We went to cat cat village after a sapa trek just to wind down the day, and boy is it interesting. You start by going down a significant amount of stairs lined to brim with souvenir shops trying to sell you knick knacks. When you finally get to the main attraction you can see the whole place is gorgeous but just to the surface level where it consistently provides you with Instagram worthy photograph locations. Here you can show off your "traditional" Vietnamese outfits or just enjoy seeing the domestic tourists going through their own photo shoots. Every location is named in a very "on the nose" way such as "ancient hydroelectric plant (1918)", or "happy bridge", and "love waterfall" to name a few. There are live performances on the hour that you can sit across the river to watch while being distracted by the many photo ops going on simultaneously. Once you get past the main attraction you will see there are more "traditional style" buildings being made with stainless steel. After a small amount of stairs, you reach the end and find yourself either paying a small fee to be driven up a hill that is technically walkable, but looks very unpleasant to anyone with bad knees or recently trecked the mountainside. Once at the top you can then catch a cab back up the hill and back to your hotel or alternatively to a bar where you recount the bizarre theme park that you just visited. 
Would absolutely recommend anyone go to cat cat village just to experience the atmosphere it encourages.

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
Our family visit to Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa during the second week of June 2024 was an unforgettable experience. The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Thac Bac Waterfall (Silver Falls)
description:
Went to the waterfall today and as it had been raining it was very impressive!
Apparently it's the water source for Sapa, very clean water.
The stairs could be slippery so care was needed to ensure no slips.
The drive up was interesting seeing where the people grow the vegetables, very big area.
Worth having a look.

name: Ta Phin Village
description: Went to the village with a tour organised through the SaPa Tourist Information Centre, in SaPa. We were fortunate enough to have Ju as our tour guide. She took us around SaPa market first, at our request. It was great to understand more about the foods and items for sale.We then were driven to Ta Phin village, as it was a foggy day the surrounding views were limited. We walked through the village, and were accompanied by some very charming local women, selling wares. We stopped for one of their marvellous herbal baths, had a lovely lunch, and then walked up to the cave.The time spent with Ju was very special, to get a young village women’s perspective on different aspects of life gave us a richer experience and appreciation of Vietnam. Highly recommend a tour with these wonderful guides.

name: Glass Bridge
description: We absolutely loved our visit to Cau Kinh Rong May Sapa! As someone personally quite scared of heights, I was incredibly proud that I managed to conquer my fear while we were there. Standing high up, the wind blowing strongly against you definitely added to the thrill – honestly, for a moment, it felt like you could be blown right off the edge, which was both terrifying and exhilarating! (Hahaha). But even more powerful than the adrenaline rush, the thing we truly adored was the view. It was simply breathtaking, almost beyond description in that moment. The surrounding landscape, with the layers of mountains and perhaps clouds drifting by, looked exactly like a scene from a traditional Japanese painting – so serene and majestic. I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting on a clear, sunny day if possible; the visibility will allow you to appreciate the stunning panorama even more fully.

name: Terraced Rice Fields in Shin Chai Village
description: Sapa Landscapes is an international destination and the spirit is in between landscapes and local culture. The team is composed by youngsters of several families from the villages around. The difference is that it is possible for the visitors to communicate directly with the villagers, travel with ethnic people who will become local guides, because they are extremely knowledgeable about local cultures, history and the environment, learn English and French from tourists. However the spirit remains the same; we favorise the cultural exchanges by sharing all the natural moments of a day, meals, discovery activities, cooking, drinks, sometimes ceremonies, and even some everyday work like handcart. If there is a request, we can hire local artists for some simple representations, but most of the time, we interact with the local culture more than “watch it”.

name: Sapa Culture Museum
description: I lowered my expectations based on earlier reviews,  but felt it was an indoor activity worth seeing during down time (it's free). I was pleasantly surprised at the caliber of exhibits and design.The Sapa Museum is mainly in the top building where the tourism offices are located. The museum was clean and informative with explanations in Vietnamese,  French and English. It primarily explained the history of the area as a recreational respite for the French military and the 5 ethnic groups residing in the area. The floor below has a handicraft shop, but also an area where you can watch the workers in action. There is a garden too.In the lowest building is an interpretation center of the area's tourism. The French bombed their original town buildings in 1952 rather than have them taken by the NVA, and the area basically laid dormant until the 1990s. Gave me a better understanding of Sa Pa and how tourism operates.

With FREE Parking, FREE Inner Tubes and FREE Sunscreen you'll get more smiles per gallon with every visit!

name: Topeekeegee Yugnee Park
description: The Seminole Indian name of this 138.6-acre urban park, Topeekeegee Yugnee, means "meeting or gathering place," appropriate for a park known for its shady picnic areas, many shelters, and a gazebo that is often booked for small weddings and receptions.T.Y. Park is home to Castaway Island water park, a full-hookup RV campground with Wi-Fi, 13 picnic shelters, an abundance of open picnic areas, and a large, open field suitable for a variety of family activities. Especially popular with our health-conscious patrons is the two-mile loop of paved pathways for walking, jogging, skating, and biking. Join our walking club and register your miles to earn incentives. NEW FITNESS ZONE! In December 2013, Broward County Parks and Memorial Healthcare System teamed up to provide The "Memorial Fitness Zone" which consists of 11 outdoor fitness equipment pieces. The equipment is free to use by anyone ages 14 and up. Weekend and holiday park entrance fees apply. Other popular areas within the park are the large shaded playground, basketball and tennis courts, the fishing pier, and the scenic lake water fountain.

name: Downtown Williams Historic Walk
description: Cool little town with lots of Route 66 memorabilia-make sure to stop by the brewery in town for some fabulous cocktails-very easy drive to the Grand Canyon from there…

name: Calistoga Spa Hot Springs
description: The Calistoga Spa Hot Springs, a geothermal hot springs resort, recently completed an extensive renovation project that has dramatically transformed a property that has been attracting repeat guests for generations. Our stay in Mykonos was short enough that we didn't get a chance to compare it to other beaches.  But we were happy enough with the beach that we went every day we were there.  The water is crystal clear and mostly serene unless a ship has just come in.  That said, we enjoyed watching the ships come in; the lifeguard gives you a warning about it, but you can still stay in the water.

It's easy to get to if you have a car or if you take a bus from the Old port.  The bus ride takes about 5 minutes and costs 2 Euro.  

The beach is definitely on the quieter, more family-friendly side if that's your thing.  There's not a lot of water sports or activities, so if you just want a chill day at the beach, this is the spot for you.  There are two restaurants with very reasonably-priced beach chairs nearby.  We often purchased lunch from a small local grocery store nearby, which was very budget-friendly.

name: Kamala Beach
description:
The beach is very beautiful, the sand looks like talcum powder, the sea fantastic. They made me smile negative reviews because of the rough sea: it was the low season, maybe it would have been better to inquire before leaving. The disadvantage of going to Phuket off-season is just what you can't enjoy the sea, which doesn't mean you have to rate Sea and Beach negatively. I read reviews from years ago that talk about a foul-smelling discharge that is pouring into the sea, and I regret to note that the situation has not changed at all, indeed, I imagine it has only worsened, it is basically an open sewer that is pouring into the sea.  I wonder how it is that after all these years the Kamala authorities have done nothing to sanitize that rotten and fetid swamp. We were towards the end of the beach, not far from the Novotel which is mentioned here in other reviews and I confirm to be at the end, nice, also because there is less passage in front. Next to our five-star hotel there was an outdoor daytime disco bar called Café del Mar. So unless you like to listen to Rave party music at full volume, from lunchtime until night, stay away from that bar, the music is deafening, the percussion is in your head while you try to relax on the beach and hear the sound of the sea. In addition to that there are jet skis,
To be clear, almost in front of this coffee shop in the Sea, they go back and forth all day and they certainly do not wait to be out to sea to make the full power of the engine felt. So you have, in stereo, on one side house music, on the other the resounding noise of jet skis, and you have traveled 9000 km from Italy to look for some relaxation. The beach is still very beautiful, the important thing, if you are looking for tranquility is to stay away from that Bar .. I also confirm the presence of many modest but excellent restaurants on the beach, where you eat great food, spending a third of what you would spend at the hotel. And they're all very nice. These small restaurants are also open in the evenings , look for the paved inner path, Matteo died if you don't want to walk all the way on the sand.
I don’t know if the situation has changed compared to years ago, I was there this year for the first time, the beach is not dirty, even if it was, the fault is those who throw the stuff into the sea that then invariably spills onto land. Of course it happens to find plastic, if we all made a little effort to collect what comes before our eyes, we would do a great favor to this wonderful because the beach and the sea belong to everyone. I’ve seen much dirtier beaches, even on islands in Malaysia, the Maldives, or Diani Beach. In Kamala Beach there is also a person who in the morning, with his cart, comes to clean. Another thing I appreciated is that there are very few street vendors, you don’t even notice their presence because they are very discreet, they don’t scream and they are not pushy. 
Then there are the people who give massages, even on the feet at prices I dare say derisory.

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
Our family visit to Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa during the second week of June 2024 was an unforgettable experience. The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Cat Cat village
description:
This whole place is a massive Instagram trap of a location.
We went to cat cat village after a sapa trek just to wind down the day, and boy is it interesting. You start by going down a significant amount of stairs lined to brim with souvenir shops trying to sell you knick knacks. When you finally get to the main attraction you can see the whole place is gorgeous but just to the surface level where it consistently provides you with Instagram worthy photograph locations. Here you can show off your "traditional" Vietnamese outfits or just enjoy seeing the domestic tourists going through their own photo shoots. Every location is named in a very "on the nose" way such as "ancient hydroelectric plant (1918)", or "happy bridge", and "love waterfall" to name a few. There are live performances on the hour that you can sit across the river to watch while being distracted by the many photo ops going on simultaneously. Once you get past the main attraction you will see there are more "traditional style" buildings being made with stainless steel. After a small amount of stairs, you reach the end and find yourself either paying a small fee to be driven up a hill that is technically walkable, but looks very unpleasant to anyone with bad knees or recently trecked the mountainside. Once at the top you can then catch a cab back up the hill and back to your hotel or alternatively to a bar where you recount the bizarre theme park that you just visited. 
Would absolutely recommend anyone go to cat cat village just to experience the atmosphere it encourages.

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
Our family visit to Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa during the second week of June 2024 was an unforgettable experience. The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Cat Cat village
description:
This whole place is a massive Instagram trap of a location.
We went to cat cat village after a sapa trek just to wind down the day, and boy is it interesting. You start by going down a significant amount of stairs lined to brim with souvenir shops trying to sell you knick knacks. When you finally get to the main attraction you can see the whole place is gorgeous but just to the surface level where it consistently provides you with Instagram worthy photograph locations. Here you can show off your "traditional" Vietnamese outfits or just enjoy seeing the domestic tourists going through their own photo shoots. Every location is named in a very "on the nose" way such as "ancient hydroelectric plant (1918)", or "happy bridge", and "love waterfall" to name a few. There are live performances on the hour that you can sit across the river to watch while being distracted by the many photo ops going on simultaneously. Once you get past the main attraction you will see there are more "traditional style" buildings being made with stainless steel. After a small amount of stairs, you reach the end and find yourself either paying a small fee to be driven up a hill that is technically walkable, but looks very unpleasant to anyone with bad knees or recently trecked the mountainside. Once at the top you can then catch a cab back up the hill and back to your hotel or alternatively to a bar where you recount the bizarre theme park that you just visited. 
Would absolutely recommend anyone go to cat cat village just to experience the atmosphere it encourages.

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
Our family visit to Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa during the second week of June 2024 was an unforgettable experience. The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Cat Cat village
description:
This whole place is a massive Instagram trap of a location.
We went to cat cat village after a sapa trek just to wind down the day, and boy is it interesting. You start by going down a significant amount of stairs lined to brim with souvenir shops trying to sell you knick knacks. When you finally get to the main attraction you can see the whole place is gorgeous but just to the surface level where it consistently provides you with Instagram worthy photograph locations. Here you can show off your "traditional" Vietnamese outfits or just enjoy seeing the domestic tourists going through their own photo shoots. Every location is named in a very "on the nose" way such as "ancient hydroelectric plant (1918)", or "happy bridge", and "love waterfall" to name a few. There are live performances on the hour that you can sit across the river to watch while being distracted by the many photo ops going on simultaneously. Once you get past the main attraction you will see there are more "traditional style" buildings being made with stainless steel. After a small amount of stairs, you reach the end and find yourself either paying a small fee to be driven up a hill that is technically walkable, but looks very unpleasant to anyone with bad knees or recently trecked the mountainside. Once at the top you can then catch a cab back up the hill and back to your hotel or alternatively to a bar where you recount the bizarre theme park that you just visited. 
Would absolutely recommend anyone go to cat cat village just to experience the atmosphere it encourages.

description:
Went to the waterfall today and as it had been raining it was very impressive!
Apparently it's the water source for Sapa, very clean water.
The stairs could be slippery so care was needed to ensure no slips.
The drive up was interesting seeing where the people grow the vegetables, very big area.
Worth having a look.

name: Ta Phin Village
description: Went to the village with a tour organised through the SaPa Tourist Information Centre, in SaPa. We were fortunate enough to have Ju as our tour guide. She took us around SaPa market first, at our request. It was great to understand more about the foods and items for sale.We then were driven to Ta Phin village, as it was a foggy day the surrounding views were limited. We walked through the village, and were accompanied by some very charming local women, selling wares. We stopped for one of their marvellous herbal baths, had a lovely lunch, and then walked up to the cave.The time spent with Ju was very special, to get a young village women’s perspective on different aspects of life gave us a richer experience and appreciation of Vietnam. Highly recommend a tour with these wonderful guides.

name: Glass Bridge
description: We absolutely loved our visit to Cau Kinh Rong May Sapa! As someone personally quite scared of heights, I was incredibly proud that I managed to conquer my fear while we were there. Standing high up, the wind blowing strongly against you definitely added to the thrill – honestly, for a moment, it felt like you could be blown right off the edge, which was both terrifying and exhilarating! (Hahaha). But even more powerful than the adrenaline rush, the thing we truly adored was the view. It was simply breathtaking, almost beyond description in that moment. The surrounding landscape, with the layers of mountains and perhaps clouds drifting by, looked exactly like a scene from a traditional Japanese painting – so serene and majestic. I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting on a clear, sunny day if possible; the visibility will allow you to appreciate the stunning panorama even more fully.

name: Sapa Culture Museum
description: I lowered my expectations based on earlier reviews,  but felt it was an indoor activity worth seeing during down time (it's free). I was pleasantly surprised at the caliber of exhibits and design.The Sapa Museum is mainly in the top building where the tourism offices are located. The museum was clean and informative with explanations in Vietnamese,  French and English. It primarily explained the history of the area as a recreational respite for the French military and the 5 ethnic groups residing in the area. The floor below has a handicraft shop, but also an area where you can watch the workers in action. There is a garden too.In the lowest building is an interpretation center of the area's tourism. The French bombed their original town buildings in 1952 rather than have them taken by the NVA, and the area basically laid dormant until the 1990s. Gave me a better understanding of Sa Pa and how tourism operates.

description:

The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

Highly recommend a tour with these wonderful guides.

name: Glass Bridge
description: We absolutely loved our visit to Cau Kinh Rong May Sapa! As someone personally quite scared of heights, I was incredibly proud that I managed to conquer my fear while we were there. The surrounding landscape, with the layers of mountains and perhaps clouds drifting by, looked exactly like a scene from a traditional Japanese painting – so serene and majestic. I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting on a clear, sunny day if possible; the visibility will allow you to appreciate the stunning panorama even more fully.

name: Terraced Rice Fields in Shin Chai Village

However the spirit remains the same; we favorise the cultural exchanges by sharing all the natural moments of a day, meals, discovery activities, cooking, drinks, sometimes ceremonies, and even some everyday work like handcart. If there is a request, we can hire local artists for some simple representations, but most of the time, we interact with the local culture more than “watch it”.

description: Very small lake in the centre of sapa. We really only visited to fill our time as sapa is such a small place. Nice enough to wander around but nothing special

name: Sapa Culture Museum
description: I lowered my expectations based on earlier reviews,  but felt it was an indoor activity worth seeing during down time (it's free). I was pleasantly surprised at the caliber of exhibits and design.The Sapa Museum is mainly in the top building where the tourism offices are located. The museum was clean and informative with explanations in Vietnamese,  French and English. It primarily explained the history of the area as a recreational respite for the French military and the 5 ethnic groups residing in the area. The floor below has a handicraft shop, but also an area where you can watch the workers in action. There is a garden too.In the lowest building is an interpretation center of the area's tourism. The French bombed their original town buildings in 1952 rather than have them taken by the NVA, and the area basically laid dormant until the 1990s. Gave me a better understanding of Sa Pa and how tourism operates.

name: Amazing Swimming Pool

name: Sun Plaza

description: I spend a lot of time bird watching in the area and constantly see people logging, trapping birds, and hunting. This often just a few hundred meters from the ranger station. What I have never seen is the rangers actually out on patrol. Like in many so-called protected areas in Vietnam, the flora and fauna is pretty much doomed.

The eighteen month long renovation has touched all aspects of the property including a redesign of the guestrooms with spa-inspired bedding, honed Italian porcelain tile showers, kitchenettes with microwave ovens and modern conveniences such as full High Definition LED televisions. The focal points of the renovation are the four-geothermal heated mineral pools. The pool deck was fitted with travertine tiles, new designer-inspired pool furniture and the inclusion of grape covered arbors.

name: Into The Wild Elephant Camp
description: Established in 2016, Into the Wild is an ethical elephant camp in the south of Chiang Mai. Our mission is to give our retired and rescued elephants a sustainable home that is safe and secure, yet they are able to roam freely and live as naturally as possible. Located in Chiang Mai’s Mae Wang District, our ethical and sustainable camp is surrounded by lush tropical jungle where our elephants can go foraging for food on their own and enjoy bathing in the river that flows through the camp. All elephants at our camp are those that have been with our family for generations. After years of supporting our ancestors in the logging and tourism industries, our elephants have become our family members and it is our responsibility to provide safe and ethical care for them.

name: Cat Cat village
description:

name: Sun World Fansipan Legend
description:
