The cable car ride offered breathtaking panoramic views of the lush green mountains and terraced rice fields, making it perfect for capturing stunning photos. The cabins were clean, spacious, and well-maintained, ensuring a comfortable ride for everyone, including children and elderly family members.
Reaching the summit of Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina at 3,143 meters, was a thrilling achievement for our family. The weather was slightly chilly and foggy, creating a refreshing atmosphere, with the wind speed being quite intense at times. Dressing in layers is advisable. The sense of accomplishment was palpable as we stood next to the iconic monument.
The cultural performances at the base station were a delightful addition to our visit. The traditional music and dance showcased the rich heritage of the local ethnic groups, adding a unique cultural dimension to our trip. Additionally, the botanical garden near the summit featured a variety of native plants and flowers, making it a great spot for nature enthusiasts and photographers.
Overall, Sun World Fansipan Legend is a family-friendly destination with activities and attractions suitable for all ages. The staff were courteous and helpful, enhancing our overall experience. We highly recommend visiting early in the day to avoid crowds and to make the most of the clear weather. Don’t forget to bring a camera to capture the stunning vistas. Our visit was a memorable adventure filled with natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of achievement, making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sa Pa.

name: Ta Phin Village

Highly recommend a tour with these wonderful guides.

name: Glass Bridge
description: We absolutely loved our visit to Cau Kinh Rong May Sapa! As someone personally quite scared of heights, I was incredibly proud that I managed to conquer my fear while we were there. Standing high up, the wind blowing strongly against you definitely added to the thrill – honestly, for a moment, it felt like you could be blown right off the edge, which was both terrifying and exhilarating! (Hahaha). But even more powerful than the adrenaline rush, the thing we truly adored was the view. It was simply breathtaking, almost beyond description in that moment. The surrounding landscape, with the layers of mountains and perhaps clouds drifting by, looked exactly like a scene from a traditional Japanese painting – so serene and majestic. I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting on a clear, sunny day if possible; the visibility will allow you to appreciate the stunning panorama even more fully.

The difference is that it is possible for the visitors to communicate directly with the villagers, travel with ethnic people who will become local guides, because they are extremely knowledgeable about local cultures, history and the environment, learn English and French from tourists. However the spirit remains the same; we favorise the cultural exchanges by sharing all the natural moments of a day, meals, discovery activities, cooking, drinks, sometimes ceremonies, and even some everyday work like handcart. If there is a request, we can hire local artists for some simple representations, but most of the time, we interact with the local culture more than “watch it”.

name: Ta Van Village
description: Not thing so special. Too much local lady trying to sell things.Better visit and see the view during summer time.It is tourist place and not worth of the value.Not really high recommend

name: Chợ Cán Cấu
description: We had read about this traditional market which takes place in Can Cau every Saturday and made sure that we arrived early to be able to see the various ethnic tribes people arriving from the outlying area to attend. The majority of the women still wear traditional colourful outfits and provide photographers with many opportunities for good shots. Although very busy there are far fewer foreign tourists than at the markets in Bac Ha and Sa Pa. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience

name: The Stone Church
description: Suggestive and very attended the evening service, the boys sing very well. The church itself is very simple but made alive by the participation of the faithful, all very young.

name: O Quy Ho Mountain Pass
description: Set way up in the hills, it's often fog bound. If so, there's noting to see -- literally. On a clear day, it's wonderful. There is a small Buddhist temple, gardens, statues and more.  It's really nicely done. Just reserve it for a clear, sunny day.

name: Tram Ton Pass
description: We visited Tram Ton Pass but unfortunately the weather didn’t  permit us to have any views. It was drizzling and the clouds and the mist obscured any view. But what ever we could see in the mist showed they had done some good landscaping and horticulture.

name: Sapa Square
description: Amazing love marketSapa love market is open on every saturday ... It's great to see Hmong young people dance with umbrella ..this is a unique and vibrant event

name: Giang Ta Chai Village
description: We went for a hike into the valley to visit local villages. The views were lovely and the villages were interesting but there isn’t much by way of cultural education or opportunities to learn about the local people so you just get to pass through and peek at their lives.

name: Sapa Culture Museum
description: I lowered my expectations based on earlier reviews,  but felt it was an indoor activity worth seeing during down time (it's free). I was pleasantly surprised at the caliber of exhibits and design.The Sapa Museum is mainly in the top building where the tourism offices are located. The museum was clean and informative with explanations in Vietnamese,  French and English. It primarily explained the history of the area as a recreational respite for the French military and the 5 ethnic groups residing in the area. The floor below has a handicraft shop, but also an area where you can watch the workers in action. There is a garden too.In the lowest building is an interpretation center of the area's tourism. The French bombed their original town buildings in 1952 rather than have them taken by the NVA, and the area basically laid dormant until the 1990s. Gave me a better understanding of Sa Pa and how tourism operates.

description: Sapa Trekking is a family owned business that provides hikes through Sapa’s beautiful landscape. We are Black Hmong and grew up in the area. Our tours are led by one of the women in our family, who will share our culture as you trek through the hills and rice fields of Sapa. name: Sapa Lake

description: The Seminole Indian name of this 138.6-acre urban park, Topeekeegee Yugnee, means "meeting or gathering place," appropriate for a park known for its shady picnic areas, many shelters, and a gazebo that is often booked for small weddings and receptions.T.Y. description: The Calistoga Spa Hot Springs, a geothermal hot springs resort, recently completed an extensive renovation project that has dramatically transformed a property that has been attracting repeat guests for generations. Located in downtown Calistoga, the 56-room hotel and spa was completely redesigned with a contemporary spa inspired look and feel. The eighteen month long renovation has touched all aspects of the property including a redesign of the guestrooms with spa-inspired bedding, honed Italian porcelain tile showers, kitchenettes with microwave ovens and modern conveniences such as full High Definition LED televisions. The focal points of the renovation are the four-geothermal heated mineral pools. The pool deck was fitted with travertine tiles, new designer-inspired pool furniture and the inclusion of grape covered arbors.

name: Into The Wild Elephant Camp
description: Established in 2016, Into the Wild is an ethical elephant camp in the south of Chiang Mai. Our mission is to give our retired and rescued elephants a sustainable home that is safe and secure, yet they are able to roam freely and live as naturally as possible. Located in Chiang Mai’s Mae Wang District, our ethical and sustainable camp is surrounded by lush tropical jungle where our elephants can go foraging for food on their own and enjoy bathing in the river that flows through the camp. All elephants at our camp are those that have been with our family for generations. After years of supporting our ancestors in the logging and tourism industries, our elephants have become our family members and it is our responsibility to provide safe and ethical care for them.
